name: PEEL — the QR X-ray
one_liner: Point your phone at any shop's UPI QR sticker and it tells you in under a second whose bank account it actually pays — and lights up the exact squares of the code that were tampered with.
the_gif: Full-bleed phone camera, one continuous handheld take, no UI chrome. A hand pans along a grubby kirana counter with four paper UPI QR stickers taped to it. As each sticker enters frame a four-cornered bracket SNAPS onto it in correct perspective and stays welded to the paper while the phone keeps moving, with the decoded payee name in big white type floating just above the sticker: SHARMA GENERAL STORE (green) — SHARMA GENERAL STORE (green) — SHARMA GENERAL STORE (green) — then the fourth bracket slams RED, the floating name reads 'chhotu.tiwari@ybl', and inside the QR itself roughly forty individual black modules ignite red one after another in a constellation, showing precisely which squares of the code are the lie. A thumb and forefinger enter frame, PEEL the fake sticker off the counter, and the genuine QR underneath snaps green. Five seconds, zero words, zero audio needed.
why_it_looks_impossible: A tampered QR is, by construction, visually identical — the Delhi Police case (arrest 22 Dec 2025) says the accused 'kept the QR code's appearance unchanged to fool customers.' The viewer knows from their own life that a QR is an unreadable black-and-white mess. So watching the camera render the difference between the real code and the forgery as a glowing constellation of individual modules, in perspective, on a moving piece of paper, contradicts the viewer's direct experience. Nobody has ever seen WHICH PIXELS OF A QR CODE ARE THE LIE. And the peel at the end proves it wasn't staged — the truth was physically underneath the whole time.
problem: QR sticker swap is a real, dated, prosecuted Indian crime and the merchant's only current detection mechanism is silence. Delhi, Dec 2025: a 19-year-old diverted Rs 1.40 lakh (Rs 90,000 + Rs 50,000) from a Chandni Chowk boutique using AI-edited QR stickers; police seized 100+ edited and original codes off his phone. Khajuraho, Jan 2025: fraudsters pasted their own stickers over genuine ones overnight at ~6 establishments including petrol pumps — caught only because one customer read the payee name 'Chhotu Tiwari' on his own app. The surface is 56.86 crore QR codes across ~6.5 crore merchants. A July 2026 field study of 102 Srinagar merchants found 57.8% had already lost money to fraudulent digital transactions, 60.8% display QRs as LOOSE PAPER stickers, 41.2% display them outside the counter in blind spots, and 90.2% did not know the 1930 helpline. Soundbox — the incumbent answer — covers roughly 10-14% of merchants, costs Rs 100-150/month plus hardware, and catches a swapped QR only by silence, which a busy counter does not notice.
how_it_works: FAST LOOP, 30-60 fps, in a browser tab, fully on-device. getUserMedia -> canvas -> Sec-ant/zxing-wasm (reader-only ~1.04 MiB, MIT) or nimiq/qr-scanner (worker-based, 25 scans/sec default) decodes and returns cornerPoints — four real corners, which is exactly the pothole-detector primitive. Feature-detect native BarcodeDetector (Chrome Android 83+) and fall back to the ponyfill, because Safari hides it behind a Shape Detection preference flag. The upi://pay?pa=...&pn=... payload is parsed with plain string code — no model. Four corners plus the three finder patterns go into cv.findHomography (whitelisted in opencv_js.config.py alongside solvePnP, warpPerspective and aruco_ArucoDetector) to rectify the photographed sticker to a canonical square, then sample the module grid at the code's version pitch. THE X-RAY: regenerate the merchant's REGISTERED payload as a QR bitmap locally at the same version/ECC/mask, XOR the two module matrices, and ignite the differing modules. That is exact arithmetic, not inference. VERDICT is three deterministic tiers: decoded VPA == registered VPA (GREEN); valid UPI handle not in the merchant's registry (RED); undecodable or partial (AMBER HOLD, authorises nothing). SLOW LOOP, 2-4 Hz: PP-OCRv5 mobile det (4.7 MB, 28-58 ms CPU) + rec (16 MB, 5-21 ms CPU) reads the printed shop name on the standee for a soft cross-check, and a small self-trained ONNX classifier looks for the physical sticker-over-sticker cue (double border, laminate seam, hairline shadow) as a suspicion-only signal. AUTO-RESPONDER: on a confirmed mismatch on a code the merchant owns, offer one bounded action — POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close on the compromised code, then POST /v1/payments/qr_codes to mint a replacement — behind a two-step confirm plus a reason code, with every step appended to a hash-chained local log and reconciled against qr_code.created / credited / closed webhooks.
features: Perspective-locked bracket on every QR in frame, driven by cornerPoints, holding steady while the phone moves
Decoded payee name and VPA rendered in large type floating above the physical sticker — automating the single signal that has ever actually caught this fraud
MODULE X-RAY: homography-rectified module grid XOR'd against the locally regenerated registered code, differing modules ignited as a red constellation inside the QR
Three-tier deterministic verdict (registered / valid-but-unregistered / undecodable) with an AMBER HOLD state that authorises nothing

Multi-QR census: box and label every code on one counter simultaneously with a 'this counter pays into 3 different accounts' banner — the Hoskote biryani outlet had 30 QR codes and Rs 1.47 crore of transactions
Overnight diff: a one-tap morning shutter-up check comparing today's rectified module matrix to last night's stored one, turning the Khajuraho CCTV story into a daily 4-second habit
Suspicion-only physical-overlay classifier (double border / laminate seam / shadow) that can only ADD suspicion, never clear a code, with its own separately published false-positive rate
Torch-assisted decode for glare-heavy laminated stickers via applyConstraints({torch:true}), using a flash/no-flash differential frame
Bounded auto-response: close the compromised QR and mint a replacement, two-step gated, with a hard code-level rule that a replacement can only ever point at a VPA already in the merchant's registry
Hash-chained on-device audit log plus Razorpay webhook trail, exportable as a one-tap evidence pack for a 1930 cybercrime complaint
Offline-first: registry snapshot cached, decode and XOR run with zero network, so it works in a basement shop with no signal; network is needed only to refresh the registry and to close a code
Graceful degradation UI: dashed amber bracket, a closing confidence ring, and 'HOLDING LAST GOOD POSE' when the code is occluded or blurred, re-locking with a snap
Enforced defense-only guardrails: the app cannot render, export, or generate a QR payload for any VPA outside the merchant's registry, and cannot produce a clean forged sticker image
One-command evaluation harness that regenerates the report card (precision, recall, decode-rate vs angle and lux, time-to-verdict) against the held-out photo set
ai_judgment: The verdict is never a model's opinion. Decode, registry lookup and module XOR are deterministic, exact and explainable in one sentence each. The loudest deliberate NO: we benchmarked and then DELETED the pixel-forensics tamper detector. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026, 4,061 AI-forged receipts) measured TruFor collapsing from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 in-distribution to 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge at 0.509 — literally chance. Shipping that would have been AI theatre. Second deliberate NO: monocular depth to detect the 0.1-0.3 mm step of a sticker pasted over a sticker. Depth-Anything-V2-Small measures 323.6 ms at 518x518 on this M3 Pro (3.1 fps) and returns relative, scale-free depth — it has nothing like sub-millimetre resolution at arm's length, so this was tested-and-rejected rather than shipped. Third deliberate NO: no LLM anywhere in the money path; an LLM cannot be allowed to decide whose bank account gets paid. AI appears in exactly two subordinate roles — the overlay-suspicion classifier and shop-name OCR — and neither can turn RED into GREEN.
razorpay_fit: The Razorpay QR Codes API is simultaneously the REGISTRY and the TRUTH FEED, which is why every camera verdict is backed by a citable fact rather than a vibe. GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id gives the canonical registered payload to diff against; GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/payments gives money actually received; POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close is the bounded kill action; qr_code.created / qr_code.credited / qr_code.closed webhooks are the audit trail. Runs entirely on test API keys from the dashboard, and razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (official, 230 stars) already exposes QR create/fetch/close/retrieve-payments as agent tools. We also handle the documented edge case that qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry, only on manual close — a real stopping-rule detail judges will recognise.
measurable: A held-out set of 240 photographs the tuning pass never saw: 60 genuine Razorpay test-mode QR standees and 60 tampered ones (payload-swapped reprints plus physically pasted overlays), each shot at two angles under two lighting conditions, on a different phone. Reported: precision and recall of the RED verdict, decode rate as a function of angle (0-60 degrees) and illuminance, median time-to-verdict in ms, and — reported SEPARATELY so it is unmistakable that it never gates the decision — the precision/recall and FPR of the suspicion-only overlay classifier. Expected honest shape: near-perfect precision on payload mismatch, because that is a decode and not a guess, and materially lower, openly published recall on physical sticker-over-sticker detection.
feasibility: Solid ground: decode + cornerPoints + homography + module XOR is deterministic; I can say exactly why it works and exactly when it does not. Real risks on camera: (1) glare on a laminated sticker under a fluorescent tube kills the decode — mitigated with torch toggle and an on-screen tilt coach, but a bad shop light can still beat it; (2) the module XOR is only defined if the photographed code has the same version/ECC/mask as the registered one — if the fraudster's code is a different version the XOR is meaningless, so the system falls back to a 'WHOLE CODE REPLACED' verdict, which is a stronger red, and I will say this on camera rather than hide it; (3) native BarcodeDetector is Chrome-Android-only, so the zxing-wasm ponyfill (~1.04 MiB) ships as the default path; (4) cold load matters on Indian 4G — opencv.js is 3.33 MB over the wire, so it lazy-loads AFTER the first decode, meaning the bracket appears immediately and the X-ray arrives a beat later. Deliberate on-camera failure beat: a thumb covers half the sticker, the bracket goes dashed amber, a confidence ring closes down, no money action is offered, and it re-locks with a snap when uncovered.

name: SETTLE — the desk that reconciles itself
one_liner: Spread a month of paper invoices under a webcam and every sheet lights up green, amber or red — matched, duplicate, or won't reconcile — with the light staying glued to the paper as you shove it around the desk.
the_gif: Locked-off overhead shot. A plain wooden desk, an ordinary laptop propped so its webcam looks straight down. A hand deals printed GST invoices onto the desk like playing cards — eight of them, fast. In the same frame each sheet lands, a coloured halo snaps around it IN PERSPECTIVE and stays welded to it: green, green, green, amber, green. The hand then shoves the sheets around and spins two of them ninety degrees — every halo slides and rotates with its paper, perfectly stuck. The hand drags one RED sheet forward into close-up, and a red strike is drawn along one single line ON the paper with 'Rs 4,120' floating a few millimetres above it. The hand keeps dealing and the desk fills with light. No screen visible, no cursor, no words, one unbroken take.
why_it_looks_impossible: Light that is stuck to a moving piece of paper. The overlay is not next to the document in a panel — it is ON the document, in correct perspective, surviving being shoved, rotated and half-covered by a hand. That is the exact thing amateur AR demos get wrong (they jitter and jump), so a viewer who has seen those instantly registers that this one is different. The second impossibility is semantic rather than visual: the colours mean something that takes a human two to four minutes per sheet to determine, and they appear in the frame the paper lands.
problem: Indian finance ops still runs on paper — GST invoices, delivery challans, printed receipts, cheque leaves. The headline rupee number is enormous: central tax authorities detected Rs 74,782 crore of fake input tax credit across 30,162 cases in FY26 (Finance Ministry written reply to Parliament, 28 Jul 2026), up from Rs 58,772.51 crore across 15,283 cases in FY25 and Rs 36,373.36 crore across 9,190 cases in FY24 — more than doubling in two years. And the shape of that fraud is precisely document-versus-registry matching. At SMB scale the everyday cost is a person burning two to four days a month tying a shoebox of paper to a settlement statement, with duplicate payments, missed credit notes and part-payments as the silent leakage. Today's output is a spreadsheet nobody can audit back to the physical sheet it came from; this makes the audit trail a thing you can literally point at.
how_it_works: Two loops at different rates — the Apple FastVLM discipline that makes demos look smooth. FAST LOOP (30-60 fps, pure geometry, ZERO ML): OpenCV.js — take the green channel as cheap greyscale, adaptive LOCAL threshold by blur-compare (the atomic14 AR-Sudoku recipe; a global threshold dies under an Indian tube light), connected components, largest quads, four corners via a Manhattan-distance heuristic, cv.findHomography per sheet. Track sheet-to-sheet between frames by corner correspondence plus a small Kalman/optical-flow smoother so halos never flicker. Draw the halo and the line strike by PROJECTING points through the homography rather than warping pixels — that is what keeps the overlay glued and cheap enough for 60 fps. Optional printed ArUco tiles (aruco_ArucoDetector.detectMarkers is whitelisted in the default OpenCV.js build) as a rock-solid pose fallback under hostile lighting. SLOW LOOP (2-3 Hz, ONCE per newly-stabilised sheet, not per frame): warpPerspective to rectify, DocLayout-YOLO (ONNX, YOLO-speed, the only document model fast enough to run live) for region boxes, then PP-OCRv5 mobile det (4.7 MB, 28-58 ms CPU) + rec (16 MB, 5-21 ms CPU) for text — with PaddlePaddle/devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec and its ONNX sibling swapped in per-sheet by script detection. Fields (invoice no, date, GSTIN, taxable value, GST, total) come out by layout position plus regex, not by an LLM. MATCHER — deterministic rule engine over INTEGER PAISE, four stages: exact key (invoice_no + GSTIN + total), fuzzy invoice-no with amount tolerance +/-Rs 1 and date window +/-3 days, many-to-one and one-to-many grouping for part-payments, then duplicate detection by a (vendor, amount, date+/-2d) triple combined with a perceptual hash of the rectified sheet. Everything unmatched falls into a reason-coded exception list. MONEY LOOP: a matched-but-unpaid vendor invoice becomes a bounded Razorpay test-mode Payment Link or Payout, capped per vendor and per day, human-confirmed, and written to a hash-chained audit log that records both the rule that permitted it and the rule that would have stopped it.
features: Perspective-locked halo per sheet, projected through a per-sheet homography, surviving shoving, rotation and partial occlusion by a hand
Three-state colour semantics — green matched, amber duplicate or part-payment, red exception — legible with no legend and no caption
Line-level strike-through drawn ON the paper at the offending row, with the rupee delta floating just above the sheet
Deterministic four-stage matcher over integer paise: exact key, fuzzy invoice+amount tolerance, many-to-one part-payment grouping, duplicate triple
Duplicate-submission catch via perceptual hash of the rectified sheet, so a photocopy resubmitted next month lights amber before a human reads a single character
Batch mode: deal 50+ sheets under the camera in one continuous pan and get a match-rate readout plus a reason-coded exception list exported as CSV and signed JSON
Devanagari path: PP-OCRv5 Devanagari mobile rec (ONNX) swapped in per sheet by script detection, with accuracy MEASURED on real printed sheets and published, never claimed
ArUco fallback mode: a printed tile stuck on each sheet makes pose rock-solid under bad tube light — demoed on camera as an explicit, deliberate degradation path
'HOLDING LAST GOOD POSE' state with a closing confidence ring instead of jitter whenever a hand covers a sheet mid-read

Bounded payout execution: matched-but-unpaid invoices become a capped, human-confirmed Razorpay test-mode Payment Link or Payout, with the permitting rule and the would-have-blocked rule both printed into the audit line
GSTIN and vendor cross-check against a registry, with a green tick or red X landing directly on the GSTIN box on the paper
Exception triage ranked by rupees at risk rather than by row order, so the biggest hole is the first sheet you pick up
Optional Rs 200 thermal printer wired to the money loop, so every bounded action physically prints — the audit trail becomes a strip of paper accumulating on the desk
One-command evaluation harness that regenerates the 200-record batch, runs the matcher, and prints match rate, exception precision/recall and the full honest exception list
ai_judgment: Matching is a deterministic rule engine over integers, not an LLM. An LLM that 'decides' whether two amounts are the same is unauditable and can hallucinate a match — and a match here authorises a payout, so it is exactly the wrong place for a probabilistic component. Second deliberate NO: no image-forgery model on the scanned invoices. The same AIForge-Doc numbers apply (DocTamper AUC 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, GPT-4o judge at 0.509 against AI-inpainted receipts), so a 'this invoice was edited' heatmap would look impressive and mean nothing. Third deliberate NO: the entire fast loop contains zero ML — corner finding, homography, perspective projection and tracking are exact, explainable and 60 fps, and reaching for a model there would be slower AND less trustworthy. AI is used where it genuinely earns its place: OCR and layout, which is a perception job models are good at. There is exactly ONE narrowly-scoped VLM call in the whole system — fired only on sheets that already failed every deterministic stage — to propose a human-readable reason for the exception, written into the list as a SUGGESTION that can never change the match state. And an honest limit stated up front: handwritten Devanagari khata pages are a measured stretch goal, not a promise; the best-downloaded handwritten-Hindi model on Hugging Face has 85 downloads.
razorpay_fit: Track 04 asks to close one finance-ops loop across a 50+ record batch with a reported match rate and an honest exception list — this closes invoice-to-settlement reconciliation over 200 records. It runs on Razorpay test-mode Settlements (the official MCP server exposes settlements WITH reconciliation details), Invoices, Payment Links and Payouts. Settlement reconciliation is Razorpay's own reporting surface, so the demo is about their data model rather than a generic accounting toy, and the bounded payout action turns a report into a closed loop rather than a read-only view.
measurable: A 200-invoice held-out batch — 60 of them physically printed and filmed through the camera, 140 processed digitally — matched against a synthetic Razorpay settlement file containing 18 deliberately planted defects: 7 duplicates, 5 part-payments, 3 amount mismatches, 2 missing credit notes, 1 wrong GSTIN. Reported: auto-match rate, precision and recall of exception detection against the planted ground truth, FIELD-LEVEL OCR accuracy on total / invoice number / GSTIN measured from camera versus ground truth (separately for Latin and Devanagari sheets), median wall-clock seconds per sheet, and the complete exception list with reason codes — explicitly including the ones the system got wrong.
feasibility: The honest risks are all lighting and paper, and they are documented rather than guessed. The AR-Sudoku post-mortem and its Show HN thread state plainly that lighting is decisive, that it works better with paper flat on a table than hand-held, that recognition degrades when pointed at a screen, and that constant re-evaluation causes flicker bad enough that a user could not get a clean screen grab. All four are designed around: adaptive local thresholding instead of a global threshold, temporal smoothing plus a visible hold-last-good-pose state, an ArUco-sticker mode as the deterministic escape hatch, and a hard rule that we point at paper and never at a monitor. Second risk: thermal receipts and low-contrast GST prints will genuinely hurt OCR — the answer is to measure field accuracy and publish the number rather than assert one. Third: payload weight — OpenCV.js is 3.33 MB over the wire and PP-OCRv5 adds roughly 21 MB of models, so the load is staged such that halos appear before any text is read; on a slow connection the desk lights up first and the numbers arrive a second later, which actually reads better on camera. Fourth: heavily overlapping sheets will lose their quads — the demo deals them spread out, and I say so on camera rather than pretending otherwise.

name: COUNTER — the shop that prices itself
one_liner: A kirana counter with no barcode scanner and no POS: put the items down, they price themselves, and a UPI QR for the exact amount appears lying on the counter — which an AI buyer can also check out against.
the_gif: A phone clamped over a real shop counter, looking down. A hand slides actual Indian grocery items across the wood one at a time — a Parle-G packet, a Maggi bundle, a strip of shampoo sachets, a soap bar. The instant each one crosses the counter line a box snaps onto it and a rupee figure flies up out of the packet and lands in a running total floating in the air above the counter: Rs 10 -> Rs 22 -> Rs 32 -> Rs 42. Then the hand pulls the soap bar BACK off the counter and the total drops to Rs 32. The hand does a mid-air pinch, and a UPI QR materialises lying flat on the wooden counter in correct perspective, carrying the exact amount. A second physical phone comes into frame and scans it — and the QR on the counter flips green with a tick while that second phone is still in shot. Real packets, real hand, real counter, two devices in one unbroken frame.
why_it_looks_impossible: Every Indian has watched a shopkeeper add prices in his head or on a calculator and then say 'scan karo' over an open-amount QR. Here the amount is simply correct, instantly, with no barcode, no scanner beep and no typing. Taking an item back OFF the counter and watching the total fall is the beat that kills the 'it's a canned animation' reflex in one second. And the QR is not on a screen — it is lying on the wooden counter in perspective and stays there when the camera moves, and it is a REAL Razorpay QR that a second physical phone actually scans. A causal chain crossing a physical gap between two real devices in one continuous frame is the single most unfakeable-looking shot available.
problem: There are roughly 6.5 crore Indian merchants and 56.86 crore deployed QR codes, and the overwhelming majority run OPEN-AMOUNT QRs where the customer types the amount themselves. That produces short-payments and wrong-amount disputes, zero line-item data, no basket analytics, no catalog — and therefore nothing an AI buyer agent can transact against at all. Soundbox, the incumbent confirmation device, reaches only ~10-14% of merchants at Rs 100-150/month; a card machine is ~Rs 7,000 against Rs 1,300-1,500 for a soundbox, and a scanner-equipped POS is out of reach entirely. Meanwhile merchants are being pushed off QR from the other side — Karnataka's tax department pulled UPI data for FY22-FY25 and issued notices in 14,000 cases with receipts above Rs 40 lakh, and Bengaluru shopkeepers responded by pulling their stickers down and demanding cash. So anything that adds POS-grade line-item records has to pay for itself immediately. It does: a fixed-amount QR removes short-payment leakage, line items create a catalog, and a catalog is the only thing that makes the shop machine-transactable.
how_it_works: FAST LOOP (30-60 fps): YOLO26n ONNX for generic 'object on the counter' boxes. I measured this myself on an M3 Pro with onnxruntime 1.26 at 640x640 fp32 — 17.6 ms median, 18.8 ms p90, i.e. 57 fps on the plain CPU execution provider (bench script and raw output are in the repo). On an iPhone 17 Pro, Ultralytics publishes YOLO26n detection at 3.2 ms with the ANE, so on phone hardware the headroom goes into rendering, not the model. Boxes are drawn with supervision-grade annotators, never raw cv2.rectangle — the annotation quality is most of the perceived polish. SKU IDENTITY WITHOUT TRAINING: crop each box, take a CLIP/DINOv2 image embedding, cosine nearest-neighbour against the merchant's own enrolment gallery. Enrolment is the hero feature: hold a new packet up once, tap it, eight frames at varied poses go into the gallery, and the SKU is live in about four seconds with zero fine-tuning. YOLOE's visual-prompt mode (draw a box on a reference and boxes appear on future frames, three lines inside the ultralytics package) is the alternate path, and its prompt-free 4,585-name vocabulary provides the open-vocabulary category fallback. PRICE: a deterministic lookup, SKU -> paise, in the merchant's own catalog. Totals in integer paise. GATE: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (21 3D landmarks, 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6, first-class Web/JS build) with a hand-rolled pinch test measured as RATIOS of landmark distances rather than absolute pixels, so the gate holds at any camera distance — the one engineering lesson worth stealing from barehands. MONEY: POST /v1/payments/qr_codes with type upi_qr, usage single_use, fixed_amount true, payment_amount in paise, close_by set, and the line items in notes (max 15 pairs); the returned image_url is rendered onto the counter plane through a homography from a known-size ArUco tile taped to the counter. The qr_code.credited webhook flips it green in frame. AI BUYER LANE: the gallery built by enrolment IS a product feed, exposed through an agentic-checkout endpoint so an AI buyer agent can fetch it and complete a bounded test-mode checkout — the shop becomes machine-transactable purely as a side effect of pointing a camera at its counter.
features: Instant itemisation: a box and a rupee figure snap onto every item the moment it crosses the counter line, and the total DROPS when an item is taken back off
Running total anchored in the air above the physical counter plane rather than in a UI panel
Four-second SKU enrolment: hold a new packet up once, tap it, and it is live — nearest-neighbour embedding gallery, zero fine-tuning, no dataset, no training run
Abstain-by-design: low top-1 similarity or a thin top-1/top-2 margin renders the item as an amber '?', freezes the total, and blocks QR minting entirely
Real-world size prior derived from the counter homography and a known-size ArUco tile, to separate same-artwork different-gram SKUs (200 g vs 500 g Parle-G)
Pinch-to-mint gesture gate on MediaPipe hand landmarks with ratio-based thresholds, so 'every money action is gated' is something the viewer SEES rather than reads
Hard cap above which the gesture is disallowed entirely and an explicit tap is required — the gate gets harder as the money gets bigger
Counter-anchored fixed-amount Razorpay QR rendered in perspective on the physical wood, carrying line items in notes and a close_by expiry
Live credited state: the qr_code.credited webhook flips the counter QR green with a stamp, in frame, while the customer's phone is still in shot

Basket-change stopping rule: touch the basket after minting and the old QR is closed before a new one is created — never two live codes for one basket, and the auto-expiry edge case is handled explicitly
Catalog-as-a-side-effect: enrolment builds a real product feed exposed through an agentic-checkout endpoint, making the shop transactable by an AI buyer
AI-buyer demo lane: an agent asks for 'atta under Rs 300, today', pulls the feed, completes a bounded test-mode checkout, and a physical bell or soundbox on the counter rings
Upsell chip grounded in the merchant's own basket history, floated over the counter and never auto-added to the basket
Hash-chained audit log recording, per basket: items, the evidence crop, similarity scores, the rule that permitted the mint, and the cap that would have stopped it
ai_judgment: The model proposes an identity; a deterministic table decides the price; integer paise arithmetic decides the total. The single most important deliberate NO: we do NOT read the price off the packet with a VLM or OCR. MRP text is small, angled, glossy and often overprinted, and a hallucinated rupee figure is a real short-payment on a real counter — so the price comes only from the merchant's own catalog, and if the SKU is uncertain the system ABSTAINS with an amber '?' rather than guessing. Abstain is a first-class outcome, and its rate is a published metric. Second deliberate NO: no LLM anywhere in the money path — minting a fixed-amount QR is the only money action, it is bounded by a per-basket cap and a close_by expiry, and it is gated by a physical human gesture visible in the frame. Third deliberate NO: pose is not learned. Where the QR sits on the counter is a homography from four known corners — exact, explainable, and it cannot drift the way a learned pose estimator can. Fourth: no customer face, no biometric, nothing about the person is captured; the camera only ever looks down at goods, which keeps the whole thing clean under DPDP.
razorpay_fit: Track 01 asks either to grow merchant revenue on test-mode APIs or to make a merchant transactable by an AI buyer — this does both from the same camera loop. QR Codes API (create / fetch / close / payments) with fixed_amount and payment_amount in paise is the money primitive; Payment Links are the fallback when the QR cannot be rendered; webhooks are the audit trail; razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server is the agent-facing tool surface. Every money action is explainable (line items travel in notes), bounded (per-basket cap, single_use, close_by expiry), gated (a physical gesture or an explicit tap above the cap), and audited (webhook plus hash-chained local log). Track 01 is also the least crowded specified track — roughly 18 of the 296 public buildathon repos — and not one of those 296 repos mentions a camera.
measurable: A held-out set of 60 unseen counter arrangements, 3-8 items each, roughly 300 item instances, drawn from a 40-SKU enrolled catalog and shot on a different day under different light with item poses the enrolment gallery never saw. Reported: item-level precision and recall, SKU top-1 accuracy, abstain rate, and the headline number — BASKET-TOTAL EXACT-MATCH RATE plus mean absolute rupee error per basket — together with how often an abstain correctly prevented a wrong total (which is the metric that actually matters, because a confident wrong price is worse than a question mark). Baseline for comparison: a human typing the amount into an open-amount QR, measured for both error rate and seconds per basket, on the same 60 arrangements.
feasibility: The killer risk is honest and specific: near-identical SKUs. Same brand, different gram weight, identical artwork will collide in embedding space — 200 g versus 500 g Parle-G is the canonical failure. Mitigations are a real-world size prior from the calibrated counter plane and aggressive abstention, and the confusion matrix gets published rather than hidden. Second: occlusion and stacking — items piled on each other will drop out, so the demo deliberately places items flat and spread, and I say that on camera instead of pretending it generalises. Third: the hand occludes the item it just placed, so each item needs a short settle delay before it commits, which conveniently also stops the total flickering. Fourth: glare from plastic packaging on a glass counter degrades both detection and embedding — a matte counter and diffuse light are the demo conditions, stated aloud. Fifth: the QR render is Tier-1 anchoring (centre and scale from four corners), not full 6-DoF PnP with Kalman smoothing; in a handheld five-second shot it reads as glued, and I will not claim pose accuracy I did not measure. Sixth: the second-phone scan is the one beat that needs a network round-trip, so a webhook stall would stall the green flip — the fallback is a polled GET on qr_codes/:id/payments with a visible 'waiting' ring, which is itself the graceful-degradation story. Deliberate on-camera failure beat: hold up an unenrolled packet — it renders amber '?', the total refuses to advance, the QR cannot be minted at all, then one tap enrols it and the basket completes.

name: JAAL
one_liner: Point your phone at the QR sticker taped to a shop counter and watch the fraud ring it secretly belongs to grow out of the paper into the air above the counter — and collapse back into it when you peel the sticker off.
the_gif: Full-bleed vertical phone camera, handheld, one continuous take. A grubby paper UPI QR sticker taped crooked to a wooden shop counter; the tape edges and a thumb are visible. Four thin white brackets SNAP onto the sticker's four corners and stay glued there as the phone drifts. A single thread of warm gold light rises out of the paper square and arcs up into one calm gold sphere hovering ~20cm above the counter, with small motes trickling up the thread. The phone pans 30cm right to the second sticker on the same counter. Same corner snap — but this thread comes out RED, bends sideways, misses the gold sphere entirely, and where it lands seven more red spheres pop into existence one after another and wire themselves together into a slowly rotating ring in the air above the counter, red motes now racing around the closed loop like current. The counter, the tape, the wood grain and the thumb are visible behind the whole structure the entire time. Final beat: a hand reaches into frame, gets a nail under the fake sticker's corner, and PEELS IT OFF — and the entire red web instantly collapses, drains back down the thread into the paper as it lifts, and the frame goes back to being an ordinary counter. Two floating monospace handles over the two stickers are the only text on screen.
why_it_looks_impossible: A piece of paper on a counter is visibly generating a 3D structure that stays locked to it in correct perspective while the camera moves, and a purely physical act — a human fingernail peeling a sticker — destroys the structure in real time. There is no visible UI, no button, no panel; reality itself has been annotated. And the thing being revealed is invisible by construction: the fake sticker is pixel-for-pixel indistinguishable from the real one to a human eye, which is exactly why the Delhi case ran for weeks.
problem: QR sticker swap. Delhi, 13 Dec 2025: Rs 1.40 lakh diverted from a Chandni Chowk boutique in two payments; the 19-year-old arrested on 22 Dec had 100+ edited and original QR codes on his phone and told police he used AI image-editing apps to swap the bank details while keeping the QR's appearance unchanged. Khajuraho, Jan 2025: stickers pasted over genuine ones overnight at ~6 establishments including petrol pumps, discovered only because one customer read the payee name and saw 'Chhotu Tiwari'. Scale of the exposed surface: 56.86 crore QR codes across ~6.5 crore merchants. A 102-merchant field study in Srinagar (Jul 2026) found 57.8% had lost money to fraudulent digital transactions, 60.8% display QRs as loose paper stickers, 41.2% display them outside the counter in blind spots, and 90.2% had never heard of the 1930 helpline. Detection latency today is hours to days, via CCTV.
how_it_works: TWO LOOPS AT DIFFERENT RATES. Fast loop (25 Hz, Web Worker): nimiq/qr-scanner (2.9k stars, MIT, ~59.3 kB min / 16.3 kB gz, maxScansPerSecond default 25) returns rawValue AND cornerPoints. The upi://pay?pa=&pn=&am= payload is parsed by a plain regex — no model. POSE: OpenCV.js findHomography maps the 4 cornerPoints to a unit square (I verified findHomography, solvePnP, warpPerspective and Rodrigues are all in the default opencv.js export list via platforms/js/opencv_js.config.py; 3.33 MB brotli over the wire), and the resulting 3x3 becomes a three.js camera matrix so the graph is glued to the paper. Tier-1 fallback is a centroid+scale screen-space anchor if the homography jitters. TRUTH (slow loop, ~1 Hz): the decoded VPA is compared against the merchant's registered QR via Razorpay's QR Codes API (GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id and /payments) through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (230 stars, official, remote at mcp.razorpay.com/mcp). String equality. GRAPH: an append-only synthetic ledger of 5,000 transactions with planted mule rings; ring detection is Tarjan SCC cycle-finding plus a temporal fan-out/fan-in score plus shared-device and shared-QR edges — deterministic. RENDER: 3d-force-graph (6.3k stars, MIT) with graphData() streaming nodes in live, emitParticle(link) fired once per replayed transaction (one call = one visible rupee), and postProcessingComposer() wired to a selective UnrealBloom pass so ONLY ring nodes ignite while legitimate nodes stay matte grey. Render at 60fps on WebGL2, fully decoupled from the 25 Hz scanner. OPTIONAL SECONDARY: YOLO26n ONNX (measured by me on this M3 Pro: 17.6 ms median = 57 fps on CPUExecutionProvider) flags a sticker-over-sticker double edge — it can only ADD suspicion, never clear a code.
features: Live QR corner lock with a perspective-glued 3D overlay driven by an OpenCV.js homography from the four cornerPoints — the web stays welded to the paper as the phone moves.
The decoded payee name and VPA rendered in large type floating above the physical sticker — automating the single human signal that has ever actually caught this fraud (Khajuraho).
Deterministic registry verdict from the Razorpay QR Codes API: green if the decoded pa matches the merchant's registered QR, red if it does not. No score, no confidence, no model.
Multi-QR census: every sticker in frame gets boxed and labelled with whose account it pays, simultaneously — the Hoskote biryani outlet had 30 QR codes on one counter and Rs 1.47 crore through them.
Fraud-ring eruption: on a bad VPA, the mule network that account belongs to assembles in 3D above the sticker with selective bloom firing at the exact frame the cycle closes.
emitParticle-per-transaction, so every rupee in the replay is one visible mote travelling one edge — the audit log rendered as weather.

Scrub-to-rewind: drag a timeline and the ring un-builds itself back to the single first transaction. Because the backend is an event-sourced append-only log, every intermediate frame is real state, not an animation — no rrweb.

Peel-to-kill bounded action: on a confirmed tamper, exactly one money action is offered — POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close on the compromised QR plus mint a replacement — behind an explicit confirm, with both API responses written to the log.
Overnight diff (the Khajuraho story, automated): a signed snapshot of each standee at shutter-down, auto-diffed at shutter-up, morning frame lights red if the payload changed.

Confidence-hold state: if the camera moves too fast or the corners get noisy, the web desaturates, freezes at last-good pose, and a thin ring closes as a timer runs down. No money action can fire while held. It re-locks with a snap when the phone steadies.
Offline-first: decode plus a cached registry work with zero network. With no connectivity the verdict degrades to 'unverified — last synced 4h ago' rather than a false green.
Append-only audit strip: {frame hash, decoded payload, registry response, latency, verdict, action, operator} as JSONL, exportable, and the same log that drives the replay.
Held-out scoring harness with a published generator seed a judge can re-run, scoring ring membership precision/recall separately from the (trivially perfect) deterministic VPA check.
WebGPU→WASM graceful degradation with a one-line capability banner, because Firefox ships WebGPU disabled by default on every version.
ai_judgment: Vision is used in exactly one place and it is a place vision is genuinely excellent: finding the four corners of a high-contrast square in a camera frame. The VERDICT is never a model's opinion — it is a string comparison of the decoded VPA against the Razorpay registry, which is why it can be 100% precise and why I can say so honestly. THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT BUILD, with the measurements that killed them: (1) Pixel forensics on the sticker. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026) forged numeric fields in 4,061 real receipts with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Ideogram v2 Edit and measured TruFor at AUC 0.751 (down from 0.96 on NIST16), DocTamper at 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge at 0.509 — literally chance. A forensics component here would be theatre. TruFor's licence also forbids shipping it. (2) Monocular depth to spot the sticker-over-sticker step. A paper sticker is 0.1–0.3mm; Depth-Anything-V2-Small is scale-free relative depth and I measured it at 323.6 ms / 3.1 fps at 518x518 on this M3 Pro. Too coarse AND too slow. Tested-and-rejected, documented in the repo. (3) An LLM as the ring detector. Precision and recall from a language model are not reproducible across runs, so the detector is Tarjan SCC plus a temporal fan-out heuristic with declared thresholds. The LLM appears exactly once in the whole system: writing the one-sentence human explanation attached to a verdict that has already been decided by code.
razorpay_fit: The QR Codes API is simultaneously the REGISTRY (what this merchant's QR should decode to) and the KILL SWITCH: create (type upi_qr, usage single_use/multiple_use, fixed_amount, payment_amount in paise, close_by, notes up to 15 pairs), fetch, list payments on that QR, close. Webhooks qr_code.created / qr_code.credited / qr_code.closed give the real-time truth feed. A real edge case I handle visibly on camera because it is a genuine stopping-rule problem: qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry, only on manual close — so expired codes are reconciled by poll and the UI shows that reconciliation happening rather than pretending the webhook covered it. All of it is reachable through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server without a local install.
measurable: Held-out synthetic ledger of 5,000 transactions across 900 accounts with 40 planted mule rings, generated from a published seed the judge can re-run to get a different held-out set. Reported: node-level precision / recall / F1 for ring membership, ring-level detection rate, and median time-to-detection measured in transactions after ring closure. Reported SEPARATELY and honestly: the VPA-mismatch check is deterministic, so it is not an accuracy claim — instead I report decode success rate and registry-resolution coverage across N=120 real photographed standees under four lighting conditions (daylight, tube light, glass-counter glare, dusk), which is the number that actually determines whether the product works in a shop.
feasibility: THE REAL RISK IS THE ANCHOR, NOT THE DETECTION. Handheld jitter plus 1–2 px corner noise makes a homography-driven overlay wobble; the fix is a 4-point exponential smoother plus the hold-last-good-pose state, which conveniently is also the failure-recovery beat judges score. If the homography still fights me on the day, Tier-1 (centroid + scale, screen-space) still reads as glued in a 5-second handheld clip — I would ship Tier 1 first and upgrade only if time remains. LIGHTING IS DECISIVE and I am not going to pretend otherwise: the AR-Sudoku post-mortem is explicit that adaptive LOCAL thresholding by blur-compare beats any global threshold, and that hand-held is worse than camera-moving-over-flat-paper. Bad shop lighting is the normal case in India, not the edge case. COLD LOAD is ~3.3 MB brotli for opencv.js on top of the scanner — preload before the camera opens or the first three seconds are a white screen, which is fatal for a demo whose premise is 'instant'. PERFORMANCE: bloom plus a 60fps 3D scene plus a 25 Hz scanner will thermal-throttle a mid-range Android; 3d-force-graph's own 'larger graph' showcase is ~4k elements, so I cap visible nodes in the low thousands — more nodes reads as grey mush anyway. WHAT COULD ACTUALLY EMBARRASS ME ON CAMERA: pointing at a QR displayed on a phone screen instead of paper (recognition measurably degrades on screens), and a lighting change mid-take causing a decode drop right at the peel. Both are rehearsable. Verify early that nimiq/qr-scanner returns cornerPoints on the native-BarcodeDetector path as well as the ZXing path — if not, force the ZXing path.

name: PARCHI
one_liner: Slide a paper receipt under the camera and the ink lifts off it and pours into one of three wells — matched, duplicate, or the one where the light just hangs there and refuses to settle, because that's your exception list.
the_gif: Top-down, full-bleed, warm side light on a dark wooden desk. A hand slides a curled thermal receipt into frame and lets go. The instant the paper stops moving, its printed numbers DETACH — each digit lifts a couple of millimetres off the surface and hangs there shimmering, still in exactly the right place on the page. Then the whole receipt DISSOLVES: a few thousand gold motes peel off the ink and stream up and out of frame into one of three luminous wells hovering at the top edge. Left well swallows them with a green flare and goes quiet. The hand pulls the (still perfectly ordinary, still printed) paper away and slides the next one in. Second receipt: the motes veer to the middle well and BOUNCE — repelled off an amber shell, scattering. Third receipt: the motes reach the right-hand well and just… stop. They hang in the air, slowly orbiting, unresolved. Then the tempo doubles, then quadruples — slide, dissolve, pour, slide, dissolve, pour — the physical stack beside the frame visibly shrinking, receipts flicking past, until the desk is empty. Last frame holds: two wells dark and quiet, and nine points of light still turning slowly in the third.
why_it_looks_impossible: The ink comes off the paper. The physical object is still in your hand, unchanged and still printed, but on screen it has been emptied — and the light comes off the ACTUAL glyph positions, so when you tilt the sheet the emptying follows the tilt. Nobody has ever made reconciliation look like anything, and here the least filmable thing in finance ops (the exception list) is the most beautiful object in the frame.
problem: Indian finance ops still runs on paper: GST invoices, thermal receipts, delivery challans, cheque leaves. Matching them to settlements is a manual eyeball job done by a person with a ruler. The rupee number underneath is enormous and accelerating — central tax authorities detected Rs 74,782 crore of fake Input Tax Credit across 30,162 cases in FY26, up from Rs 58,772.51 crore / 15,283 cases in FY25 and Rs 36,373.36 crore / 9,190 cases in FY24. That is more than a doubling in two years, and the shape of the fraud is exactly the shape of the work: a document that does not match a registry. Track 04 asks for one finance-ops loop closed across a 50+ record batch with a reported match rate and an honest exception list; the honest exception list is the part every submission fudges.
how_it_works: GEOMETRY FIRST, NO MODEL. OpenCV.js: green channel as cheap greyscale → adaptive LOCAL threshold by blur-compare (not a global threshold — this is the specific thing the AR-Sudoku post-mortem says makes or breaks it under bad light) → connected components for the largest object → Manhattan-distance heuristic for the four corners → findHomography → rectified crop. Exact, explainable, sub-millisecond on a small ROI. OCR FAST PATH (12–28 fps, live): PP-OCRv5 mobile det (4.7 MB, 79.0 acc, 28.15 ms CPU) + mobile rec (16 MB, 81.29 acc, 5.32 ms CPU) ≈ 35–80 ms end-to-end. Devanagari path uses PaddlePaddle/devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec, which publishes an _onnx sibling so it can run in the browser. LAYOUT: DocLayout-YOLO (2.3k stars) snaps line-item region boxes live — it is the one document model fast enough to run on a moving page. PARTICLE EMITTERS: each OCR character box is projected back through the homography every frame, so emitters sit on the real ink and track the paper when it tilts. SLOW VERIFIER (1–2 Hz, server, never in the camera loop): PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B (96.3% OmniDocBench v1.6, 111 languages including Hindi) re-reads any field whose fast-path character confidence is below threshold; when the better read lands, that field's particle visibly stutters and re-forms. MATCHING IS DETERMINISTIC: tier 1 exact join on (amount in integer paise, date ±2 days, last-6 of UTR/RRN); tier 2 bounded fuzzy (Levenshtein ≤2 on the merchant string, ±Rs 1 amount tolerance for rounding); every tier and every tolerance is logged per row. TRUTH: Razorpay test-mode Payments, Settlements (with reconciliation details) and Invoices via razorpay-mcp-server. RENDER: three.js instanced points (~3–5k per sheet; the shipped webgl_instancing_performance example goes to 10,000 instances) with pmndrs/postprocessing (Zlib) selective bloom so only the wells glow.
features: Live corner-lock and perspective rectification of a handheld, curled, crumpled thermal receipt using deterministic OpenCV.js homography — zero model, zero training, exact.
Per-glyph particle emitters seeded from real OCR character boxes and re-projected through the homography every frame, so the light comes off the actual ink and follows the paper when you tilt it.
Three gravity wells with genuinely different physics — absorb (matched), repel (duplicate), suspend (exception) — so the classification is legible with no legend and no colour key.
The exception well IS the exception list. Tap it and each suspended mote expands into a card with a reason code. There is no separate table anywhere in the product.

Duplicate detection by perceptual hash of the rectified crop combined with the (amount, timestamp, merchant) tuple — catches the same physical receipt being presented twice, which is the manual-claims fraud pattern nobody implements.
Devanagari live path via PP-OCRv5's Devanagari ONNX recogniser for handwritten-adjacent kirana bills, with accuracy I measured on my own labelled set rather than a number I copied off a model card.
Two-tier confidence escalation: low-confidence fields get re-read server-side by PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B at 1–2 Hz, and you can SEE the correction land as the particle re-forms.

Arithmetic is done in integer paise by code, not by a model: line items must sum to the printed total before the sheet is eligible for matching at all. A sheet that fails its own arithmetic never reaches the matcher.

Hard stopping rule rendered physically: if the fast reader and the slow reader disagree on an amount, that record can never be auto-matched regardless of any score, and its motes go to the exception well immediately.
Batch mode across 60 physical sheets with a live match rate that is computed from the log, not animated, plus CSV export and an append-only JSONL audit trail.
Scrub-to-replay the entire batch from the event log — the particle run re-executes identically because the log is the state, which makes the compliance artifact and the spectacle the same object.
Deliberate-miss mode for the pitch video: hand it a coffee-stained, folded receipt on camera and show it REFUSE rather than guess, with the reason on screen.
Two-paper mode: an invoice and a settlement print side by side on the desk, with a thread of light drawn between matching lines across the physical gap between the two sheets.
Bounded recovery action on a confirmed over-charge: POST /v1/payments/:id/refund in test mode, behind an explicit human confirm, with the API response written into the audit line.
ai_judgment: OCR is the only model on the money path and it is doing a job vision is genuinely good at — turning printed glyphs into characters. Everything downstream of the characters is code. THE MATCH IS DETERMINISTIC ON PURPOSE: a tiered join with published tolerances, because a match rate produced by an LLM is not reproducible across runs and therefore cannot be scored on a held-out batch — and 'report match rate' is literally the track's bar. THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT DO: (1) I did not use a document-VLM as the matcher, and I did not let any model do arithmetic — totals are summed in integer paise by code, because floating-point money and probabilistic addition are both ways to lose a rupee you cannot explain. (2) I did not put a 7B document VLM in the camera loop. olmOCR-2-7B and Surya are excellent (83.3 olmOCR-bench for Surya at 650M) but Surya runs at 0.108 pages/s on Apple Silicon — roughly nine seconds per page — so it lives behind the fast reader as a 1–2 Hz verifier, never in front of it. (3) I did not use image-forgery localisation (TruFor / DocTamper) to decide whether a receipt was doctored, for the AIForge-Doc reasons: 0.751 and 0.563 AUC against diffusion inpainting, with pixel IoU 0.020. A receipt is verified against the ledger, not against its own pixels. The LLM writes exception narratives only, after the record has already been classified by rules.
razorpay_fit: This is Track 04 almost verbatim: close one finance-ops loop across a 50+ record batch of synthetic data and report match rate plus an honest exception list. It runs on Razorpay test-mode Payments, Settlements (the settlement recon detail endpoint is what makes the join possible) and Invoices, all reachable through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server. The one bounded money action — a test-mode refund on a confirmed over-charge — is gated behind a human confirm and produces an audit line containing the matched pair, the tolerance tier that matched them, and the API response.
measurable: 60 physically printed synthetic receipts — 40 clean thermal, 8 deliberately crumpled, 6 Devanagari, 6 constructed to be genuinely unmatchable — reconciled against a 200-row synthetic settlement file. Reported: (a) match rate, (b) PRECISION of auto-matches, i.e. how many auto-matches were wrong, which is the number that actually matters and the one most submissions omit, (c) field-level character error rate on amount / date / UTR against ground truth I typed by hand, reported separately for Latin and Devanagari, and (d) the complete exception list with a reason code per row. 20 of the 60 are printed from a published generator seed so a judge can produce a fresh held-out set. If the Devanagari CER is bad I will report the bad number — I am not going to promise Hindi accuracy I have not measured on real pages.
feasibility: THERMAL PAPER IS THE ENEMY. It is low-contrast, it curls, and it glares under any overhead light. Adaptive local thresholding helps; a diffuse side lamp on a matte dark desk helps more, and that is how I would shoot it. The genuinely hard part is small printed amounts photographed at an angle — which is precisely why the rectification pass exists, and why I will report CER rather than claim a match rate the OCR cannot support. THE EMITTER-SWIM PROBLEM IS THE REAL TECHNICAL RISK: OCR runs at 12–28 fps but render is 60, so the per-glyph emitters must be interpolated along the tracked homography between OCR frames or the light will visibly swim off the ink. Mitigation is to drive emitter positions from the homography (which updates every frame, cheaply) and only refresh their identities on OCR ticks. FALLBACK if per-glyph still swims: emit from DocLayout-YOLO line-region boxes instead of individual glyphs — coarser, but 'the text is dissolving' still reads perfectly in five seconds. WHAT COULD BREAK ON CAMERA: a decode failure on the very sheet I chose for the hero beat (rehearse with a fixed deck), and the flicker problem the AR-Sudoku Show HN thread flagged — constant re-evaluation causing the overlay to strobe. The fix is temporal smoothing plus an explicit 'holding last good read' state, which is also the failure-recovery beat. I will not point the camera at a monitor displaying a receipt; digit recognition measurably degrades on screens and that is a documented, avoidable self-own.

name: ANJALI
one_liner: Your merchant's failed payments fall past you as a stream of liquid gold light, and you cup your bare hands under it — the light pools in your palms, leaks through the gaps between your fingers, and when you tip your hands it flies back up and the leak slows.
the_gif: Full-bleed, dark room, one continuous take from a laptop webcam. A steady column of liquid gold light is falling down the frame — thousands of individual motes, not a texture — and it is missing everything, pouring past and vanishing off the bottom edge. Two bare hands rise into frame, palms up, and cup together. The light POOLS in them. It obeys the actual shape of the fingers — it heaps up in the hollow of the palms, sloshes to one side when the hands tilt, and a thin bright trickle escapes through the gap between the two little fingers and keeps falling. The hands close slightly and the pool compacts into one dense bright bead. The hands tip right and the bead rolls off the fingertips and shoots UPWARD, back against gravity, out of the top of frame — and the falling stream visibly THINS. The hands open flat and everything left spills and falls again. No cursor, no rings on the fingertips, no panel, no text. Just two hands and light behaving like water that somehow knows exactly where the fingers are.
why_it_looks_impossible: The liquid is occluded by the fingers and leaks through the gaps BETWEEN them. It is obeying the exact silhouette of a hand the webcam has never seen before, at 60fps, with no depth camera, no glove, no marker, no green screen — and then it disobeys gravity on command. The AR-calculator demos the builder loves make numbers appear near a hand; this makes a physical substance respect a hand.
problem: Revenue at risk from failed and abandoned payments, and the fact that once money is actually gone in India it is never coming back — Madhya Pradesh recovered Rs 1.94 crore of Rs 1,054 crore lost to cyber fraud between May 2021 and July 2025, which is 0.18%. All the leverage is in the seconds around the failure, not after it. That is also exactly the window the regulator has just formalised: RBI's April 2026 discussion paper proposes a one-hour hold on P2P transfers above Rs 10,000 in which the payer keeps a cancel option, requires the bank to state the NATURE of its suspicion when it asks for reconfirmation, adds a whitelisting override for trusted payees, and adds a one-stroke kill switch. On the merchant side the standard fix — blind auto-retry — burns issuer goodwill and customer trust, which is why 'bounded, with stopping rules' is the actual product requirement and not a compliance chore.
how_it_works: HANDS: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker via @mediapipe/tasks-vision v1.0.1 (4.49M npm downloads/week), 21 3D landmarks per hand, num_hands 2, published at 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6. It runs in a Web Worker with OffscreenCanvas (Safari 16.4+, Chrome 69+) because MediaPipe's own docs warn that detectForVideo() runs synchronously and blocks the UI thread — that decoupling is why the sim holds 60fps while inference runs at ~25. COLLISION BOUNDARY, NO MODEL: I build a polygon per frame from the landmarks — the palm quad (0,5,9,13,17) plus per-finger capsules down each joint chain — and turn it into a 2D signed-distance field that the particles collide against. That is exact geometry, essentially free, and it is the thing that makes the light leak between fingers instead of sitting on a rectangle. All gesture gates are measured as RATIOS of landmark distances normalised by wrist-to-middle-MCP, never absolute pixels, so they hold at any camera distance — that single trick is the difference between a demo that works at my tuning distance and one that works when a judge tries it. PARTICLES: three.js GPGPU-via-texture on WebGL2 (the webgl_gpgpu_birds / protoplanet pattern) targeting 30–60k motes at 60fps, with a WebGPU upgrade path — three.js ships webgpu_compute_particles at 200,000 and the TSL attractors example at 262,144. Each mote carries a real record id. FLOW RATE IS NOT DECORATIVE: motes per second equals at-risk rupees per second off the live synthetic failure feed, and mote colour encodes failure class (issuer decline, UPI collect timeout, mandate lapse, card expiry). MONEY: Razorpay test-mode Orders / Payments / Payment Links / Refunds / Payouts via razorpay-mcp-server; the decline reason code drives the diagnosis. THE POLICY ENGINE IS A RULES TABLE: max 2 retries per payment, minimum 20-minute spacing, never retry a hard decline code, hard cap of Rs 25,000 per batch, never contact the same customer twice in 24 hours.
features: Hand-silhouette fluid: 30–60k GPU particles colliding against a per-frame polygon SDF built from 21 landmarks, so light pools in the palm and genuinely leaks between the fingers.
Flow rate equals real money rate — the stream visibly thickens when a batch of failures lands and thins as you recover them, so the whole KPI is a physical property of the image.
Colour-coded failure taxonomy carried in the stream itself, so you can watch the failure mix change without a legend, a chart or a single word.

Physical gesture gate on every money action: nothing executes without a measured pinch-and-tilt, and the gesture event itself (with its measured ratios) is written to the audit log as the authorisation record.

Policy bounds rendered as physics: when a proposed retry would breach a rule, the bead physically will not leave your hand — it strains, shakes, and falls back. The safety control is something you feel, not something you read.
Two-hand cup equals HOLD — the RBI-shaped pause. The bead sits in your hands under a closing countdown ring and can be released at any moment before it fires.
Diagnosis before action: each caught bead expands in-frame into a one-line cause derived from the decline code plus the proposed bounded action. No side panel, no modal.
Stopping rules made visible: when the batch cap is reached, the entire stream freezes mid-air and desaturates to grey, and nothing can be caught until it is manually reset.
Held-out A/B built into the run: half the at-risk batch is a no-touch control, so 'money recovered' is reported as a lift over control rather than a flattering gross number.

Failure recovery on camera: hands leave frame mid-action, tracking is lost, the bead freezes and desaturates, a hold ring closes, and NOTHING fires; hands return and it re-locks with a snap. Ten seconds that answer the 'one failure handled gracefully' bar better than any slide.

Complete lifecycle audit: every mote's record id → caught-at timestamp → gesture hash and measured ratios → action → API response → outcome, as append-only JSONL, and scrubbing the timeline re-runs the entire rain identically because the log is the state.

Compliant escalation: once the retry budget is exhausted a record escalates to a human-reviewed queue and is never given a third contact attempt — the escalation is visible as motes leaving the scene upward into a holding cloud.
Clip production rig: a transparent-alpha OBS render route plus a portrait 9:16 mode and a hide-cursors flag, so the published clip reads as bare-hands sorcery with no UI at all.

Graceful degradation on two axes: no WebGPU falls back to WebGL2 instanced points at reduced count with a visible banner, and no hands detected for 3 seconds reverts the app to a plain keyboard-driven approval list, stated on screen rather than silently.
ai_judgment: There is no model anywhere in the money decision. Hand landmarks are a perception input; the GATE is a deterministic ratio threshold; the collision boundary is exact geometry; the recovery policy is a rules table with declared caps and spacings — because 'why did it retry?' has to be answerable with a rule id, not a token distribution. THINGS I DELIBERATELY DID NOT USE: (1) No LLM decides whether to retry, how much, or when. A retry that costs a merchant issuer goodwill needs a citable rule, and a probabilistic policy cannot be audited across a batch. (2) I deliberately did NOT use MediaPipe's canned Gesture Recognizer (8.37 MB bundle, 16.76 ms CPU, and note its GPU path is SLOWER than CPU at 20.87 ms). I hand-roll two gates from raw landmarks instead: 8.4 MB lighter, and — the actual reason — the thresholds are numbers I chose, so I can print them in the audit log. Google publishes no accuracy figures for the canned recogniser, which makes it unauditable for a money gate. (3) I deliberately do NOT use MediaPipe's z axis. It is weak; every serious demo in this genre fakes depth from landmark distances, so the sim is 2D-with-derived-depth and I say that out loud rather than implying stereo. The LLM's only job is drafting customer-facing recovery message copy, offline, from a reviewed template bank, never in the loop.
razorpay_fit: Track 03 verbatim: detect revenue at risk, diagnose it, execute a bounded recovery workflow, with measured money recovered across a batch, compliant escalation, stopping rules and an audit trail. Every one of those five clauses has a visual: the stream is the detection, the bead expansion is the diagnosis, the gesture is the gate, the freeze is the stopping rule, and the scrubbable replay is the audit trail. Built on Razorpay test-mode Orders, Payments, Payment Links, Refunds and Payouts through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server, with the payment's decline reason code as the diagnostic input.
measurable: A held-out batch of 400 synthetic at-risk payments from a published seed, split 200 treatment / 200 control. Reported: rupees recovered in treatment versus control (the LIFT, not the gross), recovery rate broken out by failure class, actions taken per recovered rupee, count of policy blocks that fired and which rule fired them, and the honest count of records the system refused to touch at all. Plus one number nobody else will report: the GATE'S OWN false-fire rate, measured over 200 deliberate non-gestures (waving, scratching, reaching for coffee) — because an authorisation gate that fires by accident is not a feature, it is a defect, and if that number is bad the honest thing is to raise the threshold and report the resulting missed-gesture rate too.
feasibility: THE HARD PART IS OCCLUSION, NOT TRACKING. MediaPipe gives landmarks, not a mask, so 'light behind the fingers' is a polygon approximation and WILL show seams at the finger edges under fast motion. Motion blur breaks tracking outright, and the palm going edge-on causes self-occlusion failures. Mitigations: keep the demo motion slow and deliberate, feather the polygon edge, and add a 2–3 frame temporal smoother — overdone, that smoother introduces visible lag, so it is a real tradeoff I will have to tune on camera rather than in theory. COLD LOAD IS BRUTAL: ~11 MB over the wire (3.12 MB brotli for the vision wasm plus 7.82 MB for hand_landmarker.task, which is served UNCOMPRESSED). Preload it behind a first-paint scene or the opening three seconds are a white screen, which is fatal for a demo whose entire premise is 'instant' — and on Indian 4G it is worse. DERIVATIVE RISK, NAMED HONESTLY: jaredrhod/barehands went from creation on 2026-08-15 to 702 stars and 140 forks in eight days, and it owns the 'bare hands manipulate floating objects' genre right now. Shipping something structurally similar six weeks later reads as a clone to anyone who has seen it. The only defensible differentiator is that the thing in your hands is a FLUID that is a real ledger with a record id per mote, not glass cards — if that does not land visually in the first two seconds, this idea should be cut rather than shipped. FALLBACK if the fluid sim fights the tracker: drop to one hand and a smaller, denser bead — fewer particles, sharper silhouette, less painterly, but the 'it is in my palm' read survives. WHAT COULD EMBARRASS ME LIVE: a lighting change causing a tracking dropout at the exact moment of the tip-right gesture. That is also, conveniently, the failure-recovery beat, so it is the one break I would rather have happen on camera than off it.

name: NAZAR — the counter that watches the shelf
track: 04 AI Finance Controller (primary) — with a Track 02 defense-only sub-loop
one_liner: A phone propped over a shop counter watches what physically leaves the shelf, mints a real Razorpay QR for exactly that amount, and turns the counter green only when the money actually lands.
the_gif: TOP-DOWN, ONE UNBROKEN SHOT, ~5 SECONDS. Frame is a real shop counter — scuffed laminate, a strip of shampoo sachets, a biscuit packet, a bottle of oil. A bare hand slides the biscuit packet across from left to right. THE INSTANT it crosses the middle of the counter a rounded white box snaps onto it with '₹20' inside, and a big luminous ₹20 appears floating flat ON the counter surface next to it — not on a HUD, lying on the laminate in perspective, like paint. Hand slides the sachets: box snaps, floating number rolls 20 → 65. Hand slides the oil: 65 → 205. Now a SECOND hand enters from the top of frame holding a phone, screen up, showing a UPI 'Payment Successful ₹205'. A thin ring draws itself around that phone's screen. One beat. The ring SNAPS RED, and every box on the counter flushes red at once, and a red wipe sweeps right-to-left back across the counter — and the merchant's hand physically drags the three items back toward himself, out of frame. No text on screen beyond the rupee numbers. No UI chrome. A grandmother says: 'the shop took the stuff back because the payment was fake.' Cut immediately to the same shot done again with a real payment — ring goes green, floating ₹205 dissolves, goods stay. Repeat-rack: real, fake, real, fake, four times in twelve seconds proves it is a capability and not a lucky take.
why_it_looks_impossible: Three separate things that each individually read as impossible are stacked in one continuous handheld-free take: (1) a price appears on an object the same FRAME it moves, with no button press, no scan beep, no barcode; (2) the rupee total is lying flat ON the counter in correct perspective and stays glued to the laminate as the camera drifts — it looks like the counter is a screen; (3) the verdict lands on a SECOND physical phone held inside the same frame, so the causal chain crosses a physical gap between two real objects, which no single screen recording can fake. And it is retail, so every viewer instantly knows what a wrong answer costs.
problem: Fake UPI 'Payment Successful' screens are an industrialised, YouTube-distributed crime against Indian merchants. A Kashmir field study of 102 merchants (July 2026) found 57.8% — 59 of them — had lost money to fraudulent digital transactions, and 9.8% admitted they rely ONLY on what the customer's phone shows. A Gurugram man lived in a DLF Phase 5 service apartment for five months on 16 fake PhonePe confirmations worth ₹6.17 lakh; a Pune mobile store lost a ₹1.35 lakh phone to a customer who said 'wait 10 minutes' and walked out. The incumbent fix is the soundbox: Paytm 6.8M devices + PhonePe 2.2M against roughly 6.5 crore merchants — 10-14% coverage, and a soundbox catches a swapped QR only by SILENCE, which nobody notices at a busy counter. The other 86% have zero independent confirmation and a phone already in their hand.
how_it_works: TWO LOOPS AT DIFFERENT RATES (the Apple FastVLM pattern). FAST LOOP, 30-57 fps, drives every pixel the viewer sees: YOLO26n ONNX — I measured 17.6 ms median / 18.8 ms p90 = 57 fps on CPUExecutionProvider on an M3 Pro at 640×640 fp32, and Ultralytics publishes 3.2 ms with the ANE on an iPhone 17 Pro (INT8) vs 9.2 ms CPU-only — fine-tuned to a single generic class 'counter item'. SKU IDENTITY is a few-shot embedding gallery, not a trained detector: the merchant photographs each SKU once from three angles at enrollment, SigLIP embeddings go into a local index, and each detected crop is a nearest-neighbour lookup with an explicit reject margin. Unknown → amber dashed box, excluded from the total. GEOMETRY is pure OpenCV.js: a printed ArUco tile taped to the counter gives findHomography/solvePnP a rock-solid plane, so the floating rupee glyphs are projected through the homography and painted in perspective (the atomic14 trick — project the cell centre through H and draw text, never warp pixels). SELL EVENT is a deterministic directional line-crossing test on the tracked centroid, supervision-style zone logic — an item counts only when it crosses the counter's sell-line toward the customer, and dragging it back decrements. MONEY OUT: one tap creates a genuine Razorpay QR (type upi_qr, usage single_use, fixed_amount true, payment_amount in paise, close_by set) via the official razorpay-mcp-server, and the QR image is rendered pinned to the counter plane through the same homography. MONEY IN: the qr_code.credited webhook flushes the boxes green inside the live frame. SCREENSHOT PATH (Track 02 sub-loop): when a phone screen is detected in frame, PP-OCRv5 mobile (det 4.7 MB, 28-58 ms CPU; rec 16 MB, 5-21 ms CPU — so ~35-80 ms end-to-end, genuine live-camera territory) reads UTR/RRN and amount off the screen, and the verdict is an exact lookup against the Razorpay Payments list. SESSION CLOSE: a 50+ event batch is reconciled — items sold vs payments credited — emitting a match rate and a categorised exception list.
features: Same-frame snap: a price box lands on an item the frame it crosses the sell-line, no scan, no beep, no barcode — YOLO26n at a measured 57 fps CPU / 3.2 ms on iPhone ANE

60-second merchant enrollment: photograph each SKU once from three angles, SigLIP embedding gallery built on-device, no labelling, no training, no dataset — and it generalises to a judge's own desk objects, which kills the 'hardcoded demo' suspicion
Floating rupee total painted flat on the counter in true perspective via ArUco + OpenCV.js findHomography, holding as the camera drifts
Deterministic directional sell-line: an item counts only crossing toward the customer; pull it back and the total decrements — geometry, not a model
AR QR mint: a real Razorpay upi_qr with fixed_amount and payment_amount in paise, rendered pinned to the counter surface with the exact detected total already inside it
qr_code.credited webhook flushes every box on the physical counter green inside the same live shot — money arriving becomes an event on real objects
Screenshot verification path: PP-OCRv5 mobile reads UTR/RRN/amount off the customer's phone screen inside the frame (~35-80 ms), then an exact Razorpay Payments lookup decides
Red retrieval sweep: on a failed verify, all boxes go red and a wipe runs back across the counter — the goods-return prompt, expressed physically
Duplicate-screen memory: perceptual hash + UTR ledger, so the same success screen shown twice at one counter surfaces a ghost of the earlier frame and 'seen 4 minutes ago'
LOW CONFIDENCE — HOLDING state: boxes go dashed amber, the overlay freezes at the last good pose with a closing confidence ring, and no money action is permitted until the scene steadies
Expiry stopping rule that handles a real Razorpay edge case: qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry, so a local timer plus an explicit close call greys the QR out and closes the loop visibly

Append-only signed audit event per money action — amount, the rule that permitted it, and the rule that would have stopped it; optional ₹200 thermal printer makes the audit trail a strip of paper on the floor
End-of-session reconciliation over a 50+ event batch: match rate plus a categorised exception list (unknown SKU, goods with no payment, payment with no goods, amount mismatch, duplicate UTR)
Offline degradation: detection is 100% on-device, so if the network drops the QR path disables itself and the UI says 'cash only' rather than guessing
ai_judgment: AI IS USED FOR: object detection and tracking (YOLO26n), few-shot SKU identity (SigLIP embeddings), and reading characters off a phone screen (PP-OCRv5 mobile). All three are pure perception tasks where models genuinely beat hand-written code. DETERMINISTIC INSTEAD, DELIBERATELY: (1) The payment verdict. No classifier ever decides whether money arrived. The UTR is extracted by OCR and then looked up in the Razorpay ledger — a string comparison. (2) NO PIXEL FORENSICS ON THE SCREENSHOT, and this is the component we built and then DELETED. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026) forged numeric fields in 4,061 real receipts with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Ideogram v2 Edit: TruFor fell from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 in-distribution to 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge scored 0.509 — literal chance. We can say on camera: 'we benchmarked the forgery detectors against 2026 diffusion inpainting, they score at coin-flip, so we removed that component and replaced it with a ledger lookup.' (3) The sell event is a line-crossing test on a tracked centroid, not a learned 'is this a sale' model — because a merchant must be able to argue with it, and you cannot argue with a logit. (4) The total is exact integer paise arithmetic; no language model is ever asked to add up money. (5) We also measured and rejected the CoreML execution provider: 21.9 ms vs 17.6 ms on plain CPU on this M3 Pro, a 25% regression caused by unbounded/dynamic dimensions falling off the Neural Engine — so we shipped CPU EP on laptop and ANE only on iPhone where we verified it wins.
razorpay_fit: Track 04 asks to close one finance-ops loop across a 50+ record batch of synthetic data and report match rate plus an honest exception list — NAZAR closes the oldest loop in Indian retail, physical stock-out versus cash-in, over a 60-event counter session. Razorpay surface used, all test mode: QR Codes API (create with type upi_qr / usage / fixed_amount / payment_amount in paise / close_by / notes, fetch, close, retrieve payments), the qr_code.created / qr_code.credited webhooks, the Payments list for UTR lookup, Refunds for the correction path, and the official razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (230 stars) so the agent's money tools are Razorpay's own published tool surface rather than raw HTTP I wrote myself. QR Codes and Payments are the two most camera-native primitives Razorpay ships: one is a physical object you point a phone at, the other is the single source of truth about whether money moved.
measurable: Three numbers on a held-out counter session never used for tuning. (1) ITEM PERCEPTION: precision and recall of the sell-line crossing event across 60+ item movements including deliberate adversarial cases — items dragged back, two items moved together, a hand occluding an item mid-crossing. (2) RECONCILIATION MATCH RATE: percentage of the 60-event batch automatically matched to a Razorpay payment, with every unmatched row itemised by exception class, and the explicit statement of how many rupees sit in the exception bucket.
