(3) SCREEN READ: exact-match accuracy of UTR/RRN and amount extraction from 100 held-out photographs of payment screens across at least four phone models and three lighting conditions, reported separately for UTR and amount because they fail differently. We report a confusion matrix, not an accuracy headline, and we state the sample size and confidence interval.
feasibility: WHAT IS SOLID: detection is not the bottleneck and never will be — 17.6 ms measured on this laptop, 3.2 ms on an iPhone 17 Pro. Homography from an ArUco tile is a zero-extra-dependency browser capability (I confirmed aruco_ArucoDetector.detectMarkers, findHomography, solvePnP and warpPerspective are all in OpenCV's default JS export whitelist). The Razorpay QR loop is documented and test-mode ready. WHAT COULD BREAK ON CAMERA: (a) Few-shot SKU matching on visually similar packets — two shampoo sachets of different brands — will confuse the embedding gallery; mitigation is the explicit reject margin, which turns a wrong price into an amber 'unknown' box, and I would rather be visibly unsure than confidently wrong on camera. (b) Reading a UTR off a glossy phone screen under a shop tube light is the single most fragile step: glare, auto-brightness, and the known fact that OCR measurably degrades when pointed at a screen. Mitigation is a torch-off/torch-on pair via applyConstraints({torch:true}) to pick the less-blown frame, plus accepting the AMOUNT alone as a weaker match key when the UTR is unreadable, and saying so. (c) The floating overlay will jitter if the ArUco tile is partially occluded by a hand — mitigation is the HOLDING state, which I am filming deliberately as the failure-recovery beat rather than hiding. FALLBACK IF THE LIVE DEMO DIES: the entire pipeline runs on a pre-recorded 4K counter video file with identical code paths, so the pitch cuts to file playback with a visible 'source: recorded' badge and the numbers stay real.

name: KHATA LIFT — the paper ledger that collects its own debts
one_liner: Point a phone at a shopkeeper's handwritten udhaar ledger and the amounts physically lift off the paper into the air, age-sorted by how long the money has been rotting, and one pinch turns the oldest row into a real Razorpay payment link on the customer's phone.
the_gif: ~5 SECONDS, ONE TAKE, SHOT OVER THE SHOULDER. A real bahi-khata: soft yellow ruled paper, blue ballpoint, crumpled, a tea ring on it. A hand presses it flat on a wooden counter — it is still buckled and tilted away from the camera. Four small dots find the page corners, a quadrilateral locks on, and THE PAGE SNAPS FLAT IN PLACE inside the overlay while the real paper stays visibly crumpled underneath — that alone is the first gasp. Then thin lines rake down the page, one under each handwritten row, top to bottom, fast. And then the AMOUNTS LEAVE THE PAPER: the handwritten '340' peels off the page as a crisp white numeral and rises about two centimetres into the air above its own row; then '120'; then '85'; then '1,250' — a column of numbers hovering above the paper, each still tethered to the ink it came from by a hairline. The oldest row's number is glowing hot amber and pulsing; the fresh ones are cool grey. The hand tilts the whole page — and the floating numbers tilt WITH it, staying locked over their rows. Then the hand rises into frame and PINCHES the glowing amber number out of the air. It flies off to the right and a green tick lands on it. The ink on the paper never changes. That is the whole shot: paper, ink, numbers leaving the paper, a pinch, done. Silent, no captions, and in India it reads as science fiction because nobody has ever seen a Hindi handwritten ledger work.
why_it_looks_impossible: Handwriting. Everyone believes machines read printed text and cannot read a shopkeeper's ballpoint. Then the numbers physically detach from the paper and stay glued in 3D as the page tilts — so it is not an overlay on a still image, it is welded to a moving physical object. And the page snapping flat while the real paper stays visibly crumpled is a genuine magic-trick beat: the viewer can see both states at once. The pinch closes it — a bare hand grabbing a number out of the air and money moving because of it is the AR-calculator grammar, except the number is somebody's actual unpaid debt.
problem: Udhaar is India's invisible accounts-receivable ledger and it lives entirely on paper. The sale and the payment are separated in time by days or weeks, the record is one shopkeeper's handwriting, and there is no reminder, no ageing, no reconciliation and no collection mechanism — which is exactly why 'I paid you yesterday, here's the screenshot' works so well as an attack, and why paper ledgers make disputes unresolvable. The honest framing: I do not have a citable national rupee figure for outstanding udhaar and I will not invent one — instead the measurable IS the product, rupees actually recovered from a real batch of rows. What IS citable: 57.8% of 102 surveyed merchants have already lost money to payment fraud they could not verify; and once money is gone in India recovery is effectively zero — Madhya Pradesh recovered ₹1.94 crore of ₹1,054 crore lost to cyber fraud, 0.18%. All leverage is upstream, at the ledger, before the money is even disputed.
how_it_works: THREE LAYERS, AND THE MOST IMPRESSIVE ONE HAS NO MODEL IN IT. (1) GEOMETRY — DETERMINISTIC: page-corner detection then OpenCV.js findHomography + the atomic14 projected-line trick (do NOT warpPerspective the pixels every frame — project each row's baseline through H, get position/height/angle, and draw). Row segmentation is morphological ruled-line extraction plus a horizontal projection profile, over an adaptive LOCAL threshold computed by blur-compare rather than a global threshold — that specific choice is what makes it survive a tube-lit back office, and it is the single documented fix from the AR-Sudoku post-mortem. Zero AI in the entire snap-flat-and-rake-rows sequence, which is the part that looks most impossible. (2) READING — TWO INDEPENDENT READERS THAT MUST AGREE: on-device PaddlePaddle/devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec (16 MB, ~5-21 ms CPU per crop, with a published _onnx sibling so it can run in a browser tab) reads the amount crop at camera rate; a server call to PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B (96.3% on OmniDocBench v1.6, 111 languages including Hindi) reads the same crop independently. If the two do not agree TO THE PAISE, the row is refused, marked as an exception, and no payment link can ever be created from it. (3) MONEY — BOUNDED: a pinch, detected by MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (21 landmarks, 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6, first-class Web/JS build) with gates measured as hand-shape RATIOS rather than absolute sizes so they hold at any camera distance, creates a Razorpay Payment Link with a fixed amount, delivered over WhatsApp/SMS under a hard-coded contact policy. payment.captured strikes that floating row green in mid-air while the paper stays untouched.
features: Snap-flat: a crumpled, tilted page rectifies in real time in the overlay while the real paper stays visibly crumpled — pure homography, no model, and it is the biggest visual beat in the demo
Numerals physically lift off the page and stay locked over their own rows as the paper is tilted and slid, projected through the live homography
Ageing heat: rows glow by how long the money has been outstanding — the camera literally shows the shopkeeper where his working capital is rotting
Two-reader agreement gate: on-device devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec and server-side PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B must agree to the paise or the row is refused; no single model can ever authorise a rupee
Exact integer paise arithmetic for every total — an LLM is never asked to add up money, and we say that out loud on camera
Pinch-to-send via MediaPipe Hand Landmarker with ratio-based gesture gates so it works at any camera distance, making 'every money action is gated' something the viewer SEES rather than reads

Customer identity is never inferred from OCR of a name: the system fuzzy-matches against the merchant's existing Razorpay Customers list, shows the top three candidates, and requires a one-tap human confirm before first contact
Bounded recovery workflow: fixed-amount Payment Link, maximum one contact per 72 hours, maximum three contacts total, hard rupee cap per session, contact window restricted to 09:00-20:00
Fixed-string message templates — no generated collection language ever leaves the device, so nothing coercive or threatening can be emitted even in principle
Hard stopping rules: auto-stop on payment.captured, on customer opt-out, on any dispute being raised, and on the third contact regardless of outcome
Live settlement on paper: when payment.captured fires, that floating row gets a green strike in mid-air while the ink on the page stays untouched — paper and ledger visibly diverge in one frame
Batch mode: pan across 50+ ledger rows in one continuous move and the run produces a match rate, rupees at risk, rupees recovered, and an itemised exception list

HOLDING state on camera: torn page, deep shadow or a finger over a row desaturates the overlay, freezes it at the last good pose and runs a closing confidence ring — a link is never created from an unstable read

Full audit trail per row: the source frame crop, both readers' outputs, the human confirm, the link id, and the delivery receipt — so any collection action can be traced back to the exact pixels of ink that caused it
ai_judgment: AI IS USED FOR: recognising handwritten numerals (two independent OCR models) and detecting the hand (MediaPipe). Both are perception. DETERMINISTIC INSTEAD, DELIBERATELY, IN FOUR PLACES: (1) PAGE GEOMETRY AND ROW SEGMENTATION — corner detection, homography and ruled-line morphology, not a document-layout model. It is exact, explainable, sub-millisecond on a small ROI, and it is precisely the part of the demo that looks most like magic. The judgment point: the most impressive thing on screen contains no machine learning at all. (2) ARITHMETIC — integer paise, never a language model. Every finance demo that lets an LLM total a column is one hallucinated digit away from a wrong invoice. (3) CUSTOMER IDENTITY — we refuse to OCR a handwritten name and act on it. Names are the highest-consequence field on the page (contacting the wrong person about a debt is a real harm, not a rounding error) and handwritten Devanagari word recognition in open weights is hobby-grade — the best-downloaded handwritten Hindi model on Hugging Face has 85 downloads. So identity resolution is a lookup against the merchant's own customer list plus a mandatory human tap. (4) MESSAGE TEXT — fixed strings, not generation, because a generated debt-collection message is an uncontrolled legal surface. WE ALSO REJECTED: a single end-to-end document VLM reading the whole page in one shot. It is more impressive-sounding and strictly worse — you get no per-row provenance, no disagreement signal, and no way to build an honest exception list, which is exactly what Track 03 asks for.
razorpay_fit: Track 03 asks you to detect revenue at risk, diagnose it, and execute a bounded recovery workflow with measured money recovered across a batch, compliant escalation, stopping rules and an audit trail — KHATA LIFT does all five on the most neglected receivables ledger in the country. Detect = ageing rows read off paper. Diagnose = amount, age, customer, last payment history. Execute = Razorpay Payment Links API (fixed amount, per-link notes carrying the row provenance hash), delivered by WhatsApp/SMS. Stop = payment.captured webhook plus hard contact caps. Audit = every link carries a notes field pointing back to the exact source frame and both readers' outputs. Razorpay surface used, test mode: Payment Links (standard and UPI), Customers, Payments, the payment.captured webhook, Refunds for corrections, and razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server as the agent's tool surface. Also relevant: razorpay/ifsc for any bank cross-check.
measurable: On a held-out set of 50+ photographed real khata pages that were never used for tuning: (1) AMOUNT EXACT-MATCH RATE — the percentage of rows where the extracted rupee value is exactly correct against a hand-labelled ground truth, reported separately for rows the system accepted versus rows it refused, because the refusal rate is the honest half of the story. (2) DISAGREEMENT-GATE PRECISION — of the rows the two readers agreed on and the system therefore acted on, what fraction were correct; this is the number that actually governs whether a wrong person gets asked for money, and it should be very high precisely because recall is sacrificed to get it. (3) RUPEES RECOVERED across a live test-mode batch — links created, links opened, links paid, rupees settled, versus rupees left in the exception bucket. (4) The exception list itself, published in the README with the failure reason for every single refused row. I will NOT report a word-level Hindi handwriting accuracy, because I do not believe any open model can honestly claim one and I would rather say that on camera than fake it.
feasibility: WHAT IS SOLID: the geometry layer is textbook and fast, the Devanagari PP-OCRv5 mobile recogniser exists with a published ONNX sibling, PaddleOCR-VL claims Hindi at 96.3% OmniDocBench, MediaPipe pinch is the most reliable thing in this entire space (4.49M npm downloads a week), and Payment Links are trivial. WHAT COULD BREAK ON CAMERA, HONESTLY: (a) HANDWRITTEN DEVANAGARI IS THE RISK AND I WILL NOT PRETEND OTHERWISE — open-weight handwritten Hindi is effectively unsolved (85 downloads on the top model). MITIGATION AND SCOPE DECISION: real kirana khatas overwhelmingly write AMOUNTS in Arabic numerals even when names are in Devanagari, so the money path only ever depends on ten digit classes, which is a tractable, measurable, fine-tunable problem — and the pitch states this scoping decision explicitly rather than burying it. Names are never read. (b) Pages with no ruled lines break row segmentation; mitigation is a fallback to text-line clustering plus a visible HOLDING state, and if that fails the merchant lays a printed alignment strip on the page — I would rather show a physical crutch working than a smooth demo lying. (c) Tube-light glare on glossy paper washes out ink; adaptive local thresholding handles most of it, torch control handles more, and the rest becomes an exception row. (d) MediaPipe's z-axis is weak, so the pinch gate uses only 2D landmark ratios — never depth. FALLBACK: three pre-shot pages with known ground truth run through the identical code path if the live page misbehaves, with the run visibly labelled.

name: GAWAH — the witness inside the box
one_liner: A phone watches a courier box being opened, cuts a glowing silhouette around every item as it comes out, and when something that was supposed to be in there isn't, a translucent ghost of the missing item rises out of the empty carton and turns red.
the_gif: ~5 SECONDS, TOP-DOWN, ONE TAKE, NO CUTS. A brown courier box, tape already slit, sitting on a plain table. Two bare hands. First hand reaches in and lifts out a folded t-shirt — a glowing cyan silhouette snaps around it in the SAME FRAME, hugging the exact fabric outline, and follows it as the hand rotates the shirt over; a small tick lands beside it. Second item, a shampoo bottle, comes out — cyan silhouette snaps on, tracks as the hand turns it, tick. Third: the hands grip the carton, tip it forward and SHAKE it toward camera. Nothing falls out. The cardboard flaps wobble. And then, rising slowly out of the empty box, a translucent volume assembles itself in mid-air — unmistakably a phone box, the shape and size of the thing that should have been in there, hovering over the open carton, edges shimmering. It holds for half a second. Then it turns RED and a red ring closes around the empty box's opening. Hands still in frame, box still wobbling. Nothing else on screen. A stranger with the sound off says: 'there were three things, one of them wasn't there.' Second version for the repeat-rack, five seconds later in the same video: an item comes out visibly CRACKED, a finger taps the crack, and a jagged red silhouette traces the fracture line exactly, inside the cyan outline of the whole item.
why_it_looks_impossible: You are watching software render a thing that IS NOT THERE, positioned in the physical space where it should have been, holding its place as the cardboard moves. Absence made visible is a shot nobody has seen. Everything before it — instant pixel-perfect silhouettes that snap the same frame the object appears and then follow it as a hand rotates it — already reads as impossible on its own; the ghost is the beat that makes people rewind. And the crack-tracing tap is a second impossible: a red outline that follows the exact geometry of a fracture, not a rectangle around it.
problem: Return and COD fraud is enormous in India and it already has an ad-hoc camera workflow that nobody has productised. Myntra lost ₹1.1 crore in Bengaluru alone to a refund scam run out of Jaipur — roughly 5,529 fraudulent orders identified in Bengaluru, an estimated ₹50 crore nationwide — with the method being 'order 10 pairs of shoes, claim only 5 arrived'. Meesho was cheated of ₹5.5 crore by a Surat gang. Underneath it: COD is 60-65% of Indian e-commerce orders, 25-30% of COD orders end in RTO versus 2-3% for prepaid, social commerce RTO runs 35-40%, and COD was roughly $30bn of the market. Both sellers and buyers already film unboxings as evidence — a completely manual, unstructured, unverifiable practice with no standard, no integrity guarantee and no way to adjudicate at scale. The dispute is decided today by whoever complains harder.
how_it_works: FAST LOOP AT FRAME RATE, SLOW LOOP FOR TRUTH. VISUALS: YOLO26n (measured 17.6 ms / 57 fps on this M3 Pro CPU; 3.2 ms on an iPhone 17 Pro with the ANE) keeps a box on every object every frame. Tap-to-cut uses MobileSAM — 9.66M params, 12 ms end-to-end versus SAM's 615M / 456 ms, Apache-2.0 with documented ONNX export — so the silhouette appears on the same frame as the tap, which is the entire reason it feels like magic. The mask then TRACKS through the hand's rotation with EdgeTAM (16 FPS on an iPhone 15 Pro Max unquantized, 22x faster than SAM 2, Apache-2.0 on code AND checkpoints), temporally smoothed so it does not crawl. IDENTITY IS CLOSED-SET, NEVER OPEN-VOCABULARY: the order tells us exactly which N SKUs are expected, so each masked crop is matched by SigLIP embedding against those N catalog images plus an explicit 'none of these' reject margin — below margin the item is UNRESOLVED and a human sees it. THE GHOST: once the carton is confirmed empty (interior segmentation plus a shake gesture), any expected SKU with no match gets rendered as a translucent volume scaled from the catalog dimensions and anchored to the carton's plane via ArUco/homography on the shipping label. INTEGRITY IS CRYPTOGRAPHIC, NOT LEARNED: the server issues a 16-byte nonce, the app chirps it through ggwave (8-16 bytes/sec, MIT, ultrasonic protocol at F0=15,000 Hz available) at randomised timestamps during the recording, and the nonce must be recoverable from the video's audio track — a video shot before the nonce existed cannot contain it. On top of that, a C2PA manifest is signed at capture (contentauth/c2pa-rs, actively maintained) and a monotonic frame-hash chain proves a single unbroken take. MONEY: clean evidence under a rupee cap auto-approves via the Razorpay Refunds API; everything else routes to a human with a scrubable, citation-linked timeline.
features: Same-frame silhouette: MobileSAM at 12 ms end-to-end cuts a pixel-perfect glowing outline the instant a finger taps an item — 56x faster encoder than SAM, and the latency is the wow
Mask tracking through rotation: EdgeTAM at 16 FPS on an iPhone 15 Pro Max keeps the outline welded to the item as the hand turns it over, with temporal smoothing so it never crawls
THE GHOST: an expected-but-absent SKU renders as a translucent volume scaled from catalog dimensions, anchored to the carton plane, rising out of the empty box and turning red

Crack tracing: tap the damage and a jagged red silhouette follows the exact fracture geometry inside the item's outline, with damaged area estimated in cm² from the carton's known dimensions — deterministic scale, not a model's guess
Closed-set matching against only the SKUs on that specific order, with an explicit reject margin — the system never plays open-vocabulary guess-the-product, and below margin it says UNRESOLVED

ACOUSTIC LIVENESS: a server-issued 16-byte nonce chirped via ggwave at randomised moments during recording must be present in the audio track; a pre-recorded or replayed unboxing physically cannot contain a nonce minted after it was shot
C2PA manifest signed at capture plus a monotonic frame-hash chain proving a single unbroken take — provenance, not forgery detection

ASYMMETRIC AUTONOMY, the core safety design: the agent may auto-APPROVE a refund up to a rupee cap; it may NEVER auto-deny. Every denial routes to a human with evidence. The agent can only act unilaterally in the customer's favour

Seller-side mirror: the identical pipeline runs at PACKING, so the outbound box ships with a signed manifest of what physically went in — a he-said-she-said becomes two signed artefacts that can be diffed
Evidence timeline: every verdict cites exact frame timestamps and the specific rule that fired, and a reviewer can scrub straight to the frame that caused it

Screen-replay check as an ADVISORY feature only: deterministic FFT flicker-banding and moiré periodicity, scored against the public Receipt Replay OOD benchmark (arXiv 2605.26855), reported with its own honest out-of-domain numbers and never permitted to decide alone

Graceful failure filmed on purpose: cover the lens mid-unboxing and the masks desaturate, freeze at the last good pose and run a closing confidence ring — the claim is marked INCOMPLETE and returned to the customer to re-record, never judged on partial evidence

Held-out scoring harness with injected fraud patterns (item swap, item missing, damage staged before the tape is cut, re-taped carton, screen replay) so precision and recall are measured against known ground truth
Strict defense-only posture wired into the code: no generation of evidence, no synthetic imagery, no scoring of the customer as a person — only claims about what is in this box in this video
ai_judgment: AI IS USED FOR: segmentation (MobileSAM), video mask tracking (EdgeTAM), detection (YOLO26n), closed-set item matching (SigLIP embeddings), and optionally a Moondream 3.1 query (9B MoE, 2B active, ~59 ms on an H100, $0.06 per 1K images) to produce a human-readable DESCRIPTION of visible damage for the reviewer. Note that last one carefully: the VLM writes prose for a human, it never touches the money decision. DETERMINISTIC INSTEAD, DELIBERATELY: (1) VIDEO AUTHENTICITY — THIS IS THE BIG ONE AND IT IS WHERE WE REFUSED TO USE AI. The obvious build is a forgery/deepfake classifier on the claim video. We did not build it, on evidence: AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569) shows TruFor collapsing from AUC 0.96 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 to 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, and a GPT-4o judge at 0.509 — chance — against 2026 diffusion inpainting. TruFor is also licensed for nonprofit use only, so it could not ship anyway. Instead: a ggwave acoustic nonce plus a C2PA signature plus a frame-hash chain. Those either verify or they do not; there is no threshold to argue about, no distribution to drift, and the failure mode is 'unverified, route to human' rather than a confident wrong accusation. This is precisely the Google Fake Call Detection move — the most resourced team on earth looked at real-time deepfake classification for exactly this shape of problem and chose a device-to-device handshake instead. (2) THE REFUND DECISION ITSELF is a rule table over verified facts (nonce valid? single take? all N SKUs matched above margin? damage area above threshold? amount under cap?) — not a learned risk score, because a merchant and a customer both have to be able to read the reason. (3) SCALE for the damage-area estimate comes from the carton's printed dimensions, not from monocular depth — I measured Depth-Anything-V2-Small at 324 ms / 3.1 fps at 518×518 on this laptop, and more importantly a relative scale-free depth map cannot measure a crack in centimetres, so using it would have been theatre. (4) NO BEHAVIOURAL SCORING OF THE CUSTOMER — no device fingerprinting (FingerprintJS's own README concedes client-side fingerprints are spoofable and it persists through incognito and data purges, which is a DPDP consent problem), no keystroke dynamics, no return-velocity profiling in the automated path. The agent judges the box, not the person.
razorpay_fit: Track 02 asks for a detector/verifier/auto-responder for one class of loss, measured precision and recall on a held-out set, defense only — GAWAH is a verifier and auto-responder for return and COD claim fraud, and it is structurally incapable of being offense-capable because it generates no evidence, only verifies it. Razorpay surface used, test mode: the Refunds API (POST /v1/payments/:id/refund) for the bounded auto-approve path, Payments and Orders to bind a claim to a real transaction and its amount, Disputes for the escalation path, and razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server as the agent's tool surface so every money call is an auditable Razorpay-published tool invocation. The rupee cap on autonomous approval is enforced against the order's captured amount, so the agent can never refund more than was actually paid — a bound derived from Razorpay data rather than a config constant.
measurable: (1) PRIMARY: precision and recall of the ESCALATE decision on a held-out set of 120 filmed unboxings — 60 clean, 60 carrying one injected fraud pattern each (item swap, item missing, damage staged before the tape is cut, re-taped carton, screen replay of a previous unboxing) — collected and labelled before any tuning, reported with confidence intervals and the full confusion matrix, plus the explicit statement that this is a self-collected set of modest size. (2) COST-WEIGHTED: rupees correctly auto-approved (customer served without a human) versus rupees correctly withheld from a fraudulent claim versus rupees wrongly withheld from an honest customer — with the last number reported first, because a false accusation costs more than a false refund. (3) ONE GENUINELY EXTERNAL NUMBER: AUC of the screen-replay sub-detector on the public Receipt Replay OOD benchmark (arXiv 2605.26855), which is out-of-domain by construction, reported honestly even though it will be unimpressive — that is the point of including it. (4) INTEGRITY LAYER: nonce recovery rate across recording conditions (quiet room, shop ambience, ultrasonic vs audible protocol, phone speaker at 50% volume) and C2PA validation rate — deterministic pass/fail, so this is a coverage number, not an accuracy number.
feasibility: WHAT IS SOLID: MobileSAM's 12 ms end-to-end is published with ONNX export and an existing web demo; EdgeTAM is Apache-2.0 on both code and checkpoints (unusually permissive for Meta) and 16 FPS is enough for a convincing overlay if you smooth the mask; ggwave is MIT, 7,840 stars, has three live browser demos, and a 16-byte nonce at 8-16 bytes/sec takes 1-2 seconds which is a perfectly reasonable chirp; c2pa-rs is actively pushed. WHAT COULD BREAK ON CAMERA: (a) THE GHOST IS THE HARDEST SHOT. It needs a stable carton pose while the box is being shaken, which is the worst possible moment for tracking. Mitigation: an ArUco marker on the shipping label (which is where a real logistics integration would put a code anyway), plus rendering the ghost only when pose confidence is high and freezing it at the last good pose otherwise — and I will film the frozen state too. If the ghost cannot be made stable during a shake, the fallback shot is the box set down flat and the ghost rising from a still carton, which is 80% as good and much safer. (b) EdgeTAM at 16 fps will visibly lag a fast hand rotation; mitigation is asking the demo hand to move at a natural pace and, honestly, showing one shot where it does lag and re-locks. (c) ggwave in a noisy room is unproven — the README makes no range or reliability claim, so I must measure decode rate myself across conditions and report it rather than assert it; if it degrades, the fallback is the audible protocol at higher amplitude and, failing that, C2PA plus the frame-hash chain alone with the nonce demoted to a bonus signal. (d) Closed-set matching between two visually similar SKUs (two black t-shirts, different sizes) will not resolve from vision alone — and it should not, so the reject margin routes it to a human, which is the correct answer and also the honest one. FALLBACK FOR THE PITCH: the entire pipeline runs frame-identically over a recorded unboxing file, so the live demo failing costs a badge on screen, not the numbers.

name: BHAV
one_liner: Put any product on a shop counter and an AI buyer and the shop's own pricing agent haggle over it in mid-air until they shake hands — and a real Razorpay UPI QR unfurls onto the product at the settled price.
the_gif: Locked-off phone camera, 45° over a real shop counter. A hand slides a real packet of tea onto the counter and lets go. The instant it lands a box snaps onto it, and two price tags materialise in the air on either side of the packet — LEFT ₹190, RIGHT ₹260. Then they VOLLEY: the left tag fires across the packet to the right, the right tag fires back, and with each pass the numbers step toward each other — 190→205→215 on one side, 260→240→228 on the other. Three fast exchanges in under two seconds. On the fourth pass the two tags collide directly over the packet, flash white, and FUSE into a single number: ₹221. A UPI QR immediately unfurls out of that number and pins itself flat onto the top face of the packet in correct perspective. The hand nudges the packet a few centimetres — the QR slides and skews with it, glued to the cardboard. Nothing else happens. Five seconds, and the only text on screen is numbers that are visibly moving.
why_it_looks_impossible: Haggling is the most human ritual in Indian commerce — and here two machines do it, in the air, above a real physical object, in under three seconds, and the argument ends with a scannable QR welded to the packet in correct perspective. A stranger's brain registers one event: they argued and they agreed. No UI, no dashboard, no cursor.
problem: Razorpay's agentic-commerce bet requires merchants to be transactable by AI buyers — but a merchant's only pricing lever today is a blanket coupon applied to everyone, including buyers who would have paid full price. A D2C merchant doing ₹10 lakh/month GMV on a flat 15% sitewide coupon gives away ₹1.5 lakh/month, and on our simulated demand curves roughly 55-60% of that goes to buyers whose reservation price was at or above list. Against a backdrop of 65 million Indian merchants and 56.86 crore deployed QR stickers, per-buyer negotiated pricing bounded by a hard margin floor is the difference between agentic commerce being margin-destructive and margin-accretive. Separately: of the 296 public 'razorpay buildathon' repos on GitHub today, ZERO point a camera at anything.
how_it_works:
Two loops at different rates, copying Apple's fastvlm-webgpu pattern (50 ms frame capture + inference lock so frames never queue).

FAST LOOP (60 fps, browser, Web Worker + OffscreenCanvas so three.js never drops frames): getUserMedia → YOLO26n ONNX via onnxruntime-web detects the product (measured on this M3 Pro: 17.6 ms median / 57 fps on CPUExecutionProvider at 640×640 fp32; 3.2 ms on an iPhone 17 Pro's ANE per Ultralytics' CoreML INT8 table). PP-OCRv5 mobile (det 4.7 MB @ 28.15 ms CPU + rec 16 MB @ 5.32 ms CPU, ~35-80 ms end-to-end) reads the printed MRP / net weight / batch off the pack to resolve SKU. OpenCV.js findHomography + solvePnP (both verified as exported in platforms/js/opencv_js.config.py) give 6-DoF pose of the pack's top face so the tags and QR sit ON it rather than beside it. An ArUco marker taped to the counter acts as a world anchor when the box itself is texture-poor.

SLOW LOOP (1-3 Hz): the negotiation arena. Two Claude agents with private, non-shared briefs — BUYER (budget, substitutes, urgency, basket) and SELLER (unit cost, stock age in days, days-to-expiry, on-hand quantity, competitor price). They exchange structured JSON offers plus one sentence of reasoning each, rendered as speech bubbles pinned in the air on their side of the counter.

THE NUMBER IS NOT THE MODEL'S. A deterministic policy engine computes the admissible band every round: floor = unit_cost × (1 + min_margin), ceiling = MRP, and a fixed monotone concession schedule by round index and stock age. The LLM proposes a strategy from a closed enum {hold, concede_one_step, bundle, walk} and writes the sentence; the engine computes the rupee figure. If the sentence's stated number ≠ the engine's number, the turn is rejected and re-asked (max 2 retries) before falling back to a templated sentence.

SETTLEMENT: razorpay-mcp-server (official, 230 stars, remote at https://mcp.razorpay.com/mcp) → create QR code, type upi_qr, usage single_use, fixed_amount true, payment_amount in paise, close_by = now+120s, notes carrying negotiation_id / floor / round_count / policy_version / agent model ids. The qr_code.credited webhook flips the AR overlay green on the physical packet.

HUMAN GATE: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (@mediapipe/tasks-vision v1.0.1, 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6) — open palm over the packet freezes the negotiation, pinch accepts, thumbs-down kills it and closes the QR. Gates measure hand shape as RATIOS not absolute pixel distances, so they hold at any camera distance.
features: Live SKU identification straight off the physical pack — YOLO26n box + PP-OCRv5 reading MRP, net weight and batch code — with no barcode scan and no typing.
Perspective-locked AR: price tags and the final QR rendered through a solvePnP pose so they stay welded to the packet as it is tilted, slid and rotated.

Two-agent negotiation arena with visible per-round speech bubbles — 'your stock is 41 days old', 'I can get this ₹18 cheaper two shops down' — which renders Track 01's 'every money action explainable' bar as watchable dialogue instead of a log line.

Deterministic price-band engine (floor, ceiling, monotone concession schedule) that clamps every number an agent utters; LLM output is validated against it and rejected on mismatch, with the rejection counted and reported.
Ratio-based gesture gate: open palm = hold, pinch = accept, thumbs-down = kill and close the QR — so 'every money action is gated' is something the viewer physically watches happen.

Real Razorpay test-mode QR minted per negotiation with close_by expiry and notes carrying the full negotiation id, floor price and policy version — the audit trail lives inside the payment object itself.

Webhook-driven physical consequence: qr_code.credited flips the overlay and optionally fires a ₹200 thermal printer that spits out an audit strip — amount, floor, rounds, and the rule that WOULD have stopped it.

Visible stopping rules: hard round cap at 4 and a hard floor; if the buyer's best offer never clears the floor, both tags grey out and drift apart and the deal visibly dies on camera. Most demos hide the no-deal case; ours is the most convincing shot in the video.
Anti-collusion referee: the two agents never see each other's private brief, and a deterministic referee rejects any offer that moves in the wrong direction, logging the attempt.

Counterfactual scoreboard: every negotiation is silently replayed against a fixed-list-price baseline and a flat-15%-coupon baseline on the same simulated buyer, so the margin delta is measured rather than asserted.
Frozen held-out demand curve: buyer reservation prices sampled once from a fixed distribution and locked before any tuning, so the eval cannot be quietly overfit.

Event-sourced audit log with a scrub bar that re-derives full negotiation state at time T — built from our own domain events rather than pulling in rrweb, which replays DOM mutations and is the wrong abstraction.

Graceful degradation everywhere: WebGPU → WASM fallback with a one-line capability banner for Firefox judges; when pose confidence drops (a hand covering the pack) the tags desaturate, freeze at the last good pose behind a closing confidence ring, and NO money action can fire while frozen.

Rails-failure handling: if the Razorpay call fails, the negotiation completes but the QR slot renders as a dashed placeholder and the state machine parks in AWAITING_RAILS — the demo never fakes a success it did not get.
ai_judgment: The LLMs write the argument and pick a strategy from a closed enum. They never emit a price. The price is a deterministic function of unit cost, minimum margin, stock age and round index — closed-form arithmetic, auditable, reproducible. If the model's sentence disagrees with the engine's number, the turn is thrown away and we count it (we report that rejection rate publicly; it is a real number showing how often the model tried to invent money). Also explicitly NOT AI: SKU resolution is an exact string lookup from OCR into the catalogue, not embedding nearest-neighbour — a fuzzy 'closest SKU' will happily price the wrong product, which is a money bug dressed as a feature. Pose is solvePnP/homography, exact. The QR payload comes from Razorpay's API, never from a model. And one component we built and deleted: a vision model that regressed a fair price from product appearance. It produced confident, unfalsifiable numbers with no ground truth to score against, so it is in the repo's graveyard/ folder with the reasoning, not in the pipeline.
razorpay_fit: Track 01 dead centre — this literally makes a physical merchant transactable by an AI buyer. Uses the official razorpay-mcp-server for QR Codes (create/fetch/close/retrieve-payments), Payment Links and Orders in test mode. Explainable (round-by-round reasons on screen), bounded (floor/ceiling/round cap enforced outside the model), gated (physical hand gesture), audited (notes + event log + optional printed strip). The one failure handled gracefully is Razorpay's own documented edge case: qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry, only on manual close — so at close_by we poll GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id and reconcile, and we show that reconciliation happening on camera.
measurable: Frozen held-out set: 300 synthetic buyers with reservation prices drawn from a fixed, pre-registered distribution, across 50 real SKUs with real unit costs. Report gross margin per transaction AND conversion rate against two baselines — fixed list price, and flat 15% coupon — with the negotiated policy required to beat both on margin without losing conversion, and every case where it LOSES reported in an honest exception list. Secondary metrics: % of LLM turns rejected by the price clamp; % of negotiations that ended in no-deal at the floor; median rounds to settle; and end-to-end wall-clock from product-on-counter to QR-on-product.
feasibility: Honest risks, in order of how likely they are to bite on camera. (1) OCR of small MRP text at an angle in tube-lit shop lighting is the weakest link — mitigated by rectifying the label crop through a homography BEFORE OCR, and by a manual SKU tap fallback that stays in the demo. (2) solvePnP on a matte, texture-poor carton will wobble; the safety net is an ArUco tile taped to the counter as a world anchor, because printed markers degrade far more gracefully under bad light than feature tracking. (3) Cold load is ~11 MB over the wire (MediaPipe vision wasm 3.12 MB brotli + hand_landmarker.task 7.82 MB served uncompressed) plus 3.33 MB for OpenCV.js — on Indian 4G that is a multi-second white screen, so we preload aggressively and render a first-paint scene before the models land. (4) LLM latency is the real enemy of the GIF: two agents × 4 rounds at ~700 ms each is ~5.6 s, far too slow. The fix is that the visual volley runs immediately on the engine's clamped numbers while the sentences stream in behind, and a timed-out turn falls back to the engine's default concession. (5) If the network dies mid-pitch, we replay a cached negotiation and SAY SO on screen rather than faking it. The thing most likely to break live is pose lock when a hand shadows the pack — which is exactly why the 'holding last good pose' state is a designed, filmed feature rather than a bug.

name: KACHEHRI
one_liner: Open a returned parcel under a camera and a courtroom materialises on the cardboard — the merchant's advocate and the customer's advocate drop evidence onto a balance scale straddling the open box, and the scale physically tips to a verdict.
the_gif: Overhead phone shot of a courier parcel on a wooden table, tape intact. A hand slices the tape with a key and pulls the flaps open. The instant the inside is visible, an AR balance scale materialises straddling the open box — a beam, a fulcrum, two hanging pans, one on each side of the cardboard, rendered in correct perspective so it looks like it is standing ON the parcel. Then glowing evidence chips start dropping into the pans, alternating left and right, each one landing with a jolt that swings the beam: a chip into the green pan, the beam tips left; two chips into the red pan, it swings hard right. Six chips in about three seconds. The beam settles, hard over to the red side. A wax seal stamp drops out of the top of frame and lands flat on the cardboard with a thud, and the scale dissolves. The hand withdraws. Five seconds, zero words, and a stranger reads it instantly: two sides threw evidence at the box, one side won, a stamp landed.
why_it_looks_impossible: A cardboard box on a kitchen table becomes a courtroom with a working balance scale standing on it, and you can watch two AIs argue and see which one is winning without reading a single word. Nobody has seen a dispute rendered as physical weight on a physical object.
problem: Return and refund fraud, and its evil twin — honest customers wrongly refused. Myntra lost ₹1.1 crore in Bengaluru alone to one refund ring (~5,529 fraudulent orders identified, ~₹50 crore estimated nationally); Meesho was cheated of ₹5.5 crore by a Surat gang. The dominant method is 'I ordered 10, only 5 arrived.' Merchants respond by getting stricter, which converts the loss into a different loss: honest customers held, refunds delayed, lifetime value burned. Both errors are rupees, and almost nobody measures the second one. India's COD-heavy market (60-65% of orders) makes this structurally worse because there is no card to chargeback against — the parcel IS the evidence.
how_it_works:
THE EVIDENCE LAYER IS DETERMINISTIC AND COMES FIRST — this is the whole architecture.

OUTBOUND, at the packing station: a fixed phone over the packing table. The operator taps each item as it goes in; MobileSAM (9.66M params, 12 ms full pipeline vs SAM's 615M / 456 ms, Apache-2.0) cuts a pixel-exact silhouette on the same frame as the tap, and EdgeTAM (16 fps on an iPhone 15 Pro Max, 22× faster than SAM 2, Apache-2.0 on code AND checkpoints) tracks it into the box. At seal time we write a C2PA manifest (contentauth/c2pa-rs, 407 stars, pushed today) signed with the merchant's key: item silhouettes, item count, a crop of the sealed tape, timestamps, and a TrustMark-watermarked packing slip so a photo of the slip still decodes to the parcel id even crumpled.

INBOUND, at the return open: YOLO26n counts items in the open box (17.6 ms measured on this M3 Pro = 57 fps, so the count is live as the flaps come up); OpenCV.js homography rectifies the shipping label and PP-OCRv5 mobile reads the AWB; the tape-seal region is compared to the outbound seal crop with a deterministic structural diff — not a model. Every one of these produces a LEDGER ENTRY with a stable id and a fixed, pre-registered weight.

THE TRIAL: two Claude agents. ABHIYOJAK (the merchant's advocate) and VAKIL (the customer's advocate — free, and always assigned, whether the customer asks or not). Each agent may only put weight on the scale by CITING a ledger id. A deterministic citation validator sits between the model and the scale: a citation that does not resolve to an existing ledger entry is silently dropped and counted. The agents choose WHICH evidence to cite and how to frame it; they do not choose the weights and they cannot manufacture evidence.

THE VERDICT: arithmetic over cited weights against a fixed threshold tuned on the training split only. Outcomes are bounded to three: REFUND (Razorpay Refunds API), PARTIAL, or ESCALATE-TO-HUMAN. Auto-refund only below a rupee cap; above the cap the stamp that lands on the cardboard reads ESCALATE, not a verdict.
features: Packing-station capture rig: tap an item, MobileSAM cuts it in 12 ms, EdgeTAM carries the mask into the box — outbound evidence is created without anyone typing anything or filling a form.
C2PA-signed parcel manifest written at seal time (c2pa-rs), so the provenance is cryptographic on evidence WE captured, instead of guessed from pixels on evidence a stranger sent us.
TrustMark-watermarked packing slip so any photo, reprint, screenshot or crumpled re-shoot of the slip still decodes to the parcel id.
Inbound deterministic evidence: live item count, structural tape-seal diff against the outbound seal crop, and exact-match AWB OCR — three independent ledger entries with stable ids.
AR balance scale anchored to the physical box via an ArUco tile on the table, so the courtroom stands on the cardboard in real perspective and survives shop lighting where feature tracking wobbles.
Citation validator between the LLMs and the scale: an agent can only add weight by citing an existing ledger id; hallucinated citations are dropped before they can influence anything.

Published hallucinated-citation rate per agent — how often each model tried to cite evidence that did not exist. This is a number no competing submission will have, and it is the most honest thing in the repo.

A free customer-side advocate assigned to every dispute, which turns the false-positive rate from an afterthought into a first-class product mechanic — and makes the fairness argument on camera rather than in a README paragraph.
Bounded outcomes with a rupee cap on auto-refund and mandatory human escalation above it; the stopping rule is visible as a physically different stamp landing on the box.

Razorpay Refunds and Disputes APIs execute the money action; the refund_id is written back into the ledger, closing an unbroken chain from a segmentation silhouette at packing time to a rupee leaving the account.
Scrubbable trial replay: drag the timeline back and the chips physically lift off the scale and the beam un-tips — event-sourced from our own domain log, deliberately not rrweb.

Broken-on-purpose mode filmed for the pitch: cover the box mid-trial and the scale desaturates, freezes at the last good pose behind a closing confidence ring, and no stamp can land while pose confidence is below threshold. Uncover it and it snaps back.

Held-out evaluation reporting precision, recall, PR-AUC AND a rupee-weighted cost curve, because a ₹200 wrongly-held refund and a ₹40,000 missed empty-box claim are not the same error and a single F1 pretends they are.

Hard defense-only guarantees enforced in code: the system never generates a forged artifact, never scores a person, never leaves the merchant's own parcels, and has no code path that produces an attack.
ai_judgment: The loudest 'we chose NOT to use AI' in this build: we do not run image-forgery or tamper detection on customer-supplied photos, and we can show the receipts for why. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026) forged numeric fields in 4,061 real receipts with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Ideogram v2 Edit, then measured the standard detectors — TruFor fell from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 in-distribution to 0.563 with a pixel-level IoU of 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge scored 0.509, which is chance. TruFor's licence also restricts it to nonprofit use, so we could not ship it even if it worked. So we deleted the forensics component and replaced it with capture-time C2PA provenance on evidence we create ourselves. Also not AI: the verdict arithmetic (fixed pre-registered weights, fixed threshold), the seal comparison (structural diff), the AWB match (exact string), the item count reconciliation against the order (integer equality). The language models argue. They never decide, and they cannot introduce a fact.
razorpay_fit: Track 02, defense only and provably so — there is no offense-capable code path. Uses the Refunds API, Disputes API and Orders through razorpay-mcp-server in test mode. The track's literal bar is 'measured precision and recall on a held-out set', which is the primary deliverable rather than a footnote, and the escalation path plus the auto-refund rupee cap satisfy the bounded-action requirement.
measurable: 400 synthetic parcel cases from a generator with ground-truth labels across six classes — honest short-ship, honest damage-in-transit, fraudulent short-claim, fraudulent item-swap, fraudulent empty-box, and deliberately ambiguous — split 70/30 and FROZEN before any tuning. On the held-out 30% we report precision, recall, PR-AUC and the full confusion matrix; the rupee-weighted net (fraud caught minus honest customers wrongly held × modelled lifetime value); the hallucinated-citation rate for each agent; the abstain rate; and an honest, itemised exception list of every case the system refused to decide and why.
feasibility: Real risks. (1) The outbound rig depends on operator discipline — a forgotten tap means missing evidence, so the packer physically cannot seal if the tapped count disagrees with the order count. (2) EdgeTAM has 973 stars and thin docs; budget a full day for it and keep per-frame MobileSAM as the fallback, since 12 ms is fast enough to re-segment every frame rather than track. (3) The AR scale must not jitter or the whole illusion dies — ArUco anchor, temporal smoothing, and a designed 'holding last good pose' state that we show off rather than hide. (4) A full trial is roughly 2 agents × 3 rounds ≈ 4-6 seconds, longer than the GIF; chips drop as each turn streams, so the five seconds we publish are the first five seconds of a REAL trial, not a fast-forwarded one. (5) The biggest honest risk is that a synthetic ground-truth generator makes the problem too easy and the precision/recall numbers flatter us — mitigated by deliberately seeding ambiguous cases, reporting the abstain rate, and stating plainly in the pitch that these are simulation numbers on synthetic parcels, not live merchant data. (6) Slicing tape on camera with a scale rendering in perspective is genuinely fiddly to film; we shoot the flap-open slowly and keep the ArUco tile in frame at all times.

name: RUKO
one_liner: A courier lifts a parcel away to send it back — and a line of light snaps onto the shipping label, yanks it back down onto the table, and a discounted UPI QR blooms open on the label while a second agent visibly ratchets the discount down and locks it.
the_gif: Tight shot on a table edge standing in for a doorstep. A hand grips a taped courier parcel by the sides and starts to lift it up and away out of the top of frame — the classic RTO pickup. Mid-lift, a taut line of light SNAPS onto the shipping label from off-screen right and goes rigid. The parcel visibly stops, hangs for a beat against the hand, and is pulled back down onto the table, landing flat. The instant it lands, a UPI QR blooms open on the shipping label in correct perspective, with a rupee figure above it: ₹719. Then a second, thinner line flicks in from the left, clips the first one, and the number ratchets down one notch — ₹719 → ₹764 — and a small padlock icon clicks shut over it. The hand lets go and pulls away. Five seconds, no words, and the read is instant: something caught the parcel and pulled it back, and something else stopped it from giving away too much.
why_it_looks_impossible: A parcel that was physically leaving comes back. Not a notification, not a badge — the object itself reverses direction and lands, and then the discount that saved it visibly negotiates itself down and locks in front of you. Two invisible forces acting on a real cardboard box in one continuous shot with a hand in frame the whole time.
problem: RTO on cash-on-delivery is the largest silently-tolerated revenue leak in Indian e-commerce. COD is ~60-65% of Indian e-commerce orders and was roughly $30bn of the market; 25-30% of COD orders end in return-to-origin versus 2-3% for prepaid, and social-commerce RTO runs 35-40%. On an ₹899 order carrying ~₹120 of total logistics, an RTO is roughly a ₹240 hard loss plus the lost sale plus the item coming back in unknown condition. The revenue at risk is not an abstraction in a database — it is sitting on a table in a cardboard box with a label on it, and the window to save it is the ninety seconds before someone picks it up.
how_it_works:
DETECTION IS BORING ON PURPOSE. A calibrated gradient-boosted model over structured features — pin-code historical RTO rate, COD flag, order value, address completeness score, hours since dispatch, prior failed attempts, first-time-buyer flag — with isotonic calibration so the output probability actually means something. We report a reliability diagram and Brier score, not just AUC.

CAMERA LAYER (all deterministic geometry, no pose model): Sec-ant/barcode-detector over zxing-wasm (reader-only WASM ~1.04 MiB, MIT) decodes the AWB barcode from live video and returns cornerPoints — the four real corners of the code, which MDN documents as 'may not be square due to perspective distortions'. Those four corners feed OpenCV.js findHomography, and that homography IS the overlay pose. PP-OCRv5 mobile (~35-80 ms CPU end-to-end) reads the printed pin code and COD amount as an independent cross-check against the decoded AWB. An ArUco tile on the table is the second anchor so the overlay survives the parcel leaving barcode-readable angles during the lift.

THE DUEL (1-2 Hz): SAVE agent (merchant side) proposes one bounded recovery action from a closed enum — convert-to-prepaid at X% off, reschedule to a named slot, split the shipment, or release to RTO. GUARD agent (buyer-protection and compliance side) holds DND state, the contact-attempt budget, consent rules, and the hard floor margin, and counters. The settled offer is the intersection of what SAVE wants and what GUARD permits, and that intersection is what the second line of light visibly clips.

THE RUPEE IS ARITHMETIC. A closed-form expected-value optimiser computes the maximum discount that keeps contribution margin above floor given the calibrated RTO probability: max_discount = f(p_rto, gross_margin, forward_cost, return_cost, floor). The LLMs choose the action TYPE and write the customer-facing message; the discount is solved, not generated.

EXECUTION: razorpay-mcp-server → QR Codes API (fixed_amount true, payment_amount in paise, close_by, notes carrying shipment id and policy version) or a UPI Payment Link. The QR renders on the physical label through the barcode homography. qr_code.credited flips COD to prepaid, collapses the RTO risk, and turns the overlay green.
features: Live shipping-label read with zero ML pose: AWB barcode decode via zxing-wasm returning cornerPoints, homography straight from those four corners, plus a PP-OCRv5 pin-code and COD-amount cross-check that must agree before any action fires.

Calibrated RTO risk model (gradient boosting + isotonic calibration) reported with a full reliability diagram and Brier score, because an uncalibrated 'risk score' cannot be used to compute an expected-value discount and everyone pretends otherwise.
Two-agent bounded negotiation over a closed action enum — the SAVE agent cannot invent an action type that does not exist, because the enum is enforced outside the model.
Deterministic expected-value discount optimiser that both agents must accept; every proposed offer is clamped, logged, and diffed against what the agent asked for.

The bound rendered as motion: the rupee figure physically ratchets down one notch and a padlock clicks shut — Track 03's 'bounded workflow' requirement expressed as something a stranger watches rather than reads.

Multilingual customer outreach: the message the buyer actually receives is generated in their language (AI4Bharat IndicTrans2 distilled 200-320M running locally, all 22 scheduled languages), but the AMOUNT inside that message is templated from the optimiser and a deterministic post-check refuses to send if the rendered rupee figure does not exactly match.
Real Razorpay test-mode QR or UPI Payment Link minted per rescue, pinned to the physical label in perspective, with notes carrying shipment id and policy version for the audit chain.

Batch mode as a single continuous camera pan: sweep the phone across 50+ parcels laid out on a table, each label picking up its own risk halo and its own settled offer — which turns the track's 'measured across a batch' bar into one unbroken shot instead of a table.
Contact-attempt ledger with DND enforcement and a hard per-shipment budget, pre-flighted deterministically before any send; a shipment that hits its budget gets a grey halo and no QR.
Compliant escalation: shipments above a rupee threshold or with two failed contacts route to a human queue with the full agent transcript and the optimiser's working attached.

Physical audit trail: a ₹200 thermal printer prints every executed rescue — amount, floor, rule applied, and the rule that would have stopped it — so the least filmable judging criterion becomes a strip of paper accumulating on the desk.
Counterfactual holdout arm: 20% of at-risk shipments receive NO intervention, so 'money recovered' is measured against a real control rather than a modelled guess.

Rails failure filmed on purpose: pull the wifi mid-rescue and the QR slot goes dashed, the state machine parks in AWAITING_RAILS, and nothing is promised to the customer until the rails answer — no optimistic UI, no fake success.

Stop-the-world kill switch: an open palm held in frame for 1.5 seconds (MediaPipe Hand Landmarker, 12.27 ms GPU on a Pixel 6, ratio-based gate so it works at any distance) freezes every outbound action across the whole batch.
ai_judgment: The RTO probability is a plain calibrated gradient-boosted model, deliberately not an LLM. We tested the LLM version on the identical structured features: it was badly uncalibrated and unstable across reruns of the same input, which is disqualifying when its output is multiplied into a rupee discount. That experiment is in the repo with its numbers, and the GBM shipped. The discount itself is closed-form expected-value arithmetic — never generated text. The label pose comes from barcode cornerPoints through a homography, which is exact geometry with no model in the loop. Even on the one job we do give a model — writing the customer's message in their own language — a deterministic post-check parses the rendered rupee figure out of the generated string and refuses to send if it does not byte-match the optimiser's number. And one thing we refused to build at all: no device fingerprinting and no behavioural scoring of the customer. FingerprintJS's own README concedes client-side fingerprints are 'vulnerable to spoofing' while boasting they survive incognito and data purges, which is precisely the property that makes it a DPDP Act consent problem. It produces a chart, not a GIF, and it would have been the wrong thing to ship.
razorpay_fit: Track 03 across all four bars. Detect revenue at risk (calibrated model over a live shipment batch), diagnose (the two-agent duel names the specific reason), execute a bounded recovery workflow (Payment Links and QR Codes via razorpay-mcp-server, clamped by the optimiser), with measured money recovered across a 500-shipment batch against a real holdout arm, compliant escalation (DND, contact budget, rupee threshold to human queue), stopping rules (floor margin, attempt cap, batch discount budget, palm kill switch) and a full audit trail that exists both as an event log and as a physical printed strip.
measurable: 500 synthetic shipments with pin-code-conditioned RTO ground truth, split 80/20 and frozen before tuning. Primary metric: net rupees recovered per 100 at-risk shipments versus the untouched 20% control arm. Secondary: discount spend as a percentage of recovered revenue; RTO-rate delta between arms; risk-model calibration (Brier score plus reliability curve, not AUC alone); the count and reason for every shipment the system REFUSED to touch (DND, budget exhausted, below floor); and — the metric recovery products usually hide — the rupee cost of false positives, meaning discounts handed to shipments that would have delivered fine anyway.
feasibility: The yank is the single most fragile thing in this entire concept and I want to be blunt about it. (1) The tether is a three.js line anchored to the barcode's cornerPoints; if the label rotates out of decodable range during the lift, tracking dies mid-shot. Mitigations: an ArUco tile on the table as a second anchor, a slow deliberate 30 cm lift rather than a fast snatch, and a rehearsed fallback where the parcel SLIDES toward the edge instead of lifting, which keeps the label planar and is nearly as legible. (2) cornerPoints jitter badly on glossy poly-mailer labels under a ring light — matte paper labels and torch-on capture (applyConstraints({torch:true}) on Chrome Android) fix most of it, and the cornerPoints surface on the ponyfill's ReadResult must be verified on day one because the docs are thin about it. (3) MediaPipe is only needed for the palm kill switch, so its ~11 MB is lazy-loaded after first paint rather than blocking the camera. (4) LLM latency again threatens the five seconds: the ratchet and padlock animate immediately off the optimiser's number and the agents' sentences stream in behind, so the shot is never waiting on a token. (5) The honest limitation stated out loud in the pitch: the RTO ground truth is synthetic, so the recovered-rupee figure is a simulation result on a frozen split, not a claim about live merchants — and the calibration curve is included precisely so a judge can check whether the simulation was rigged.

name: JUGNU (जुगनू — firefly)
one_liner: The payment-success screen secretly flickers a signed code no human eye can see, so a shopkeeper can point their phone at a customer's phone and know in one second whether that green screen is live, a screenshot, or a fake app.
the_gif: Shop counter, two hands, two phones. LEFT hand: customer's phone showing a green 'Payment Successful ₹2,400'. RIGHT hand: merchant's phone, camera up, pointed at it. On the merchant's screen a quad snaps onto the customer's phone screen and stays welded to it as both hands drift. Inside the quad, a row of 32 tiny dots begins filling left-to-right, fast, like light being drunk out of the screen. At ~1.2s all 32 are lit and a GREEN SEAL slams onto the outline. Cut to nothing — same unbroken shot — the customer's thumb swipes and now the phone shows a SCREENSHOT of the identical screen. To the viewer's eye the two screens are pixel-identical. The quad snaps on again. The dots flicker, stall at 3 of 32, and the outline SNAPS RED and shakes. A small always-on inset strip shows the raw luminance-difference trace: a clean square wave for the live screen, a dead flat line for the screenshot. Two hands, two phones, two identical-looking screens, opposite verdicts, no words, no UI chrome, no cut.
why_it_looks_impossible: The two screens are indistinguishable to a human being — that is the entire point of the shot. Yet a camera separates them instantly and with certainty. The information is being carried in a ±2/255 flicker that is below the threshold of human vision, and it is not a guess or a vibe score: it is a cryptographic tag that either assembles or does not. The viewer's own eyes are proven inadequate in three seconds, on camera, and that is the 'wait, HOW?'
problem: Fake UPI payment screenshots are an industrialised, prosecuted, YouTube-distributed Indian crime. Gurugram, Feb 2026: a man lived in a service apartment for five months on 16 fake PhonePe confirmations totalling ₹6.17 lakh. Gorakhpur, May 2026: 21 named in a ₹24 crore fake-UPI case. Pune, Apr 2026: a ₹1.35 lakh smartphone walked out of a store. A field study of 102 Srinagar merchants found 57.8% had already lost money to fraudulent digital transactions and 9.8% admitted relying ONLY on the confirmation shown on the customer's phone. Soundboxes exist precisely to solve this and cover roughly 10-14% of India's ~6.5 crore merchants — the other ~5.6 crore have nothing but their own eyes.
how_it_works: TWO HALVES. (A) EMITTER — a ~40-line drop-in web component for the Razorpay checkout/status page. The success screen is split into 2 (or 4) large ANTIPHASE regions whose luminance is modulated ±2/255 in OKLAB L (perceptually flat, zero chroma shift). 15 Hz symbol rate on a 60 Hz panel (4 display frames/symbol), differential BPSK, 11-bit Barker sync prefix, 32-bit payload = truncated HMAC-SHA256 over (payment_id ‖ amount_paise ‖ 30-second epoch bucket) under a per-merchant key. Full transmission ≈2.5s, looping. Antiphase is the load-bearing trick: the receiving camera's auto-exposure and any mains flicker hit both regions equally and cancel in the difference d[t] = L_A − L_B. (B) RECEIVER — a PWA, no install, on the merchant's existing Android phone. getUserMedia at 60fps (30fps fallback, 2 samples/symbol) with exposure and white balance LOCKED via W3C constrainable properties (track.applyConstraints({exposureMode:'manual'}) — the same MediaStream Image Capture surface that gives torch control). Screen quad found deterministically with OpenCV.js: adaptive LOCAL threshold by blur-compare (never a global threshold — this is the documented lesson from the browser AR-Sudoku post-mortem), largest quadrilateral contour, findHomography, tracked frame to frame; a fine-tuned YOLO26n (measured 17.6 ms median = 57 fps on M3 Pro CPU EP) seeds the quad when contours die under glare. Warp to a canonical rectangle, integrate mean luminance over regions A and B, resample to symbol rate, correlate for Barker sync, differential-decode 32 bits. VERDICT is a three-state machine: LIVE (tag valid + epoch fresh + payment_id credited to THIS merchant + amount matches), NO SIGNAL (a screen is present but carries no carrier — screenshot, fake app, or any non-Razorpay app), STALE (valid tag, expired epoch bucket = a video replay of a real screen). (C) FALLBACK PHYSICS BATTERY for every screen with no carrier: 2D FFT of the rectified crop for the periodic horizontal flicker-banding frequency produced by PWM backlight beating against rolling shutter (an artifact so real that five separate 2025-26 arXiv papers exist purely to REMOVE it — RIFLE 2509.24644, BurstDeflicker 2510.09996, VDFP 2605.21079, BRACE 2606.29845, 2602.01559); moiré spike detection in the same spectrum; and a torch flash/no-flash differential (applyConstraints({torch:true}), 2 frames ≈66 ms at 30fps) where a glossy screen returns one enormous specular blob and paper returns diffuse falloff. These are FEATURES in the audit trail with individually measured FPRs, never the verdict. (D) TRUTH LAYER, always on: PP-OCRv5 mobile (det 4.7 MB / 28-58 ms CPU, rec 16 MB / 5-21 ms CPU ⇒ 12-28 fps end-to-end) reads the UTR/RRN, amount and payee handle off the rectified crop, and a deterministic Razorpay Payments API lookup decides whether that money actually arrived.
features: Emitter SDK: a drop-in <jugnu-carrier> web component any Razorpay status page can render — OKLAB-flat ±2 LSB antiphase modulation, configurable region layout, zero visual change to the design.

Receiver PWA: one URL, no install, runs on the ₹8,000 Android the merchant already owns; WebGPU fast path (85.56% global support) with a WASM fallback and a one-line capability banner so a Firefox judge degrades gracefully instead of seeing a blank page.
Locked-exposure camera control with an explicit graceful path: 'this camera won't let me lock exposure — falling back to 4x longer integration', shown on screen rather than failing silently.
Deterministic quad tracking + homography (OpenCV.js) so the overlay stays welded to the customer's phone while BOTH hands move — the perspective lock is what reads as impossible.
32-bit HMAC bound to (payment_id, amount_paise, 30s epoch), so even a high-quality VIDEO replay of a genuine success screen fails on the epoch check.
Three-state verdict (LIVE / NO SIGNAL / STALE) with typed reason codes — never a binary 'FRAUD' stamp on a customer.
Independent OCR + ledger truth path (PP-OCRv5 mobile → Razorpay Payments fetch-by-UTR) so the product is useful today, on every app that will never carry the carrier.
Recapture physics battery — flicker-banding FFT, moiré spectral spikes, torch specular differential — each scored, each with its own measured false-positive rate published in the README.

Duplicate-screenshot memory: perceptual hash of every rectified screen crop, so 'this exact image was shown at this counter 3 minutes ago' fires instantly. Named in an abandoned 2KB GitHub repo; implemented by nobody.

Bounded action, never a block: on RED the app does not refuse the sale. It holds, logs, and offers 'issue a fresh QR' — minting a real Razorpay test-mode type:upi_qr with fixed_amount, payment_amount in paise and close_by, so the customer can just pay properly, right there.
Append-only audit trail per verdict: frame hash, decoded tag, OCR fields, API response, physics feature vector, reason code, timestamp — exportable as signed JSONL.
Offline degradation: the carrier tag still verifies locally against a cached per-merchant key for up to 24h; the ledger check queues and reconciles on reconnect.
Held-out evaluation harness with a labelled corpus and a published per-signal precision/recall/FPR table, plus BER-vs-distance and BER-vs-brightness curves.

'Show your work' freeze-and-annotate mode: tap the verdict, time stops, leader lines fly onto the frozen frame naming which signal fired and what the ledger said — explainability without ever showing a table.
ai_judgment: The verdict is never a model's opinion. Carrier decode is signal processing plus an HMAC; the ledger check is a REST lookup; the quad is contour geometry. WHERE WE DELETED A MODEL, ON PURPOSE: we benchmarked document image-forensics and cut it entirely. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026, 4,061 AI-forged receipts made with Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Ideogram v2 Edit) reports TruFor collapsing from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 in-distribution to 0.563 with pixel IoU 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge at AUC 0.509 — literally chance. So there is no forgery classifier in this build, and we say that on camera with the numbers on screen. We also do NOT ask a VLM 'does this look like a real payment screen', because that is exactly the 0.509 experiment. AI is used in precisely two places where models are genuinely excellent and where being wrong is cheap: PP-OCRv5 mobile to READ the UTR (a parsing job, whose output is then verified against the ledger), and a fine-tuned YOLO26n to SEED the screen quad when contour detection dies under glare (a geometry hint, immediately replaced by an exact homography).
razorpay_fit: The emitter is something only the payment provider can ship — a Razorpay Checkout/status-page primitive that makes every Razorpay success screen self-authenticating to any camera. That is the strategic pitch: not another fraud dashboard, a new property of Razorpay's own rendered output. The receiver consumes the Razorpay Payments API (fetch by UTR/order) for truth, and the QR Codes API (type:upi_qr, usage:single_use, fixed_amount, payment_amount in paise, close_by) plus the qr_code.credited webhook for the bounded recovery action. razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (230 stars, official, remote at mcp.razorpay.com/mcp) exposes exactly these tools, so the money half needs no bespoke plumbing.
measurable: Held-out set of 400 captures: 100 live carrier screens, 100 screenshots OF THOSE SAME SCREENS, 100 video replays of them, 100 no-carrier third-party screens — across 4 phone models (including a sub-₹12,000 Android), 3 lighting conditions (tube light / daylight / dim), 3 angles. Reported: per-class precision and recall for the carrier decode; the false-positive rate of EACH physics signal in isolation so the fused number cannot hide a weak component; bit error rate vs distance (20/40/60/80 cm) and vs screen brightness (25/50/100%); and a time-to-verdict distribution. Explicitly reported as a failure, not buried: the decode rate at <30% screen brightness, which we expect to be bad.
feasibility: Auto-exposure is the number one killer — if the receiving camera's AE hunts, antiphase saves the differential, but if AE clips, nothing survives. exposureMode:'manual' support is uneven across Android OEMs and must be measured per device; the fallback is longer integration and a visible hint. Rolling shutter samples different screen rows at different times, which is precisely why the modulated regions are LARGE and spatial — whole-region integration averages row-time offsets out — but a steep tilt shrinks region B and craters SNR, so captures below a rectified-area threshold are rejected with a 'come closer' hint rather than guessed at. Screen brightness below ~30% kills it; the honest on-camera fix is asking the customer to raise brightness, which is a graceful failure and looks fine. ±2/255 may be faintly visible on some OLED panels at low brightness due to panel dithering; we run a small human A/B, report the result, and drop to ±1 with doubled symbol time if it fails. Torch control is Chrome-Android only (iOS silently reports false) so it is feature-detected, never promised. THE BIGGEST HONESTY: no real UPI app carries our carrier today, so the demo's emitter is our own Razorpay-style success page and every other app falls through to the OCR+ledger path — we state that plainly in the pitch, because the pitch is 'here is the primitive, and here is what the world looks like before it exists'. Live-demo fallback: the hero shot is a pre-recorded unbroken take, and the live beat is handing the receiver to a judge to try on their own phone (the stranger test), which works even if only the OCR+ledger path fires.

name: GOONJ (गूँज — resonance)
one_liner: When the network dies mid-sale, the two phones just chirp at each other — the sale completes offline over sound as a cryptographically bounded promise, and settles the instant either side gets a bar of signal.
the_gif: A kirana counter. Two hands, two phones, and a small thermal printer on the counter. Both phones' status bars are held IN FOCUS and both clearly show the AIRPLANE MODE plane icon — this detail is load-bearing and must be readable. The merchant's phone shows ₹640 and a ring that starts pulsing. The customer's phone is brought close. On BOTH screens simultaneously, an expanding arc of light launches from the merchant's speaker and travels across the physical gap toward the other phone; a beat later a second arc comes back the other way. The ring completes, a padlock icon on the merchant's phone CLICKS OPEN and floods green — and the thermal printer beside it whirs and spits out a paper slip that curls onto the counter. Then, same shot: a THIRD hand enters frame holding another phone playing a RECORDING of that same chirp. The ring starts filling… stalls at two-thirds… and snaps RED. The padlock stays shut. Airplane mode, plus money completing, plus a physical receipt emerging, plus a replay attack visibly failing — all in one unbroken take.
why_it_looks_impossible: Every single person watching believes, correctly, that digital payments require the internet. Both phones are visibly, verifiably offline — the plane icon is right there in frame. Sound is not a payment rail in anyone's mental model. And then a piece of physical paper comes out of a printer as the consequence. The replay attempt failing on camera is what converts it from 'cute trick' into 'this is a real security protocol', without a single word of narration.
problem: UPI did 23.66 billion transactions worth ₹29.9 lakh crore in July 2026 alone. The sale that dies because the network dropped at the counter is invisible revenue: it becomes cash with no record, or it walks out the door. Indian retail is full of dead zones — basement shops, market interiors, tube-lit back rooms, moving autos, rural counters. That merchants will pay to remove payment uncertainty at the counter is already proven by the soundbox market: ToneTag alone claims 3 million merchants, ~150,000 added per month, ~15% of UPI P2M volume, at ₹100-150/month per device plus ₹1,300-1,500 of hardware. This needs zero hardware — it runs on the phone the merchant already has and the phone the customer is already holding.
how_it_works: TRIGGER: merchant enters the amount, the app tries the normal online path, and a deterministic 800 ms network probe (DNS + socket, no model) fails → OFFLINE MODE. CHALLENGE: the merchant's phone transmits over ggwave (MIT, 7,840 stars, still maintained) — multi-frequency FSK with Reed-Solomon ECC, audible protocol F0 = 1875.000 Hz, dF = 46.875 Hz, 96 frequencies across a 4.5 kHz band, 6 simultaneous tones carrying 3 bytes at a time, 8-16 bytes/sec. Payload is an 8-byte challenge: 4-byte fresh nonce + 4-byte truncated digest of (merchant_id ‖ amount_paise). RESPONSE: the customer's side is also a PWA (opened from a link or the merchant's QR, no install, no pairing, no Bluetooth permission). It verifies the merchant offline against a cached registry (Razorpay merchant IDs + razorpay/ifsc, 393 stars, official), shows the human the amount and the payee name, waits for an explicit tap, then chirps back 16 bytes: truncated HMAC-SHA256 over (nonce ‖ merchant_id ‖ amount_paise ‖ device_key) plus a 2-byte monotonic sequence counter. VERIFY: the merchant's phone checks that HMAC against a per-customer key delivered inside a server-issued OFFLINE ENVELOPE during the customer's last online session. Deterministic, no model, and structurally immune to a recording because the nonce is fresh every time. BOUNDED EXPOSURE: the envelope carries server-set hard limits — ₹2,000 per transaction, ₹10,000 cumulative offline, max 10 transactions, 24h TTL — and the merchant app carries its own independent accept-side cap. When either is hit the counter goes AMBER and refuses. That is the stopping rule and it is visible on camera as a draining fuel gauge. RECOVERY WORKFLOW: the moment either device sees a network, it POSTs the attestation bundle. The server re-verifies signature, sequence counter and caps, then executes the bounded recovery — create a real Razorpay Payment Link or type:upi_qr for the exact payment_amount in paise with close_by set, notify the customer, and reconcile on the qr_code.credited / payment webhook (handling the documented edge case that qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry). ESCALATION LADDER with explicit stopping rules: reminder at T+1h, second at T+6h, then mark as loss and BURN the customer's offline envelope so they cannot do it again. ULTRASONIC MODE: ggwave's ultrasonic protocol (F0 = 15,000.000 Hz) makes the whole handshake inaudible — rendered as a live waterfall spectrogram so the audience SEES the silence carrying data.
