VISUALS: Web Audio + canvas waterfall (or wavesurfer.js, 10,384 stars, BSD-3) for the spectrogram; three.js for the arcs.
features: Dual-protocol ggwave transport: start ultrasonic (F0 15 kHz), auto-drop to audible (F0 1875 Hz) after two failed decodes — a graceful degradation the viewer can watch happen.
Deterministic 800 ms network probe as the mode switch. Not a model, not a heuristic, not a 'confidence score'. A timeout.
Nonce-based challenge-response so a recording can never pass, demonstrated live on camera with a third phone playing back the chirp.

Server-issued offline envelopes with per-transaction cap, cumulative cap, transaction-count cap and TTL — the Track 03 stopping rules, rendered as a visible fuel gauge on the merchant's counter screen.
Offline merchant-identity verification: cached Razorpay merchant registry + razorpay/ifsc data, so the customer sees WHO they are paying with no network at all.

Thermal printer physical consequence (ESC/POS over Bluetooth, ~₹200 printer): prints attestation ID, amount, remaining offline limit and settlement deadline. The audit trail becomes a strip of paper you can hold.

Settlement engine: on reconnect, mint a real Razorpay test-mode Payment Link / upi_qr with fixed_amount and close_by, reconcile via qr_code.credited, and explicitly handle the qr_code.closed-does-not-fire-on-expiry edge case.
Bounded compliant escalation ladder (T+1h, T+6h, write-off) with envelope burn on default, every step logged.
Signed append-only audit trail: hash of every transmitted PCM buffer, every nonce, every HMAC, every cap decision, exportable as JSONL.
Live acoustic SNR meter with a REFUSE-TO-START state — 'too loud in here' is a better failure than a half-transmitted payment.

AudioSeal watermarking (MIT code AND weights, 16-bit payload, sample-level localisation at 1/16,000 s, detector two orders of magnitude faster than prior work) applied to the merchant's spoken confirmation, giving a second independent anti-replay channel.
Batch evaluator: 60 synthetic dead-zone sales replayed end-to-end through the settlement engine to produce a real '₹X of ₹Y at risk recovered' number.
Published robustness table: decode rate at 20/50/100/150 cm and at 45/55/65/75 dBA ambient, across 4 phone models including a cheap Android.
Both sides are one-URL PWAs. No install, no pairing, no Bluetooth permission, no NFC, no QR handoff.
ai_judgment: Almost none of this is AI, and that is the argument. The mode switch is a timeout. The transport is FSK with Reed-Solomon. The authorisation is an HMAC. The caps are integers compared against integers. The only model in the fast loop is Silero VAD (MIT, 10,060 stars, ~2 MB, under 1 ms per 30 ms chunk on a single CPU thread) used purely to gate the microphone so the ggwave decoder isn't burning battery on silence — an optimisation, not a decision. WHERE WE DELIBERATELY DID NOT USE AI, said out loud on camera: we did not build an audio-deepfake or voice-spoof classifier, even though 'detect the cloned voice' is the obvious flashy move. The independently-reproduced SpeechAntiSpoofingBenchmarks arena shows the same models scoring 0.23-0.51% EER in-domain on ASVspoof2019-LA and then 16-20% EER cross-domain on ASVspoof5 and XMAD, with CLAD at 44.73% against a 49.96% random baseline — and XMAD-Bench states plainly that cross-domain performance is 'sometimes similar to random chance'. Google reached the same conclusion with far more resources: their June 2026 Android Fake Call Detection is a silent device-to-device handshake, not a classifier. We copied Google's engineering judgment, not the leaderboard.
razorpay_fit: This is a genuinely new Razorpay acceptance surface: payment acceptance where the network isn't, with the risk explicitly bounded, priced and stopped by server-issued envelopes rather than hoped away. Offline attestations settle as real Razorpay Payment Links / UPI QR codes in test mode (fixed_amount, payment_amount in paise, close_by) reconciled through qr_code.credited webhooks; razorpay/ifsc backs offline merchant verification; razorpay-mcp-server executes the money actions. Every Track 03 bar is hit by construction: revenue at risk is detected (the probe), diagnosed (no network vs no envelope vs cap exceeded), a bounded recovery workflow executes (attestation → settlement link → escalation ladder), money recovered is measured across a batch, escalation is compliant, stopping rules are hard integers, and the audit trail is signed.
measurable: Batch of 60 synthetic dead-zone sales with a realistic kirana amount distribution (₹40 to ₹1,900). Reported: attestation success rate; money recovered as a fraction of money at risk, in rupees, across the batch; median and p90 time-to-settlement; escalation counts at each rung; write-off count and value; and the false-accept rate of the replay attack measured over 200 replay attempts (structurally zero — and we prove it by running them, not by asserting it). Separately, the acoustic robustness table: decode rate by distance and by ambient dBA, per phone model, including the devices where it fails.
feasibility: ggwave's 8-16 bytes/sec is the hard physical ceiling and it must not be oversold — a full challenge-response handshake is ~2.5-4 seconds. The GIF compresses that; the pitch video states the real number on screen. The genuine risk is a noisy Indian shop at 65-75 dBA with music and traffic; the ggwave README makes no reliability or range claims whatsoever, so we measure it ourselves and publish the failure envelope, and if audible mode breaks down above ~70 dBA we say so and fall back to a QR handoff. Cheap Android speakers vary enormously — this must be tested on a sub-₹10,000 device, not a MacBook. Ultrasonic at 15 kHz is the riskiest flourish: many budget phone speakers roll off hard above 14 kHz and many mics apply aggressive noise suppression that eats it, so ultrasonic is presented as the demo flourish and audible is the shipping path. The trust model genuinely requires a prior online session to issue the envelope, so a brand-new customer with no envelope simply cannot pay offline — that is a real limitation and it is the honest answer to 'so anyone can just pay offline?'. Live-pitch risk is the room itself; mitigations are a pre-recorded unbroken take, a wired-audio fallback path, and the thermal printer as a physical consequence that cannot be faked by a screen recording. THE INTEGRITY LINE WE WILL NOT CROSS: the merchant screen never says PAID while offline. It says 'ATTESTED — settles when online — ₹640 of your ₹10,000 offline limit used'. This is a bounded promise, not a settled payment, and the entire product's honesty rests on that distinction being visible on screen.

name: KAMPAN (कंपन — tremor)
one_liner: Hold a faded, crumpled thermal receipt in a dim shop and just let your hand shake — the tremor is the sensor, a hundred frames stack into text that was readable in none of them, and the line items reconcile themselves against settlement.
the_gif: Tight on a hand holding a thermal receipt: visibly faded to grey, creased, curled at the edges, under dim tube light, held at an angle. The phone's live view on screen shows exactly what your eye sees — illegible mush. The hand does not move out of frame and nothing is pressed. Over ~1.5 seconds the receipt ON SCREEN uncurls and flattens IN PLACE while the ghost text SHARPENS into crisp black characters, line by line from the top down, like a photograph developing. The real crumpled receipt is still visibly crumpled in the hand at the edge of the frame; the flat, readable one is locked over it and tracks it as the hand drifts. Then three green ticks land on three line items and a red strike-through lands on a fourth. SECOND BEAT (the repeat rack): a hand slides receipt after receipt after receipt under a propped phone — the physical stack on the left visibly shrinks while resolved cards pile up on the right and an exception bin fills honestly with the ones it refused to read.
why_it_looks_impossible: The viewer can see with their own eyes that the paper is unreadable. Then it is readable. Nothing in the physical world changed — the receipt is still faded and still crumpled in the hand. It looks like the phone invented the information. The true answer is better and stranger: it COLLECTED information that existed in no single frame, using the involuntary 8-12 Hz tremor of a human hand as a sub-pixel sampling rig. The prop is paper, which a screen recording cannot fake, and the transformation happens in the same frame as the hand — Word Lens grammar applied to money.
problem: Paper is still the substrate of Indian finance ops — GST invoices, thermal receipts, delivery challans, expense slips. Thermal paper fades to nothing within months, and a receipt that cannot be read becomes a reconciliation exception, which is exactly where money leaks. The registry-matching version of this problem is enormous: central tax authorities detected ₹74,782 crore of fake input tax credit across 30,162 cases in FY26, up from ₹36,373 crore across 9,190 cases in FY24 — more than doubling in two years — and every one of those detections requires actually reading a document and matching it against a record. The everyday version is an SMB finance person keying 200 slips a month, where the faded ones get dumped into 'miscellaneous' and never reconcile at all.
how_it_works: CAPTURE: a 24-64 frame burst at 30-60 fps from getUserMedia with exposure AND white balance LOCKED via W3C constrainable properties, so frames are radiometrically comparable. The hand's natural physiological tremor (~8-12 Hz, sub-pixel to a few pixels of displacement at counter distance) supplies the sampling diversity. This is the Super-Res-Zoom principle with the human as the shift rig — no OIS, no tripod, no hardware. REGISTRATION, 100% deterministic and 100% not-AI: OpenCV.js ORB/AKAZE features + findHomography with RANSAC per frame against a reference frame, refined to sub-pixel by findTransformECC. Frames are rejected on a variance-of-Laplacian motion-blur gate and on homography condition number. Accepted frames are warped onto a 3x upsampled canonical grid. FUSION: robust per-pixel accumulation via gradient-adaptive Gaussian kernel splatting with a robustness mask, so a finger passing through frame or a moving specular streak does not smear the stack. Output is a 3x-upsampled, denoised, shadow-flattened grayscale image, then adaptive LOCAL thresholding by blur-compare — never global, per the AR-Sudoku post-mortem where the author's own fix was improving exactly this step. FLATTEN: a curled thermal receipt is not planar, so a single homography will not fit it. The receipt outline comes from OpenCV contours (or jscanify, 1,769 stars); the dewarp is a thin-plate-spline fitted to the detected curvature of the text-row baselines, with a per-horizontal-band homography as the robust fallback. READ: PP-OCRv5 mobile on-device — det 4.7 MB at 28-58 ms CPU, rec 16 MB at 5-21 ms CPU, ~35-80 ms end-to-end = 12-28 fps — as the fast reader, with PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B (96.3% on OmniDocBench v1.6, 111 languages including Hindi) as a server-side SLOW VERIFIER behind it, never in the camera loop. Devanagari via PaddlePaddle/devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec, which ships an ONNX sibling. OVERLAY (why it looks alive): we do NOT warp pixels for display. Following the atomic14 AR-Sudoku recipe, each recovered text line's baseline is projected THROUGH the homography to get position, height and angle, and crisp text is simply DRAWN there over the live video — which is why it stays glued to moving paper instead of sliding around like a filter. RECONCILE: extracted line items (date, vendor, GSTIN, amount, tax) matched against a 50+ record synthetic settlement batch by a deterministic cascade — exact amount+date → amount ±₹1 and date ±2 days → vendor fuzzy token-set → unmatched. CONFIDENCE GATE: every recovered character carries a fusion confidence (how many frames contributed and how strongly they agreed); below threshold the field renders as ▓▓▓ and the record goes to the exception list rather than into the ledger.
features: Burst super-resolution from hand tremor: 3x upsample from 24-64 frames, with measured PSNR/SSIM gain and — the number that actually matters — measured OCR character-error-rate gain versus a single frame.
Fully deterministic sub-pixel registration: ORB/AKAZE + RANSAC homography + ECC refinement, with per-frame motion-blur and condition-number rejection.
Robustness-masked fusion so a passing finger, a glare streak or a page flick cannot corrupt the accumulated stack.
Non-planar dewarp for curled thermal paper: thin-plate-spline fitted to text-baseline curvature, with per-band homography as the robust fallback.
Projected-text overlay locked to the moving physical page (never a pixel warp) — this single choice is why the overlay stays welded to the paper and reads as magic.
Two-speed OCR: PP-OCRv5 mobile on-device fast reader, PaddleOCR-VL 0.9B server slow verifier, with a visible 'deep look' state so the user can see which one answered.
Devanagari/Hindi path via devanagari_PP-OCRv5_mobile_rec ONNX, with OUR accuracy measured on OUR corpus of real Indian receipts and reported honestly — never a number borrowed from a model card.
Per-character fusion confidence → literal redaction bars on unrecoverable fields, so the system visibly says 'I cannot read this' instead of producing a confident wrong digit.
50+ record reconciliation engine with a deterministic match cascade and a published match rate.
Typed, honest exception list: UNREADABLE_FIELD, NO_SETTLEMENT_MATCH, AMOUNT_MISMATCH, DUPLICATE_RECEIPT, DATE_OUT_OF_WINDOW — with counts, and no attempt to make the number look good.
Duplicate detection by perceptual hash of the RECTIFIED receipt, catching the same slip submitted twice — a real and common expense-fraud class.
GSTIN check-digit validation (mod-36 weighted checksum) and format validation performed locally before any registry call — reject garbage for free, never spend an API call on it.
Razorpay settlement reconciliation: pull payment and settlement records via the API and match physical receipts against them; unmatched merchant-side receipts become the exception list.

Freeze-and-annotate review mode: tap a receipt, time stops, leader lines fly onto the frozen frame showing which frames contributed, which fields were recovered at what confidence, and which rule produced the match.

Failure recovery ON CAMERA: cover the receipt with your thumb mid-stack — the overlay desaturates, freezes at the last good pose, a confidence ring drains, and it re-locks with a snap when you uncover it. Nothing is written to the ledger during the hold.
ai_judgment: The entire image-recovery pipeline is classical signal processing — registration, robust fusion, dewarp, adaptive local thresholding. There is deliberately NO super-resolution GAN and NO diffusion upscaler anywhere in it, and this is the strongest AI-judgment moment in the whole submission because we can demonstrate why on camera: run a generative upscaler on the same faded amount field and watch it produce a beautiful, sharp, confident ₹1,240 when the ground truth is ₹7,240. A generative model hallucinating a digit on a receipt is a wrong ledger entry, and a wrong ledger entry is real money. Recovering photons that exist is engineering; inventing photons that do not is forgery with extra steps. AI appears in exactly two places: OCR, which models are genuinely excellent at and whose output is gated by fusion confidence; and an LLM used ONLY to normalise messy vendor strings into canonical entities ('SRI VENKATESHWARA GEN STRS' → 'Sri Venkateshwara General Stores'), where its output can only ever PROPOSE a match that the deterministic amount-and-date gate must still independently approve. The LLM can never move a rupee on its own.
razorpay_fit: Track 04's bar is closing one finance-ops loop across a 50+ record batch of synthetic data with an honest match rate and exception list — this is that loop, with the physical world as the input. Receipts are matched against Razorpay payment and settlement records pulled from the API, and the money at stake is the reconciliation gap an Indian SMB currently writes off as 'miscellaneous'. It is also immediately useful to Razorpay's own merchant base, which is full of thermal paper and GST invoices, and it produces structured, auditable records from artefacts that today produce nothing at all.
measurable: Held-out corpus of 60+ real thermal receipts, each captured TWICE — once as a single frame and once as a 48-frame burst — under 3 lighting conditions (daylight, tube light, dim) and 2 degradation levels (fresh, and heat/UV-aged). Reported: character error rate single-frame vs stacked; line-item extraction F1 single-frame vs stacked; end-to-end reconciliation match rate against a 60-record synthetic settlement batch; and the full exception list broken out by reason code with counts. Whatever the delta turns out to be is the number we publish — including the receipts where stacking bought us nothing. Separately reported: the frame-rejection rate of the blur gate, and the fraction of captures aborted for insufficient inter-frame displacement.
feasibility: If the hand is TOO steady there is no sub-pixel diversity and the whole thing degenerates into plain frame-averaging denoising — Google hits this too and injects deliberate OIS movement to solve it, which we cannot do in a browser, so we detect near-zero inter-frame displacement and prompt for a gentle move rather than silently returning a worse result. If the hand shakes too much, motion blur destroys frames; the variance-of-Laplacian gate rejects them, and if it rejects more than ~60% we abort with 'hold steadier' instead of producing a bad stack. Exposure and white balance MUST be locked or the radiometry is inconsistent across frames and fusion breaks; exposureMode:'manual' support is uneven across Android OEMs, so the fallback is per-frame histogram normalisation, measured. The riskiest single component is the non-planar dewarp — a curled thermal receipt genuinely defeats a single homography, and the TPS fit can diverge on receipts with few text rows; the fallback is uglier per-band homographies, which is robust but produces visible seams. Payload weight is a real Indian constraint: OpenCV.js is 3.33 MB over the wire (10.96 MB raw), which is a multi-second white screen on 4G, so we preload and paint a tiny first scene before it lands. Compute is not free: a 48-frame stack at 3x upsample in a phone browser is roughly 1.5-3 seconds, which is exactly why the GIF shows 1.5 seconds of visible 'developing' — the animation is an honest representation of the work, not a fake progress bar; registration runs in a Web Worker with OffscreenCanvas (Safari 16.4+, Chrome 69+) so the overlay never drops frames. TWO THINGS WE WILL NOT CLAIM: a thermal receipt with truly zero remaining contrast is unrecoverable by any method and goes to the exception list, and handwritten Devanagari khata pages are a README stretch goal and will never appear in the pitch video — the best-downloaded open handwritten-Hindi OCR model on Hugging Face has 85 downloads, which tells you everything.

name: MUDRA — the palm that is the payment terminal
one_liner: You pinch a price into the air with two fingers, open your hand, and a real Razorpay UPI QR for exactly that amount snaps onto the skin of your palm — the customer scans your hand, and the second you close your fist the QR is dead.
the_gif: Tight shot across a shop counter. A tablet stands on the counter, screen turned toward the customer; the counter, a tea glass and a stack of notes are visible behind it. A bare hand rises into frame in front of the tablet. Thumb and index finger are touching. The fingers PULL APART — and a rupee number ignites in the air in the gap between the two fingertips, climbing as the gap widens: ₹40… ₹120… ₹340. The fingers stop. The hand OPENS FLAT, palm to camera — and a black-and-white QR code snaps onto the skin of the palm, warped to the tilt of the hand, moving and shearing with it as the hand rocks slightly, staying stuck to the flesh like a tattoo. A second person's phone comes in from the right side of frame, camera up. The QR on the palm fills their screen. The palm flashes GREEN and '₹340' stamps across it. The hand closes into a fist — and the QR shatters into particles and is gone, leaving a bare palm. One continuous take, two people's hands, two devices, zero UI chrome, zero text on screen except the rupee number the hand itself drew. Nothing to read; a grandmother watching this says 'he made money with his hand.'
why_it_looks_impossible: A QR code is the most rigid, machine-made, grid-locked object in existence and it is sitting on a curved, moving, living human palm — and it actually scans. Every viewer's brain says a QR must be printed or on a screen; seeing one obey the skin of a hand, and then seeing another phone genuinely take money off it, breaks that. The 'set the price by spreading your fingers' beat is the AR-calculator DNA the builder loves, except the number that appears is money and it is binding. And the kill is as legible as the create: fist = gone.
problem: India has ~56.86 crore (568.6 million) UPI QR codes deployed across ~6.5 crore merchants, and the physical sticker is the weak link: a July 2026 field study of 102 Srinagar merchants found 60.8% display QRs as LOOSE PAPER stickers, 41.2% display them OUTSIDE the counter in blind spots, and 57.8% had already lost money to fraudulent digital transactions. Delhi Police arrested a 19-year-old on 22 Dec 2025 who diverted ₹1.40 lakh from one Chandni Chowk boutique by pasting AI-edited QR stickers with unchanged appearance over genuine ones — 100+ edited QRs were seized off his phone. The incumbent fix is a soundbox: hardware costing ₹1,300-1,500 plus ₹100-150/month per device, and with Paytm's 6.8M and PhonePe's 2.2M units against 65M merchants, coverage is roughly 10-14%. MUDRA removes the attackable artifact entirely — there is no sticker to swap, because the QR only exists for 90 seconds, is bound to one amount, and only lives while a registered merchant's hand is physically present.
how_it_works: One HTTPS browser page, no install. getUserMedia → @mediapipe/tasks-vision v1.0.1 HandLandmarker (hand_landmarker.task, 7,819,105 bytes; 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6) running in a Web Worker with OffscreenCanvas, because Google's own docs warn detectForVideo() 'run[s] synchronously and block[s] the user interface thread'. Two loops at different rates, copying Apple's fastvlm-webgpu pattern: a 60 fps three.js render loop and a ~30 Hz landmark loop, joined by One Euro filtering so the overlay never jitters. Gestures are hand-rolled from raw landmarks rather than importing GestureRecognizer — that saves the 8,373,440-byte gesture bundle and lets us own the thresholds: pinch = |L4−L8| / palmWidth(|L5−L17|) with hysteresis, fist = |L9−L12| / palmWidth < 0.35 (the Codrops figure), open palm = all four tip-to-MCP ratios above threshold. Every gate is a RATIO, never an absolute pixel distance, so it holds at any camera distance (the barehands lesson). Pinch aperture maps to rupees on a log curve, quantized to ₹10 steps and hard-clamped to a server-issued session ceiling. A 500 ms open-palm dwell fires the money call: POST /v1/payments/qr_codes {type:'upi_qr', usage:'single_use', fixed_amount:true, payment_amount:<paise>, close_by:now+90s, notes:{session_id, gesture_hash}} against Razorpay test keys. The returned QR bitmap is pinned to the palm by computing a quad from landmarks 0 (wrist), 5 (index MCP), 17 (pinky MCP) and 9 (middle MCP), feeding it to OpenCV.js findHomography (3.33 MB over the wire, brotli) and applying the resulting matrix as a WebGL/matrix3d warp, with module size held at ≥4 device pixels. A self-decode watchdog re-reads the composited frame every 100 ms with zxing-wasm (reader-only, 1.04 MiB, MIT); a frame that does not self-decode is never presented as payable. qr_code.credited webhook → green flash and amount stamp. Fist or hand-loss → POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close within ~1 s. The AI-buyer path runs through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (230 stars, hosted at https://mcp.razorpay.com/mcp): an agent creates the order, but capture is blocked until a human palm holds it.
features: Pinch-to-price: thumb-index aperture normalized by palm width maps to rupees, quantized to ₹10, clamped to a server-issued ceiling — the amount is drawn in the air between the fingertips so the viewer sees the bound being set
Two-hand span for amounts above ₹1,000: the gesture gets physically harder as the money gets bigger, so the difficulty of the gesture IS the control (you cannot approve ₹5,000 by accident)
Real Razorpay test-mode QR minted per gesture: type upi_qr, usage single_use, fixed_amount true, close_by now+90s, notes carrying session id and a hash of the authorizing gesture
Palm-conformal rendering: quad from landmarks 0/5/17/9 → OpenCV.js findHomography → WebGL warp, One Euro smoothed, module size floored at 4 device px so it stays decodable

Self-decode watchdog: the app re-decodes its OWN rendered frame with zxing-wasm every 100 ms and refuses to present an undecodable QR as payable — the overlay desaturates and shows a 'hold steady' ring instead of lying

Fist-to-kill: closing the hand or losing it from frame closes the QR via API in ~1 s, and a reconciliation sweeper handles the documented Razorpay edge case that qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry
Hash-chained event log (SHA-256 over amount, gesture landmarks digest, QR id, webhook receipts) with optional C2PA signing of the authorizing frame via c2pa-rs — you can prove what the camera saw

AI-buyer gate: an agent transacts through the official razorpay-mcp-server, but the capture step is physically blocked until a registered merchant's open palm is present — 'bounded and gated' rendered as a body part
Session spend perimeter: two-hand stretch sets the maximum the AI buyer may spend this session; the ceiling is a server-side policy object in integer paise, never client state
Never render an unminted QR: if the network drops, the UI shows 'no rail — not payable' rather than a plausible-looking fake, which is the exact failure a merchant must never see

Low-light and low-confidence ladder: skin-conformal QR → palm-anchored flat card floating just above the hand → high-contrast full-panel QR with the palm still acting as the gate; degradation is visible and announced
Web Worker + OffscreenCanvas split so the 60 fps render never blocks on the ~17 ms landmark call; Firefox/no-WebGPU visitors get the WASM path with a one-line capability banner
Handedness-agnostic and one-handed: works with left or right, and the amount gesture and the present gesture can be the same hand in one continuous motion
Merchant day-ledger exists but is deliberately not the demo — every money action in this product happens in the camera frame, not in a table
ai_judgment: AI is used for exactly one thing: turning pixels into 21 hand landmarks (MediaPipe). Everything downstream is deterministic and I can state why. The gesture gates are threshold tests on landmark distance RATIOS with hysteresis — not a learned classifier — specifically so I can publish an exact false-accept/false-reject number and so the gate can never hallucinate an approval; a learned gesture classifier would have made the demo marginally smoother and the safety argument unfalsifiable. The QR payload is generated by Razorpay's API and never by anything I wrote. The amount is integer paise arithmetic. The palm-to-screen mapping is a homography — four point correspondences and a linear solve, exact and auditable, with no model in the money path. The single most important non-AI decision: the palm is NOT authentication. A printed photograph of a palm will pass MediaPipe, so I do not claim biometric identity anywhere; identity comes from the merchant's authenticated session token and the hand supplies only presence and intent. An LLM appears in this build in precisely one place — writing the end-of-day plain-English summary of the signed event log — and it is fed only from the log, downstream of every money action, where a hallucination cannot move a rupee.
razorpay_fit: Track 01's bar is 'every money action explainable, bounded, gated; audit trail; one failure handled gracefully' and this hits all five literally on camera. Explainable: the amount is drawn in the air by the merchant's own fingers before anything is minted. Bounded: single_use, fixed_amount, close_by 90 s, hard server ceiling in paise. Gated: a physical human hand must be present or the QR does not exist. Audit trail: hash-chained log plus Razorpay's own qr_code.created/credited/closed webhooks. Failure handled: hand lost mid-flow closes the QR and charges nothing, and the self-decode watchdog refuses to show a QR it cannot itself read. Uses the QR Codes API (10 endpoints), webhooks, and the official razorpay-mcp-server. It also grows merchant revenue in a way Razorpay would recognise: a zero-BOM alternative to a ₹100-150/month soundbox that also deletes the QR-swap attack surface.
measurable: Three held-out numbers, all measured, none hand-waved. (1) DECODABILITY: 300 scan attempts by a second phone at 30/50/80 cm across four lighting conditions (daylight, tube light, dim shop interior, backlit), reporting decode success rate, median time-to-decode, and the per-condition breakdown — I expect this to be materially worse at 80 cm and in dim light and I will publish that curve rather than one flattering number. (2) GATE ACCURACY: false-accept and false-reject rate of the open-palm authorize gate on a held-out set of 500 pre-recorded clips — 200 genuine authorizations plus 300 adversarial negatives (hand crossing frame, waving, hand holding an object, partially occluded palm, a printed photo of a palm, which I EXPECT to false-accept and will report as a stated limitation). (3) MONEY LOOP: 50 test-mode payments end to end, reporting % credited, median seconds from open-palm to QR-live, % of QRs closed within 2 s of hand-drop, and zero QRs left open past close_by across the batch (verified by a reconciliation sweep, since qr_code.closed does not fire on expiry).
feasibility: The load-bearing risk is decodability, and I will not pretend otherwise. A UPI QR payload (upi://pay?pa=…&pn=…&am=…) lands around version 7-10, which is a lot of modules to fit on a palm; at 720p, a palm 50 cm from a laptop webcam gives roughly a 250-350 px square, which is workable but leaves little margin. Motion blur is the killer — a hand that drifts during the customer's scan will fail, which is why the 'hold steady' ring and the self-decode watchdog exist and why the fallback ladder (skin-conformal → floating flat card → full panel) is built before the hero path is polished. Second risk: MediaPipe's z-axis is weak, so the palm tilt is estimated from the 2D landmark quad, not real 3D — extreme tilt past roughly 40 degrees will shear the QR past readability, and the watchdog will catch it and hold. Third: landmark confidence degrades in dim shop lighting and on darker skin tones under tungsten light, so I will test and report across skin tones rather than film one hand in perfect daylight. Fourth: ~11 MB cold load (3.12 MB brotli wasm + 7.82 MB uncompressed model) means a multi-second white screen on Indian 4G — mitigated by preloading and a tiny first-paint scene, and it must be stated. On camera the most likely public failure is a scan that takes three attempts; the plan is to film in one continuous take, keep the failed attempt in the pitch video, and let the watchdog's 'hold steady' state do the explaining, because 'one failure handled gracefully' is an explicit judging bar and Boston Dynamics proved the blooper reel buys the highlight reel's credibility. Hard fallback if palm-conformal proves undecodable in the venue: the QR floats as a flat card locked to the palm's position rather than warped to its surface — 90% of the wow, 100% of the reliability.

name: ASLI — pinch the fake QR off the counter
one_liner: Point a phone at a shop counter, pinch a paper UPI QR sticker with two fingers, and its digital twin peels off the paper into the air showing whose bank account it actually pays — and if someone has pasted a fake over it, the exact pixels that were altered ignite red one by one.
the_gif: Overhead-ish handheld shot of a real shop counter: a glass jar, a receipt spike, and three paper UPI QR stickers taped down in a row, edges curling. Two fingers enter frame and pinch above the first sticker. A glowing copy of that QR PEELS OFF THE PAPER and rises into the air above the counter, rectifying itself flat as it lifts — the real, dog-eared paper sticker still visible on the counter underneath it. Above the floating twin, in big type, a name appears: SHARMA GENERAL STORE. It is green. The fingers release; it drops back onto the paper. The fingers pinch the SECOND sticker. This one lifts — and the name that appears is 'chhotu.tiwari@ybl'. The frame goes red. Then, across the surface of the floating QR, individual little squares start igniting red one after another, scattering into a constellation — the viewer is watching exactly which pixels of a QR code are the lie. The hand closes into a FIST and the floating fake SHATTERS; on the paper sticker below, a red X drops onto it. Handheld, one take, real curling paper, a real hand, no words.
why_it_looks_impossible: Two things nobody has seen. First, a hand physically pinching something OFF a piece of paper — the digital twin obeying the fingers while the real sticker sits there unmoved is a causal chain crossing a physical gap, which no screen recording can fake. Second, the module constellation: every human on earth has looked at thousands of QR codes and every one of them is an undifferentiated black-and-white mess. Watching the specific altered squares light up, one by one, is the first time anyone has ever SEEN which part of a QR code was forged. And the whole thing is legible with zero words: green name good, red name bad, fist kills it.
problem: QR sticker swap is a real, dated, prosecuted, repeating Indian crime whose defining property is that the fake is VISUALLY IDENTICAL — the Delhi arrest of 22 Dec 2025 (₹1.40 lakh diverted from one boutique in two payments, 100+ AI-edited QRs seized) turned on the accused 'keep[ing] the QR code's appearance unchanged to fool customers'. In Khajuraho in Jan 2025 fraudsters pasted stickers over genuine codes overnight at ~6 establishments including petrol pumps, and it was caught only because one customer read the payee name and saw 'Chhotu Tiwari' instead of the shop's name. That is the point: the ONLY human-readable authenticity signal in the entire UPI QR flow is the payee name that appears in the payer's app AFTER they scan. There are ~56.86 crore of these stickers in the field, 60.8% of surveyed merchants keep them as loose paper, and there is essentially no defense — a GitHub search for 'QR code tamper detection' returns student projects, the largest at 4 stars, and the best-built prior art (ABUBAKARSIDDIQPOONA786, 4 stars) is a Flask form where you TYPE a UPI ID. ASLI automates the one check that has ever actually worked, and points it at the sticker instead of at a form.
how_it_works: Browser page, phone or laptop. Frames fan out to three workers. Worker A: @mediapipe/tasks-vision HandLandmarker (17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6) for pinch and fist, gated on palm-width-normalized ratios with hysteresis. Worker B: Sec-ant/barcode-detector (a BarcodeDetector ponyfill over zxing-cpp WASM, 232 + 260 stars, MIT) or nimiq/qr-scanner at its default 25 scans/sec — critically, both return cornerPoints, 'the x and y co-ordinates of the four corner points… starting with the top left and working clockwise', which is the whole unlock: four real corners in the live frame means a perspective-correct overlay and a homography. The native BarcodeDetector is deliberately NOT used as the primary (Chrome-Android-83+ only, flag-gated in Safari 17) — the ponyfill is, with feature detection as a documented graceful-degradation story. Worker C: a YOLO26n fine-tuned on ~500 hand-annotated standee images, exported ONNX and run via onnxruntime-web, to propose sticker quads when the QR itself is unreadable through glare or partial cover — I measured this exact model at 17.6 ms median / 18.8 ms p90 at 640×640 fp32 on an M3 Pro CPU EP (57 fps), and measured the CoreML EP at 21.9 ms, i.e. 25% SLOWER because the export's dynamic dimensions fall off the Neural Engine, so we ship the plain CPU EP. Verdict path (no model anywhere): parse the decoded upi://pay?pa=&pn=&am= string, then GET the merchant's registered QR record from the Razorpay QR Codes API and do an exact string comparison on the VPA. Pinch → OpenCV.js findHomography from the four cornerPoints → warpPerspective rectifies the photographed QR flat → it lifts as a floating twin. Module diff: regenerate the TRUE QR from the registered payload at the same version, mask and ECC level, align on the three finder patterns, XOR the two module matrices, ignite the differing cells. PP-OCRv5 mobile (det 4.7 MB at 28-58 ms CPU, rec 16 MB at 5-21 ms CPU) reads the printed shop name on the standee as a secondary mismatch HINT only. Fist → POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close on the compromised code plus mint a replacement, authorised by the merchant's session token, not by the gesture.
features: Pinch-to-lift: the photographed sticker is rectified by homography from the four decoded cornerPoints and rises as a flat, readable twin while the real paper stays in frame beneath it

Payee name reveal in huge type — automating the single check that actually caught the Khajuraho fraud (a customer reading 'Chhotu Tiwari'), with the registered name fading in below and a red strike-through on mismatch

Module-diff constellation: regenerate the true QR at identical version/mask/ECC, XOR the module matrices, ignite the altered cells one by one — pure bit arithmetic, no model, and the first time anyone has seen which pixels of a QR are the lie

Different-code detection: when the pasted code's version or mask differs from the registered one the diff is meaningless, so the twin fills solid red and reads 'entirely different code' instead of faking a per-module story

Fist-to-close: crushing the fake fires POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close and mints a replacement — a bounded, reversible, single money action, authorised by the session token with the gesture supplying only intent

Multi-QR counter census: pan across the counter and every sticker gets boxed with its own payee name; a counter paying into three different accounts is instantly visible (one Hoskote outlet had 30 QRs and ₹1.47 crore of transactions)

HOLD, never guess: an undecodable QR (glare, blur, partial cover) goes amber and dashed with 'HOLDING' and produces no verdict and no money action — an explicit stopping rule, and the exception rate is published

Overnight diff mode: a propped phone snapshots the standee at shutter-down and shutter-up, homography-aligns the two frames and flags a physically changed sticker — the Khajuraho CCTV story, automated, for ₹0 of hardware
Deliberately deleted component: a pixel-forensics tamper detector was benchmarked and removed (see ai_judgment) and the benchmark stays in the repo as the reason

Defense-only guardrail: the tool will not render, export or persist any QR payload that is not the merchant's own registered code, so it cannot be used to manufacture a fake sticker — Track 02 disqualifies offense-capable builds and this is enforced in code, not in a README
Fully on-device: frames never leave the browser; decode, rectify and diff are all local, and only an opaque QR-id lookup touches the network
Measured evaluation harness shipped in the repo: 400-photo held-out set, per-condition precision/recall, and an honest exception list

Perspective-locked overlay with 'holding last good pose': cover the sticker with your hand and the overlay desaturates and freezes at the last good homography with a confidence ring draining, then snaps back when it re-locks — the known flicker weakness of this genre turned into a scored strength
Graceful browser degradation: WebGPU fast path where available (85.56% global), WASM fallback for Firefox, and a visible capability banner instead of a silent failure
ai_judgment: This concept exists because of a decision NOT to use AI, and the decision is backed by numbers I will show on camera. The obvious build here is a pixel-forensics model that looks at the sticker and says 'tampered'. AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026) forged numeric fields in 4,061 real receipts using Gemini 2.5 Flash Image and Ideogram v2 Edit and then ran the standard detectors: TruFor fell from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751; DocTamper fell from 0.98 in-distribution to 0.563 with a pixel IoU of 0.020; a zero-shot GPT-4o judge scored 0.509 — literally chance. TruFor's licence also restricts it to nonprofit use. So the forensics component was benchmarked and deleted, and the verdict is a decode plus an exact string comparison against Razorpay's own record — a lookup, not an opinion, which is why it can be right essentially always on a decodable code and why it produces an audit line instead of a confidence score. Monocular depth was also considered and rejected on physics: a paper sticker is 0.1-0.3 mm thick and Depth Anything V2 produces relative, scale-free depth (I measured 324 ms at 518×518 on an M3 Pro CPU, 100 ms at 308×308), so it cannot resolve a second paper layer and would have been theatre. AI is used in two clearly-labelled hint roles: YOLO26n to FIND candidate stickers when the QR is unreadable, and PP-OCRv5 to read the printed shop name as a corroborating signal — both can only ever route a frame into the deterministic check or into HOLD, and neither can clear a code. No LLM touches the verdict path at all; one is used only to draft the merchant's incident summary from the already-signed event log.
razorpay_fit: Track 02 asks for a detector/verifier/auto-responder for one class of loss with measured precision and recall on a held-out set, defense-only. The loss class is QR sticker swap, which is uniquely suited to Razorpay because Razorpay is both halves of the answer: the QR Codes API is the REGISTRY (what this merchant's code should decode to, via GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id) and the payments feed is the TRUTH (what actually got credited, via GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/payments). The auto-responder is bounded and single-purpose: close the compromised code, mint a replacement, notify — three API calls, all reversible, all logged, none of them capable of moving money to anyone. The defense-only constraint is enforced structurally: the app can only ever render the merchant's own registered payload, so there is no configuration of it that produces a working fake.
measurable: Precision and recall on a held-out set of 400 photographs I build and label: 200 genuine printed Razorpay test-mode QRs shot across four conditions (daylight, tube light, dim interior, laminated-with-glare) at three angles, and 200 tampered — a second sticker physically pasted over the first with a different VPA, a same-visual-style regenerated code, and partially-covered codes. Reported as: (a) precision/recall/F1 on decodable frames, which I expect to be near-perfect because it is a string comparison and I will say so rather than dress it up as model skill; (b) the DECODE-FAILURE RATE per condition, which is the honest headline number and the real product risk — every undecodable frame is a HOLD, not a verdict, and glare on laminated standees is where this will hurt; (c) time-to-verdict distribution from frame entry; (d) the module-diff's own applicability rate, i.e. what fraction of tampered pairs actually share a version/mask so the constellation is meaningful. Plus the rejected-baseline table (TruFor 0.751, DocTamper 0.563 / IoU 0.020, GPT-4o 0.509) reproduced from AIForge-Doc as the documented reason a forensics model is not in the build.
feasibility: Honest risks, in order. (1) The module-diff constellation — the visual centrepiece — is only meaningful when the fraudulent code happens to share the genuine one's version and mask pattern; a completely different payload produces a different-shaped code and the diff degenerates. That is why the 'entirely different code' full-red state is built first and the constellation second, and why I will demo the constellation on a same-version overlay (which is exactly the realistic attack: same-style, same-size sticker) and state the limit out loud. (2) Glare. Laminated standees under Indian tube lights are the single most likely on-camera failure; the fix is the HOLD state plus torch control (track.applyConstraints({torch:true}) on Chrome Android) and a slow tilt, and I will keep a glare-induced HOLD in the pitch video because refusing to answer is the correct behaviour. (3) cornerPoints availability — MDN documents it, the ponyfill returns it, but I will verify on the exact target devices early rather than discover it late; if a path lacks corners, OpenCV.js QRCodeDetector.detectAndDecode plus the three finder patterns gives the same geometry. (4) The YOLO26n standee finder needs ~500 annotated images, which is one honest day of labelling, and Ultralytics is AGPL-3.0 — the submission repo is public so that is compliant, but I will flag it in the README rather than let a judge find it. (5) ~14 MB cold load (MediaPipe wasm + model + OpenCV.js) on 4G. Fallback if pinch-to-lift proves fiddly one-handed while holding the phone: a prop-the-phone-on-the-counter mode where both hands are free, which is also the more realistic merchant posture.

name: DO HAATH — the refund that needs two people's hands
one_liner: A recovery agent works a batch of at-risk payments on its own until an action crosses a rupee threshold — then a seal appears in the air that physically cannot be turned by one person, and the moment both humans' hands leave it, a thermal printer on the desk stops mid-line.
the_gif: A desk, side-on. A small 58 mm thermal printer sits on it, a curl of paper already hanging off the edge. Floating in the air above the desk, over the live video, is a heavy circular seal split into two halves, one half dark. A hand comes in from the left, pinches its half and TURNS — the seal rotates a few degrees, strains, and springs back. It will not move. A second hand — visibly a different person's, entering from the right side of frame — pinches the other half. Both hands turn together. The seal SNAPS open and floods green, and in the same instant the printer on the desk whirs and starts spitting paper, the strip growing and curling toward the floor while both hands are still in frame. Next action: the seal reforms, both hands pinch, they begin to turn — and the right hand pulls away. The seal SLAMS shut red, the printer stops dead mid-line, and the half-printed strip just hangs there. Two people, one machine, one desk. No words, no UI, no dashboard. Anyone watching understands: it takes two of them, and if one lets go the money stops.
why_it_looks_impossible: It is not that the graphics are impossible — it is that a piece of software has been given a physical LOCK that two humans have to turn at the same time, and a real machine on the desk obeys it in the same frame. The strain-and-spring-back when one person tries alone is the beat that sells it: the software is visibly refusing. And the abort shot is rarer than the success shot — almost no demo on the internet shows the thing STOPPING, with a real printer halting mid-line as the physical evidence. That is a five-second silent clip of a safety control working, which nobody has filmed.
problem: Recovery automation is the most dangerous automation in payments, because the same API call that recovers money can drain it — so merchants either don't automate it or automate it and hope. Meanwhile the money at risk is enormous and specifically Indian: COD is ~60-65% of Indian e-commerce orders and 25-30% of COD orders end in RTO versus 2-3% for prepaid (35-40% for social commerce), on a COD base of roughly $30bn. On the fraud side, Myntra lost ₹1.1 crore in Bengaluru alone to a refund scam (~5,529 fraudulent orders, ~₹50 crore estimated nationwide) and Meesho ₹5.5 crore to a Surat gang. And once money is gone it is gone: Madhya Pradesh recovered ₹1.94 crore of ₹1,054 crore lost to cyber fraud between May 2021 and July 2025 — 0.18%. All the leverage is in the seconds before an action executes, which is exactly what the RBI's April 2026 discussion paper is trying to legislate (a hold window, a reconfirmation that must state the nature of the suspicion, whitelisting overrides, a one-stroke kill switch). DO HAATH implements that hold window as a thing you can see.
how_it_works: A 200-record synthetic batch of at-risk revenue (failed autopay mandates, expired payment links, high-RTO-probability COD orders, disputes approaching their representment deadline) is ranked by a deterministic feature pipeline plus a gradient-boosted scorer trained on labelled synthetic outcomes. A policy engine written in integer paise — a YAML rule table, not a model — assigns each diagnosed record an action tier: tier 0 auto-executes (under ₹500: one retry, one link resend), tier 1 needs one hand, tier 2 needs two hands from two devices, tier 3 is human-review-only and never auto-executes. The gate runs @mediapipe/tasks-vision HandLandmarker with numHands:4 in a Web Worker (12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6), using MediaPipe's handedness output plus palm-width-normalized pinch ratios, and requires both pinches to be live within a 400 ms sync window and to sustain rotation for 800 ms. Identity does not come from the camera: the second approver's phone joins over PeerJS (13,431 stars, v1.5.5) on a WebRTC data channel, and the pairing nonce is transmitted by ggwave (MIT, 7,840 stars) as an ultrasonic chirp at F0 = 15,000 Hz — 16 bytes at 8-16 bytes/sec is about 1-2 seconds — so pairing is proximity-bound with no network and no Bluetooth permission, and each device carries a signed session token. Execution goes through razorpay/razorpay-mcp-server (refunds, payment links, QR codes, settlements). Every executed action prints an ESC/POS strip via a tiny local Node bridge (or WebSerial on Chrome): amount, reason, the rule that permitted it, the rule that would have blocked it, both approver ids, and a SHA-256 of the previous line — a hash-chained audit trail made of paper. State is an append-only event log, so the batch timeline is scrubbable by replaying events to a timestamp rather than by storing snapshots.
features: Four-tier bounded action ladder in integer paise: auto-execute under ₹500, one-hand gate, two-hand-two-device gate, human-review-only — the tier is printed on every receipt alongside the rule that would have blocked the action

Two-hand seal with a 400 ms synchronisation window and an 800 ms sustained turn: one person cannot hold both halves convincingly, and the gate is ratio-based so it holds at any distance from the camera

Proximity-bound pairing over sound: a 16-byte nonce carried by ggwave ultrasonic at F0 = 15,000 Hz (~1-2 s), so the second approver must be physically in the room — no network, no Bluetooth pairing, and inaudible on camera
Hands supply intent, tokens supply identity: two signed device sessions over a PeerJS WebRTC data channel; the system never claims to recognise WHO the hands belong to

Snap-back stopping rule: if either hand leaves frame or tracking confidence drops for 3 consecutive frames, the action aborts, logs ABORTED_LOST_HAND, and the printer halts mid-line — the abort is the most filmable safety control in payments

Thermal-printer audit trail: every executed action prints an ESC/POS strip with amount, reason, permitting rule, blocking rule, both approver ids and a hash of the previous line — an audit log you can hold and a physical consequence for an invisible event

Open-palm kill switch: an open palm held toward the camera for 1 s freezes ALL agent activity instantly (open palm is the most robust gesture in the MediaPipe set), mirroring the RBI's proposed one-stroke kill switch
Two-hand session ceiling: stretching both hands apart sets the maximum total recovery spend for the session, enforced server-side in paise, not in the browser

Bounded retry policy: max 2 retries per record, minimum 24 h spacing, hard stop at 3 failures, and never a retry after a dispute is opened — stopping rules stated in the rule table and printed on the receipt

Compliant escalation: outreach copy is LLM-drafted but passes a deterministic validator (no amount claims, no new promises, PII allowlist, rate limit per customer per 24 h) before any send, and a rejected draft is logged with the failing rule

Scrubbable batch timeline: drag backwards and the batch un-recovers itself, because state is re-derived from the append-only event log — the audit trail the track demands IS the time machine, so no session-replay library is needed
Held-out gate evaluation including adversarial negatives: one person using both their own hands, a printed photo of a second hand, a gloved hand, and partial occlusion

Camera-optional money path: if hand tracking is unavailable (Firefox, poor light, no GPU), the gate degrades to a two-device tap confirmation — the recovery workflow never depends on the camera being able to see
Per-class recovery reporting with an honest exception list: what was recovered, what was left alone, and specifically what the policy engine refused to touch and why
ai_judgment: AI does two jobs and is fenced out of a third. It is used for hand landmarks (MediaPipe) and for RANKING which of the 200 records are most recoverable (a gradient-boosted scorer over deterministic features). It is explicitly NOT used to decide what action to take: that is a YAML rule table evaluated over integer paise, because a ranked list that is 10% wrong costs you some recovered revenue while an action decision that is 1% wrong refunds a stranger, and only one of those is survivable. The LLM is confined to drafting customer-facing dunning and representment copy, and even there it is downstream of a deterministic validator that strips or rejects anything containing an amount, a promise, or PII outside an allowlist — the LLM writes sentences, the rule engine decides money. The most important non-AI call: I do not use vision to identify WHO is approving. MediaPipe gives 21 landmarks and a Left/Right label and nothing that constitutes identity; a printed photo of a hand will pass it. So identity comes from two signed device tokens on an ultrasonically-paired WebRTC channel — cryptography for the thing cryptography is good at, vision for the thing vision is good at. This is the same call Google made in June 2026 when it shipped Fake Call Detection as a device-to-device digital handshake rather than as a deepfake classifier, and I will cite that on camera.
razorpay_fit: Track 03's bar is measured money recovered across a batch, compliant escalation, stopping rules and an audit trail — every one of which is a design constraint here rather than a checkbox. Recovery executes through the official razorpay-mcp-server (refunds, payment links, QR codes, settlements) against test keys. Compliant escalation is a validator with rate limits, not a prompt. Stopping rules are a printed rule table with max-retries, minimum spacing, and a hard stop on disputes. The audit trail exists twice — as a hash-chained event log and as a hash-chained paper strip. And the design is deliberately shaped by what the RBI's April 2026 discussion paper proposes for exactly this window: a hold before execution, a reconfirmation that states the nature of the suspicion, an override for whitelisted counterparties, and a one-stroke kill switch — implemented here as, respectively, the seal, the printed blocking rule, the tier-0 auto path, and the open palm.
measurable: On a 200-record held-out synthetic batch with ground-truth outcomes: (1) RUPEES RECOVERED, broken out per at-risk class (failed mandates, expired links, COD-to-prepaid conversions, disputes near deadline) with the counterfactual stated honestly — recovery is scored against a labelled synthetic outcome, not claimed as real-world causal lift, and the labelling procedure is in the repo. (2) RECOVERY RATE and median time-to-resolution per class. (3) ZERO unauthorized executions: no action above its tier threshold executed without the required gate across the batch, verified by replaying the event log. (4) GATE FAR/FRR on a held-out set of ~400 recorded clips including the adversarial negatives above — I expect a single person using both their own hands to defeat the VISION gate and I will report that number, which is precisely why the two-device token exists and why the honest claim is 'the hands prove intent and simultaneity, the tokens prove two parties'. (5) ABORT BEHAVIOUR: across 50 deliberate mid-turn aborts, % that halted with zero money moved and a matching ABORTED_LOST_HAND log line. (6) The exception list: every record the policy engine refused, with the rule that refused it.
feasibility: Four honest risks. (1) The geometry: two people's hands must be in ONE camera's frame for the shot to work, which means both approvers are at the same desk — that is the realistic merchant back-office case, but a remote second approver gets the device-tap fallback and no seal, and I will say so rather than imply remote dual-control works by camera. numHands:4 also roughly doubles landmark cost, so I will measure the actual frame rate on the demo laptop rather than quote the Pixel 6 figure. (2) The printer: ESC/POS over WebSerial is Chrome-only, so the reliable path is a ~50-line local Node bridge; thermal printers jam, run out of paper, and buffer, and a stalled print is the most likely on-camera embarrassment — the mitigation is that the printer is a CONSEQUENCE, not the audit trail itself (the hash-chained log is), so a jam degrades the shot but not the claim. (3) ggwave in a noisy hackathon venue at 8-16 bytes/sec is genuinely uncertain; the README will carry my own measured decode rate at 1 m and 3 m in a quiet room and a loud one, and there is a QR pairing fallback that costs the demo two seconds. (4) Hand-tracking dropout under bad light with two people leaning over a desk casting shadows on each other — which is exactly the failure the snap-back is designed for, so the plan is to trigger it deliberately on camera once. The thing most likely to break live is the simultaneity window: 400 ms is tight for two people who have not rehearsed, and if user testing shows too many false rejects I will widen it to 600 ms and publish both FRR numbers rather than quietly tune it until the demo works.

name: NAZAR — the phone taped to the wall that watches your QR sticker
one_liner: An old phone gaffer-taped above the counter watches your UPI QR standee all day, and the second someone pastes a fake sticker over it, the QR's own pixels light up red showing exactly which bits were changed.
the_gif: Locked-off shot of a real shop counter. A paper UPI QR standee is propped on it. Taped to the wall just above — visibly, cheaply, with grey gaffer tape — is an old Android phone showing a live camera view of the standee with a calm green bracket snapped onto the QR in perspective. A stranger's hand enters frame from the right holding a fresh printed QR sticker and SLAPS it down over the standee. Within one frame the wall phone's whole screen flashes red, the bracket snaps red, and inside the bracket the individual black-and-white squares of the QR ignite one by one into a scattered constellation of glowing red cells — you are literally watching which pixels of the QR code are the lie. The hand freezes mid-air. No text, no UI chrome, no cut. The counter, the sticker, the tape and the hand are all in the same continuous frame.
why_it_looks_impossible: Nobody has ever seen a QR code shown as a diff. A QR is a black-and-white lump to a human — utterly opaque. Watching individual modules ignite red across it, in perspective, glued to a piece of paper on a counter, while a hand is still touching that paper, reads as x-ray vision. And the reaction is instantaneous with no loading state, because the verdict is a 2 ms string comparison, not a model call. The second layer of impossibility is that the whole thing runs in a browser tab on a five-year-old phone that costs nothing.
problem: India has 56.86 crore physical UPI QR stickers across ~6.5 crore merchants, and a Kashmir field study of 102 merchants found 60.8% of them are loose paper stickers and 41.2% are displayed outside the counter in blind spots; 57.8% of those merchants had already lost money to fraudulent digital transactions. Delhi Police arrested a 19-year-old on 22 Dec 2025 who used AI image editing to swap bank details inside genuine merchant QRs while keeping the appearance unchanged — Rs 1.40 lakh diverted from one Chandni Chowk boutique in a single sale, with 100+ edited QRs seized off his phone. In Khajuraho in Jan 2025 fraudsters pasted stickers over genuine codes at ~6 establishments including petrol pumps overnight; it was caught only because one customer happened to read the payee name 'Chhotu Tiwari' on his own screen. Detection latency today is hours to days, and there is essentially zero open-source defence: a GitHub search for 'QR code tamper detection' returns only student projects, the largest at 4 stars.
how_it_works: Pure browser tab over HTTPS, no install, opened by scanning a QR printed on the pitch video itself. FAST LOOP (30 fps, Web Worker): Sec-ant/barcode-detector (ZXing-C++ compiled to WASM, ~1.04 MiB reader-only build, MIT) returns rawValue AND cornerPoints — the four real corners of the code in the frame, which is exactly the primitive that makes the bracket snap on in perspective and track as the paper moves. Native BarcodeDetector is used on Chrome Android when getSupportedFormats() confirms it; the ponyfill runs everywhere else because Safari's Shape Detection API sits behind a preference flag. PARSE: the UPI payload is a plain deep link (upi://pay?pa=...&pn=...&am=...) — split it with a regex, no model. VERDICT (deterministic, ~2 ms): compare decoded `pa` against the merchant's registered VPA, fetched at enrolment from the Razorpay QR Codes API (GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id) via razorpay-mcp-server in test mode. String equality decides whether money is at risk. EXPLANATION LAYER (the constellation): OpenCV.js — whose default build I confirmed whitelists findHomography, warpPerspective and solvePnP in platforms/js/opencv_js.config.py — rectifies the photographed QR from its three finder patterns plus the four cornerPoints into a canonical N×N module grid; the TRUE QR is regenerated client-side from the registered payload; the two module matrices are XORed; differing cells are rendered as glowing red modules with selective UnrealBloom (three.js webgl_postprocessing_unreal_bloom_selective) while matching cells stay ghost-white. SUSPICION SIGNALS (advisory only, can add doubt but can never clear a code): a YOLO26n fine-tuned on one class 'sticker_over_sticker' — measured by me at 17.6 ms median / 57 fps on CPUExecutionProvider on an M3 Pro at 640×640 fp32, so it is nowhere near the bottleneck — plus a Canny parallel-edge pass hunting the double border and laminate seam of a pasted second layer, plus an optional torch differential using track.applyConstraints({torch:true}) (a real W3C MediaStream Image Capture constrainable property) to capture a flash/no-flash pair and diff the specular response of one paper layer versus two. SENTINEL MODE: same page in kiosk mode with Screen Wake Lock on a wall-mounted old phone, re-verifying every 3 s; on mismatch it flashes, vibrates, and POSTs to a server that calls POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close on the compromised QR and mints a replacement.
features: Perspective-locked bracket that snaps onto any UPI QR the instant it enters frame and tracks it as the paper moves, driven by ZXing cornerPoints at 25 scans/sec
Per-module QR diff rendered as a red constellation with selective bloom — the first visualisation anywhere of which bits of a QR were altered
Decoded payee name floated above the sticker in 48pt — automating the single human-readable signal that has ever actually caught this fraud (the Khajuraho customer reading 'Chhotu Tiwari')
Sentinel mode: a repurposed old Android phone in kiosk mode with Wake Lock, gaffer-taped above the counter, re-verifying every 3 seconds for the whole trading day

Multi-QR census: point at a counter with several stickers and every one gets boxed and labelled with whose account it pays into — the Hoskote biryani outlet had 30 QR codes and Rs 1.47 crore of transactions

Torch differential layer test — fires the phone flashlight for one frame via applyConstraints({torch:true}) and diffs specular response to spot a second paper layer (Chrome Android only, feature-detected)
Sticker-peel animation: on a confirmed swap the fake overlay curls and peels off in AR to reveal the genuine registered QR underneath
Auto-containment via Razorpay: closes the compromised QR code, mints a replacement, and logs both API call ids — bounded, reversible, fully audited

Printable 'QR Birth Certificate' A5 artifact: payee name in huge type, last four of the VPA, a three-Hindi-word checksum derived from the payload hash so a customer can eyeball it, and a verification QR that opens the checker
Overnight diff mode: the sentinel stores the 9 pm frame and auto-compares it to the 7 am frame — the exact Khajuraho CCTV story as a one-tap shutter-up check
Append-only audit log — every scan writes {timestamp, payload hash, verdict, which signals fired, frame thumbnail hash}, and the log is replayable to any point in time
Graceful degradation on glare/motion: dashed amber ring, 'HOLDING' state, last good pose frozen, and explicitly no verdict issued rather than a wrong one
Judge-tries-it: a QR on screen in the pitch video opens the live checker on the judge's own phone, where they can point it at any real shop QR they walk past
Bring-your-own-attack: the repo ships a printable PDF of a tampered sticker so anyone can try to fool their own instance
ai_judgment: AI is used in exactly two places, both non-load-bearing: a single-class YOLO26n that flags a possible pasted second layer (advisory, can only add suspicion), and an LLM that drafts the Hindi/English sentence shown to the merchant AFTER the verdict is already fixed. The verdict itself is deliberately not AI: it is a string comparison of the decoded VPA against the merchant's registered VPA from the Razorpay API. I will say on camera why. I benchmarked the obvious AI approach — image forgery localisation — and it does not work: per AIForge-Doc (arXiv 2602.20569, Feb 2026, 4,061 AI-forged receipts across 9 languages), TruFor collapses from AUC 0.96 on NIST16 to 0.751, DocTamper from 0.98 to 0.563 with pixel IoU of 0.020, and a zero-shot GPT-4o judge scores 0.509 — literally chance. TruFor's licence also restricts it to nonprofit use, so it could not ship anyway. Depth is the second deliberate rejection: a paper sticker is 0.1-0.3 mm thick and monocular depth is relative and scale-free, so Depth-Anything cannot resolve a pasted layer — and I measured it at 324 ms per frame at 518×518 on this M3 Pro (3.1 fps) anyway, which is not live-camera speed. The homography, the module grid and the XOR are exact geometry, and the constellation is not a detector — it is an explanation of a fact already established deterministically.
razorpay_fit: Razorpay's own QR Codes API is both halves of the loop: the registry (GET /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id tells you what this merchant's code should decode to) and the containment action (POST /v1/payments/qr_codes/:id/close kills a compromised code, then create mints a replacement). razorpay-mcp-server is official (230 stars) and hosted remotely at https://mcp.razorpay.com/mcp, so every camera verdict is backed by a citable API call rather than a vibe. Webhooks qr_code.created / credited / closed give the real-time trail. It runs entirely on test keys with synthetic merchants, so no real money and no PII.
measurable: Held-out set of 240 phone captures I build and never train on: 120 genuine standees (my own enrolled Razorpay test QRs, printed and mounted on cardboard) and 120 tampered (a second sticker pasted over, printed at a different DPI, some laminated, some partly peeled), shot across 6 lighting conditions × 4 angles × glare/no-glare on two different phones. Report precision and recall of the end-to-end verdict, and — separately and honestly — precision/recall of the physical-layer suspicion detector alone, since that is the only component that can be wrong when there is no registry entry to compare against. Also report decode→verdict latency p50/p95 on a mid-range Android, and a confusion breakdown of which signal fired on which failure.
feasibility: What is solid: cornerPoints is a documented return field, the decode is deterministic, the Razorpay QR API is public and test-mode ready, and my own measurement puts YOLO26n at 57 fps on plain CPU so detection will never be the bottleneck on camera. What is genuinely hard: (1) the module-level rectification — getting a clean N×N grid from a glossy, curled, glare-hit sticker photographed at an angle is the real engineering, and if the rectification is off by half a module the constellation lights up nonsense; mitigation is to only render the constellation when the finder-pattern reprojection error is under a threshold, and to show the amber HOLDING state otherwise, which is itself a good on-camera beat. (2) The sticker-over-sticker detector will be trained largely on synthetic composites and may learn the compositing artefact rather than the physical tell — which is why I have scoped it as advisory-only and will report its standalone PR curve rather than hiding it inside an ensemble. (3) Torch control is Chrome-Android-only and iOS Safari support is unverified, so that layer must feature-detect and disappear silently on iPhone. (4) The known Razorpay edge case that qr_code.closed does NOT fire on auto-expiry means the containment loop must poll rather than trust the webhook — I will demonstrate that on camera as the handled failure. What could break live: shop lighting glare washing out the finder patterns, and a judge opening it in Firefox (WebGPU disabled by default on all versions), so the WASM fallback path has to be tested, not assumed.

name: MUDRA — money decisions you push around with your hands, and a printer that spits the audit trail
one_liner: An AI buying agent proposes real payments, but nothing moves until you physically slide a blank paper card into a green zone on your desk — and a thermal printer immediately prints the receipt with the rule that allowed it.
the_gif: Overhead shot, warm wooden desk. A plain blank white index card sits on the left. A hand slides it right. The instant its edge crosses onto a printed paper mat, the BLANK CARD FILLS ITSELF — a rupee amount, a merchant name and a one-line reason appear on the paper in correct perspective, tilting and sliding exactly with the card as the hand moves it, as if the ink were printed there all along. The hand pushes the card into a green outlined zone; the zone pulses once. At the top edge of frame a small thermal printer WHIRS and a curl of paper feeds out. The hand leaves the card, reaches up, and tears the receipt off. Continuous take, no cut, two physical objects, one hand.
why_it_looks_impossible: Blank paper becoming printed paper under a moving hand is the Word Lens trick — the highest-trust shot in the entire viral-demo canon — and nobody has ever pointed it at money. Then the causal chain crosses a physical gap: a piece of paper moves on a desk and a completely separate physical machine responds by printing. A single screen recording cannot fabricate that. And the interaction model is one nobody has built: 'gesture payment authorization' returns literally zero GitHub repos, and 'AR overlay invoice camera' returns zero.
problem: Track 01's bar is that every money action an AI buyer takes must be explainable, bounded, gated and audited. Today that gate is a checkbox in a dashboard, which is exactly the control that gets clicked through at 2am — and Indian regulators are actively legislating against frictionless auto-execution: the RBI's April 2026 discussion paper proposes a one-hour hold on P2P transfers above Rs 10,000, mandatory reconfirmation for atypical transactions with the reason for suspicion disclosed, a 'trusted person' second authoriser for senior citizens above Rs 50,000, and a one-stroke kill switch reversible only by physical branch visit. Meanwhile the failure mode is real money: Delhi Police arrested a gang in June 2026 that cloned a Mumbai MD's voice and moved over Rs 10 crore through 63 accounts, caught only because a human bank manager in Sarita Vihar got suspicious about a cheque. The lesson is that the last gate has to be a human doing something deliberate, and recovery afterwards is near-zero — Madhya Pradesh recovered Rs 1.94 crore of Rs 1,054 crore lost, 0.18%.
how_it_works: PHYSICAL SETUP, total cost under Rs 400: one A3 sheet printed with four ArUco markers at its corners and four labelled zones (APPROVE / HOLD / REJECT / ESCALATE), plus a stack of blank A6 cards each carrying one small ArUco marker. A phone or laptop webcam looks down at the desk. GEOMETRY LOOP (30 fps, no ML): OpenCV.js — I confirmed against platforms/js/opencv_js.config.py and modules/js/src/core_bindings.cpp that the default browser build exports aruco_ArucoDetector.detectMarkers, aruco_CharucoDetector, solvePnP, solvePnPRansac, projectPoints, Rodrigues and warpPerspective — detects markers on a downscaled frame and solves full 6-DoF pose for the mat and every card. Rendering projects text through that pose so the overlay is welded to the paper rather than floating over it. This is why it survives on a phone with no WebXR: MDN's browser-compat-data has XRSystem safari:false and safari_ios mirroring it, so markerless WebXR would silently fail on every judge's iPhone — ArUco does not care. AGENT LOOP: an LLM buying agent shops a synthetic merchant catalog and emits structured payment proposals; each proposal is assigned to the next blank card by marker id. MONEY LOOP: Razorpay test mode through razorpay-mcp-server (official, 230 stars, remote endpoint, no install) — Orders, Payment Links, QR Codes create/fetch/close, Refunds. THE GATE: the payment executes only when the card's projected centroid is inside the APPROVE polygon AND has been still for 800 ms (hysteresis band so a card resting on the boundary cannot flicker-fire). For anything above Rs 10,000 the two-hand rule engages: MediaPipe Hand Landmarker (21 3D landmarks, 12.27 ms GPU / 17.12 ms CPU on a Pixel 6, hand_landmarker.task is 7.82 MB served uncompressed) must see two hands with both index fingertips held inside two separate corner pads for 2 continuous seconds — a gate whose physical difficulty IS the safety control, so it cannot be performed by accident. Gesture gates measure hand shape as RATIOS not absolute pixel size, so they hold at any camera distance. PHYSICAL CONSEQUENCE: a Rs 200 58 mm ESC/POS thermal printer driven over the Web Serial API straight from the same browser tab. Every execution, every refusal, every stopping-rule trip prints amount, payee, the rule that permitted it, the rule that would have stopped it, the Razorpay payment id, and a small QR linking to the audit record.
features: Blank paper cards that fill themselves with a live payment proposal in correct 6-DoF perspective and stay welded to the paper as your hand slides and rotates it
Physical zone-based approval: push the card into APPROVE, HOLD, REJECT or ESCALATE — money decisions as objects you move, not checkboxes you click
Two-hand escalation gate above Rs 10,000, both index fingertips held on separate corner pads for 2 seconds via MediaPipe Hand Landmarker — a control whose difficulty is the point
Ratio-based gesture gating so the thresholds hold at any camera distance rather than only at the distance I tuned them
Thermal printer audit trail over Web Serial from the browser tab — the compliance requirement becomes a strip of paper accumulating on the floor that you can physically hold
Every printed line carries both the rule that permitted the action and the rule that would have stopped it, so 'explainable' is legible without a dashboard
Deterministic policy engine: amount cap, per-day cap, per-payee cap, payee allowlist, merchant category, time-of-day window — a plain table, version-controlled, with a rule id on every decision
Stopping rules that visibly bite on camera: daily budget exhausted freezes every remaining card grey and prints 'BUDGET EXHAUSTED — STOPPED'
Bounded retry with idempotency keys on Razorpay API failure — prints RETRY 1/3, RETRY 2/3, then STOPPED — ESCALATED, and never double-charges
Pose-loss handling as a visible state: cover a marker and the overlay desaturates, freezes at the last good pose, a confidence ring closes over 1.5 s, and a line prints 'POSE LOST — HELD, NO ACTION'
Session spool artifact: the whole receipt tape stitched into one long shareable PNG, each line with its own scannable QR to the audit record
Agent explains itself on the card, not in a log — the reason string is rendered onto the physical object being approved
Full replay: the append-only event log re-derives the exact state of every card at any timestamp, so the audit trail and the demo are the same artifact

Optional ggwave chirp confirmation (8-16 bytes/sec, MIT, ultrasonic mode at F0=15 kHz) as a soundbox-style acknowledgment, always mirrored visually as an on-screen ripple so the clip still works muted
ai_judgment: An LLM proposes; a table decides; a hand consents. The AI agent generates payment proposals and writes the human-readable reason line — that is all it touches. The policy engine that determines whether a proposal is permissible is deliberately NOT a model: it is a versioned rules table in plain code, because a judge, an auditor and a merchant all need to be able to read the exact reason a payment was allowed, and an LLM's assent is neither reproducible nor auditable. The gate is not a model either — it is a point-in-polygon test with hysteresis plus a landmark distance ratio. Two further deliberate rejections, both with reasons I can defend on camera: (1) I rejected markerless WebXR AR, which is the obvious 'impressive' choice, because MDN browser-compat-data shows XRSystem, XRHitTestSource, XRAnchor and XRLightProbe are all false on Safari and iOS Safari — the demo would silently show nothing to any judge on an iPhone. Printed ArUco markers give exact pose, degrade gracefully under bad tube lighting, and cost nothing. (2) I rejected MediaPipe's canned Gesture Recognizer (8.37 MB, 8 fixed gestures) in favour of two hand-rolled landmark tests — 8.4 MB lighter, and I control the thresholds, which matters when the threshold is a money control.
razorpay_fit: This is Track 01 stated literally. A merchant is made transactable by an AI buyer through Razorpay test mode — Orders, Payment Links and QR Codes minted and closed through the official razorpay-mcp-server, with refunds as the reversal path. Every money action is explainable (the reason is printed on the card and on the receipt), bounded (a rules table with caps), gated (a physical human act), and audited (an append-only log plus a physical paper tape).
